class Actor(abc.ABC): 
 149class Actor(ABC):
 150    """Base Actor class. All agents inherit from this.
 151    Actors are fully async and communicate only through messages.
 152    """
 153
 154    def __init__(
 155        self,
 156        actor_id: str | None = None,
 157        name: str | None = None,
 158        persistence_dir: str | None = None,
 159        mailbox_size: int = 1000,
 160    ):
 161        if actor_id:
 162            self.actor_id = actor_id
 163        elif name:
 164            # Deterministic UUID from name — same name always gets same ID across restarts
 165            self.actor_id = str(uuid.uuid5(uuid.NAMESPACE_DNS, f"wactorz.actor.{name}"))
 166        else:
 167            self.actor_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
 168        self.name = name or f"actor-{self.actor_id[:8]}"
 169        self.state = ActorState.IDLE
 170        self.metrics = ActorMetrics()
 171
 172        # Async mailbox (inbox)
 173        self._mailbox: asyncio.Queue = asyncio.Queue(maxsize=mailbox_size)
 174        self._outbox: dict[str, asyncio.Queue] = {}  # actor_id -> queue ref
 175
 176        # Registry reference (set by ActorSystem)
 177        self._registry: ActorRegistry | None = None
 178        self._mqtt_client: Any | None = None
 179        self._mqtt_broker: str = "localhost"
 180        self._mqtt_port: int = 1883
 181
 182        # Persistence
 183        # Use name as persistence folder so it survives restarts with same name
 184        # Falls back to actor_id for anonymous actors
 185
 186        # `resolve_state_dir` rather than a literal: where durable state lives is
 187        # one question with one answer (explicit argument, else
 188        # `WACTORZ_STATE_DIR`, else `./state`). The old `./actor_state` default
 189        # was a second opinion that disagreed with the resolver, so a caller who
 190        # omitted the argument wrote somewhere nothing else would look.
 191        # Through `agent_state_dir`, so a name like `..` is refused rather than
 192        # walking out of the state directory it was given.
 193        self._persistence_dir = agent_state_dir(persistence_dir or resolve_state_dir(), self.name)
 194        self._persistence_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
 195        self._persistent_state: dict = {}
 196
 197        # Unified persistence API — set by ActorSystem if available,
 198        # otherwise falls back to legacy pickle behavior
 199        self._persistence_api: PersistenceAPI | None = None
 200
 201        # Protection — if True, delete is refused. These are agents defined in
 202        # code rather than spawned, so deleting one drops a spawn-registry entry
 203        # that nothing can recreate from the interface.
 204        self.protected: bool = False
 205
 206        # Essential — if True, stop is refused as well. Reserved for an agent the
 207        # user would be stopping their own way of undoing it: everything else can
 208        # be stopped and started again from its card.
 209        self.essential: bool = False
 210
 211        # Supervisor reference — set by Supervisor when this actor is registered under it
 212        self.supervisor_id: str | None = None
 213
 214        # Handlers
 215        self._handlers: dict[MessageType, Callable] = {}
 216        #: Correlation id → the future waiting on that request's RESULT.
 217        #: Populated by whoever sends a TASK carrying `_task_id`; drained by
 218        #: `_resolve_pending_result` before the message reaches a handler.
 219        self._result_futures: dict[str, asyncio.Future] = {}
 220        self._setup_default_handlers()
 221
 222        # Background tasks
 223        self._tasks: list[asyncio.Task] = []
 224
 225        # Cached process handle for heartbeat metrics — one per actor so each
 226        # has an independent cpu_percent baseline (interval=None, non-blocking).
 227        self._proc: Any | None = None
 228        try:
 229            self._proc = psutil.Process()
 230            self._proc.cpu_percent(interval=None)  # prime the baseline
 231        except Exception:
 232            pass
 233
 234        logger.info("[%s] Actor created with id=%s", self.name, self.actor_id)
 235
 236    # ─── Lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 237
 238    async def start(self):
 239        """Start the actor's event loop."""
 240        self.state = ActorState.RUNNING
 241        self.metrics.start_time = time.time()
 242        await self._load_persistent_state()
 243        # Restore the message count from a previous run — but only into a fresh
 244        # instance. The supervisor restarts by building a new actor, whose count
 245        # is zero; the start command restarts *this* object, whose count is
 246        # already the live total. Adding the persisted value there counts every
 247        # message twice, and again on each subsequent stop/start.
 248        if self.metrics.messages_processed == 0:
 249            saved_msgs = self.recall("_messages_processed", {})
 250            if isinstance(saved_msgs, dict) and saved_msgs.get("count"):
 251                self.metrics.messages_processed = int(saved_msgs["count"])
 252        await self.on_start()
 253        self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._message_loop()))
 254        self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._heartbeat_loop()))
 255        self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._command_listener()))
 256        await self._publish_status()
 257        logger.info("[%s] Actor started.", self.name)
 258
 259    async def stop(self):
 260        """Gracefully stop the actor."""
 261        self.state = ActorState.STOPPED
 262        await self._wind_down_tasks()
 263        # Shield cleanup from CancelledError — chat tasks run as fire-and-forget
 264        # asyncio tasks outside actor._tasks and get cancelled by asyncio.run()
 265        # cleanup BEFORE these awaits if we don't shield them.
 266        #
 267        # A cancellation arriving here belongs to whoever is *calling* stop(),
 268        # not to this cleanup: `shield` keeps the inner coroutine running and
 269        # raises in the awaiting task. Discarding it told that caller its
 270        # cancellation had been honoured when it had not — the supervisor's watch
 271        # loop resumed polling, and `Supervisor.stop()` waited forever on a task
 272        # already marked cancelling. So it is remembered, both steps still run,
 273        # and it is re-raised once cleanup is done.
 274        cancelled = False
 275        try:
 276            await asyncio.shield(self.on_stop())
 277        except asyncio.CancelledError:
 278            cancelled = True
 279        except Exception:
 280            pass
 281        try:
 282            await asyncio.shield(self._save_persistent_state())
 283        except asyncio.CancelledError:
 284            cancelled = True
 285        except Exception:
 286            pass
 287
 288        # ── Persist message count so overview survives restarts ──────────
 289        if self.metrics.messages_processed > 0:
 290            self.persist("_messages_processed", {"count": self.metrics.messages_processed})
 291
 292        # ── Persist final cost metrics (for LLM-backed agents) ─────────
 293        # Cost data lives in-memory and dies with the agent object.
 294        # Persist it so the UI can show lifetime costs for deleted agents.
 295        if hasattr(self, "total_cost_usd") and getattr(self, "total_cost_usd", 0) > 0:
 296            self.persist(
 297                "_final_cost",
 298                {
 299                    "input_tokens": getattr(self, "total_input_tokens", 0),
 300                    "output_tokens": getattr(self, "total_output_tokens", 0),
 301                    "cost_usd": round(getattr(self, "total_cost_usd", 0), 6),
 302                    "name": self.name,
 303                    "stopped_at": time.time(),
 304                },
 305            )
 306
 307        # ── Publish final metrics before the agent disappears ──────────
 308        # The heartbeat loop is already cancelled at this point, so this
 309        # is the UI's last chance to capture cost/usage data.
 310        try:
 311            final_metrics = self._build_metrics()
 312            final_metrics["final"] = True  # signals UI this is the last message
 313            await self._mqtt_publish(
 314                f"agents/{self.actor_id}/metrics",
 315                final_metrics,
 316            )
 317        except Exception:
 318            pass
 319
 320        await self._publish_status()
 321        # ── Unregister from TopicBus ───────────────────────────────────
 322        # Remove this agent's TopicContract so the planner doesn't wire
 323        # against topics from stopped/deleted/replaced agents.
 324        try:
 325            from .topic_bus import get_topic_bus
 326
 327            bus = get_topic_bus()
 328            if bus:
 329                bus.unregister(self.name)
 330        except Exception:
 331            pass  # TopicBus not initialised or unavailable — not fatal
 332        logger.info("[%s] Actor stopped.", self.name)
 333        # Deferred to here rather than raised where it arrived: the shield exists
 334        # so cleanup completes, and stopping half way through would defeat it.
 335        # The caller still learns its cancellation was real.
 336        if cancelled:
 337            raise asyncio.CancelledError
 338
 339    #: How long stop() waits for a cancelled task before giving up on it.
 340    TASK_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT = 5.0
 341
 342    async def _wind_down_tasks(self) -> None:
 343        """Cancel the actor's own tasks and wait for them to actually finish.
 344
 345        ``cancel()`` only requests cancellation. Returning without awaiting left
 346        a task that was part-way through a message to unwind after ``stop()``
 347        had already reported the actor stopped — and since the task list was
 348        never cleared, starting the actor again ran a second message loop, a
 349        second heartbeat and a second command listener alongside the ones still
 350        winding down, so every command was handled twice.
 351
 352        The task this runs in is left alone: a stop command arrives on the
 353        command listener, and a task cannot wait for itself. Each loop is
 354        written to exit once the state is STOPPED, which is already set.
 355        """
 356        current = asyncio.current_task()
 357        others = [task for task in self._tasks if task is not current]
 358        for task in others:
 359            task.cancel()
 360        try:
 361            if others:
 362                # Bounded: a task that will not unwind must not hold up shutdown.
 363                await asyncio.wait_for(
 364                    asyncio.shield(asyncio.gather(*others, return_exceptions=True)),
 365                    timeout=self.TASK_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT,
 366                )
 367        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
 368            logger.warning(
 369                "[%s] %d task(s) did not stop within %gs.",
 370                self.name,
 371                sum(1 for task in others if not task.done()),
 372                self.TASK_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT,
 373            )
 374        # CancelledError is deliberately not caught. Swallowing it consumes the
 375        # caller's own cancellation: the supervisor's watch loop was cancelled
 376        # here while stopping an actor, never saw the error, resumed its poll
 377        # loop, and left Supervisor.stop() awaiting a task that could no longer
 378        # finish. Clearing the task list still happens either way.
 379        finally:
 380            self._tasks.clear()
 381
 382    # ─── Message Loop ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 383
 384    async def _message_loop(self):
 385        """Main message processing loop."""
 386        while self.state not in (ActorState.STOPPED, ActorState.FAILED):
 387            try:
 388                msg = await asyncio.wait_for(self._mailbox.get(), timeout=1.0)
 389                self.metrics.messages_received += 1
 390                # Only count meaningful messages — not heartbeats, status pings, lifecycle
 391                _noise = {
 392                    MessageType.HEARTBEAT,
 393                    MessageType.STATUS_REQUEST,
 394                    MessageType.STATUS_RESPONSE,
 395                    MessageType.STOP,
 396                }
 397                if msg.type not in _noise:
 398                    self.metrics.messages_processed += 1
 399                await self._dispatch(msg)
 400                self._mailbox.task_done()
 401
 402            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
 403                continue
 404            except asyncio.CancelledError:
 405                break
 406            except Exception as e:
 407                self.metrics.errors += 1
 408                logger.error("[%s] Error in message loop: %s", self.name, e, exc_info=True)
 409
 410    def _resolve_pending_result(self, msg: Message) -> bool:
 411        """Settle a waiting future from a RESULT's correlation id.
 412
 413        Request/reply is a convention rather than a framework feature: the
 414        sender tags a TASK with `_task_id` and blocks on a future keyed by it,
 415        and the recipient echoes that id back.
 416
 417        It belongs here, ahead of every handler, so that any actor can receive a
 418        reply without opting in — a per-agent implementation makes the ability
 419        depend on which agent is receiving. Returns True when the message was a
 420        reply someone was waiting for, in which case there is nothing left to
 421        dispatch: the caller already has it.
 422        """
 423        if msg.type != MessageType.RESULT or not isinstance(msg.payload, dict):
 424            return False
 425        # "task" is the older spelling and still on the wire from some agents.
 426        fid = msg.payload.get("_task_id") or msg.payload.get("task")
 427        future = self._result_futures.get(fid) if fid else None
 428        if future is None:
 429            return False
 430        if not future.done():
 431            future.set_result(msg.payload)
 432        return True
 433
 434    async def _dispatch(self, msg: Message):
 435        """Dispatch message to the appropriate handler."""
 436        if self._resolve_pending_result(msg):
 437            return
 438        handler = self._handlers.get(msg.type)
 439        if handler:
 440            await handler(msg)
 441        else:
 442            await self.handle_message(msg)
 443
 444    def _setup_default_handlers(self):
 445        self._handlers = {
 446            MessageType.START: self._handle_lifecycle,
 447            MessageType.STOP: self._handle_lifecycle,
 448            MessageType.STATUS_REQUEST: self._handle_status_request,
 449            MessageType.HEARTBEAT: self._handle_heartbeat_msg,
 450        }
 451
 452    async def _handle_lifecycle(self, msg: Message):
 453        """Apply a lifecycle message through the one implementation of it.
 454
 455        Message-passing is another way to ask for the same thing, not another
 456        set of rules: START/STOP all route through `apply_command`,
 457        so an essential actor refuses a STOP message exactly as it refuses the
 458        REST and dashboard routes, and the supervision release happens once
 459        rather than per entry point.
 460        """
 461        await self.apply_command(msg.type.value)
 462
 463    async def _handle_status_request(self, msg: Message):
 464        status = self.get_status()
 465        # Reply to sender_id (always), reply_to is optional override
 466        target = msg.reply_to or msg.sender_id
 467        if target:
 468            await self.send(target, MessageType.STATUS_RESPONSE, status)
 469
 470    async def _handle_heartbeat_msg(self, msg: Message):
 471        pass  # Monitor actor handles these
 472
 473    # ─── Heartbeat ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 474
 475    async def _heartbeat_loop(self, interval: float = 10.0):
 476        """Periodically publish heartbeat via MQTT."""
 477        # Publish immediately on start so monitor sees agent right away
 478        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
 479        self.metrics.heartbeats += 1
 480        await self._mqtt_publish(f"agents/{self.actor_id}/heartbeat", self._build_heartbeat())
 481        await self._mqtt_publish(f"agents/{self.actor_id}/metrics", self._build_metrics())
 482        while self.state not in (ActorState.STOPPED, ActorState.FAILED):
 483            try:
 484                await asyncio.sleep(interval)
 485                hb = self._build_heartbeat()
 486                self.metrics.heartbeats += 1
 487                self.metrics.last_heartbeat = time.time()
 488                await self._mqtt_publish(f"agents/{self.actor_id}/heartbeat", hb)
 489                await self._mqtt_publish(f"agents/{self.actor_id}/metrics", self._build_metrics())
 490            except asyncio.CancelledError:
 491                break
 492            except Exception as e:
 493                logger.warning("[%s] Heartbeat error: %s", self.name, e)
 494
 495    def _estimate_memory_mb(self) -> float:
 496        """Bounded deep-size walk over this actor's own data structures.
 497
 498        Bounded in breadth as well as depth: the walk runs on the event loop on
 499        every heartbeat, so it stops after ``SIZE_WALK_BUDGET`` objects and its
 500        cost stays flat however far the actor's state has grown. Past that point
 501        the result is a lower bound rather than a full accounting.
 502        Uses only sys.getsizeof — no new deps, works on Windows.
 503        """
 504        seen: set[int] = set()
 505
 506        def _deep(obj: object, depth: int) -> int:
 507            if depth > 5 or len(seen) >= SIZE_WALK_BUDGET:
 508                return 0
 509            oid = id(obj)
 510            if oid in seen:
 511                return 0
 512            seen.add(oid)
 513            sz = sys.getsizeof(obj)
 514            if isinstance(obj, dict):
 515                sz += sum(_deep(k, depth + 1) + _deep(v, depth + 1) for k, v in obj.items())
 516            elif isinstance(obj, (list, tuple, set, frozenset)):
 517                sz += sum(_deep(item, depth + 1) for item in obj)
 518            return sz
 519
 520        total = 0
 521        for attr in ("_persistent_state", "_outbox", "metrics"):
 522            val = getattr(self, attr, None)
 523            if val is not None:
 524                total += _deep(val, 0)
 525        # Rough proxy for messages sitting in the mailbox (~512 B each)
 526        total += self._mailbox.qsize() * 512
 527        return total / (1024 * 1024)
 528
 529    def _build_heartbeat(self) -> dict:
 530        cpu = 0.0
 531        try:
 532            if self._proc is not None:
 533                cpu = self._proc.cpu_percent(interval=None)
 534        except Exception:
 535            pass
 536        return {
 537            "actor_id": self.actor_id,
 538            "name": self.name,
 539            "timestamp": time.time(),
 540            "state": self.state.value,
 541            "cpu": cpu,
 542            "memory_mb": self._estimate_memory_mb(),
 543            "task": self._current_task_description(),
 544            "protected": self.protected,
 545            "essential": self.essential,
 546        }
 547
 548    def _build_metrics(self) -> dict:
 549        return {
 550            "actor_id": self.actor_id,
 551            "messages_processed": self.metrics.messages_processed,
 552            "errors": self.metrics.errors,
 553            "uptime": self.metrics.uptime,
 554            "tasks_completed": self.metrics.tasks_completed,
 555            "tasks_failed": self.metrics.tasks_failed,
 556            "restart_count": self.metrics.restart_count,
 557        }
 558
 559    LIFECYCLE_COMMANDS = ("start", "stop", "delete")
 560
 561    def _release_from_supervision(self) -> None:
 562        """Tell the supervisor this actor is leaving deliberately.
 563
 564        The Erlang unlink. Stopping without it is indistinguishable from
 565        crashing, so the heartbeat-silence watchdog fires ~35s later and
 566        restarts the actor that was just deliberately stopped.
 567        """
 568        if self._registry and hasattr(self._registry, "_supervisor_ref"):
 569            sup = self._registry._supervisor_ref
 570            if sup is not None:
 571                sup.release(self.name)
 572
 573    def _resume_supervision(self) -> None:
 574        """Put this actor back under supervision after a deliberate stop.
 575
 576        The mirror of :meth:`_release_from_supervision`. Without it a restarted
 577        actor runs unwatched — it would crash and stay down, which is exactly
 578        what supervision exists to prevent.
 579        """
 580        if self._registry and hasattr(self._registry, "_supervisor_ref"):
 581            sup = self._registry._supervisor_ref
 582            if sup is not None:
 583                sup.resupervise(self.name, self)
 584
 585    async def apply_command(self, command: str) -> bool:
 586        """Run a lifecycle command on this actor. Returns whether it took effect.
 587
 588        These are not a dispatch table, which is why they live here rather than
 589        in the transport below: ``stop`` must release from supervision first, and
 590        ``delete`` also clears the spawn registry and unregisters. A caller that
 591        holds the actor and simply awaits ``stop()`` gets it restarted half a
 592        minute later by the watchdog.
 593
 594        Every entry point routes through this — the broker listener, and the web
 595        layer when the actor is local — so the two cannot drift apart.
 596
 597        Returns ``False`` when the command was refused -- ``delete`` on a
 598        protected actor, ``stop`` on an essential one -- or unknown, so a caller
 599        can report that rather than claim success.
 600        """
 601        if forbidden(command, protected=self.protected, essential=self.essential):
 602            logger.warning("[%s] Ignoring %r — refused by policy.", self.name, command)
 603            return False
 604
 605        if command == "start":
 606            if self.state != ActorState.STOPPED:
 607                logger.warning("[%s] Ignoring 'start' — actor is %s.", self.name, self.state.value)
 608                return False
 609            await self.start()
 610            self._resume_supervision()
 611        elif command == "stop":
 612            self._release_from_supervision()
 613            await self.stop()
 614        elif command == "delete":
 615            self._release_from_supervision()
 616            if self._registry:
 617                main = self._registry.find_by_name("main")
 618                if main and hasattr(main, "_remove_from_spawn_registry"):
 619                    main._remove_from_spawn_registry(self.name)  # pyright: ignore[reportAttributeAccessIssue]
 620                await self._registry.unregister(self.actor_id)
 621            await self.stop()
 622        else:
 623            logger.warning("[%s] Unknown command: %r", self.name, command)
 624            return False
 625        return True
 626
 627    async def _command_listener(self):
 628        """Carry commands from agents/{id}/commands to :meth:`apply_command`.
 629
 630        Transport only. Needed for actors a caller cannot reach in process —
 631        after the direct-dispatch change that means agents on remote nodes.
 632        """
 633        try:
 634            import aiomqtt  # noqa: F401  # pylint: disable=unused-import
 635        except ImportError:
 636            return
 637        from .mqtt import mqtt_client  # local: avoids core/__init__ import cycle
 638
 639        topic = f"agents/{self.actor_id}/commands"
 640        while self.state not in (ActorState.STOPPED, ActorState.FAILED):
 641            try:
 642                async with mqtt_client(self._mqtt_broker, self._mqtt_port) as client:
 643                    await client.subscribe(topic)
 644                    logger.debug("[%s] Subscribed to %s", self.name, topic)
 645                    async for message in client.messages:
 646                        try:
 647                            data = json.loads(message.payload.decode())
 648                            command = data.get("command", "")
 649                            logger.info("[%s] Received command: %s", self.name, command)
 650                            applied = await self.apply_command(command)
 651                            # Only stop listening if it actually took effect: a
 652                            # an actor that refuses a command by policy must keep
 653                            # receiving commands afterwards.
 654                            if applied and command in ("stop", "delete"):
 655                                return
 656                        except Exception as exc:
 657                            logger.error("[%s] Command parse error: %s", self.name, exc)
 658            except asyncio.CancelledError:
 659                break
 660            except Exception:
 661                if self.state not in (ActorState.STOPPED, ActorState.FAILED):
 662                    await asyncio.sleep(5)
 663
 664    def _current_task_description(self) -> str:
 665        return "idle"  # Override in subclasses
 666

 669    async def send(self, target_id: str, msg_type: MessageType, payload: Any = None) -> bool:
 670        """Send a message to another actor."""
 671        if self._registry is None:
 672            logger.warning("[%s] No registry attached, cannot send messages.", self.name)
 673            return False
 674        msg = Message(type=msg_type, sender_id=self.actor_id, payload=payload)
 675        return await self._registry.deliver(target_id, msg)
 676
 677    async def broadcast(self, msg_type: MessageType, payload: Any = None):
 678        """Broadcast to all registered actors."""

 680            await self._registry.broadcast(self.actor_id, msg_type, payload)
 681

 683        """External entry point - put message in mailbox."""
 684        await self._mailbox.put(msg)

 686    # ─── Actor Spawning ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 687
 688    async def spawn(self, actor_class: type[Actor], **kwargs: Any) -> Actor:
 689        """Spawn a child actor. The child inherits:
 690        - MQTT client (so it can publish heartbeats/status)
 691        - Registry (so it can send/receive messages)
 692        - Persistence dir defaults to same root
 693        - Persistence API (SQLite/memory/Pickle routing)
 694
 695        Erlang/OTP supervision: if the owning ActorSystem has a Supervisor,
 696        the child is automatically registered under it with ONE_FOR_ONE so it
 697        will be restarted if it crashes — no child is an orphan.
 698        """
 699        # Default persistence to same root as parent
 700        kwargs.setdefault("persistence_dir", str(self._persistence_dir.parent))
 701
 702        child = actor_class(**kwargs)
 703
 704        # Inherit everything from parent
 705        child._mqtt_client = self._mqtt_client  # MQTT publish connection
 706        child._mqtt_broker = self._mqtt_broker  # broker address for command listener
 707        child._mqtt_port = self._mqtt_port  # broker port
 708        child._registry = self._registry  # message routing
 709
 710        # Inherit persistence API if available
 711        if self._persistence_api is not None:
 712            try:
 713                from .persistence import PersistenceAPI, get_db, get_pickle_store
 714
 715                db = get_db()
 716                pkl = get_pickle_store()
 717                if db and pkl:
 718                    child._persistence_api = PersistenceAPI(db, pkl, child.name)
 719            except ImportError:
 720                pass
 721
 722        # Register in registry
 723        if self._registry:
 724            await self._registry.register(child)
 725
 726        # Start the child
 727        await child.start()
 728
 729        # ── Erlang/OTP: register child under Supervisor so it's never an orphan ──
 730        # We reach into the registry to find the ActorSystem's supervisor.
 731        # If no supervisor is available this is a safe no-op.
 732        try:
 733            if self._registry and hasattr(self._registry, "_supervisor_ref"):
 734                supervisor = self._registry._supervisor_ref
 735                if supervisor is not None and child.name not in supervisor._specs:
 736                    # Snapshot what the child was built from. The factory runs
 737                    # again on every restart, possibly much later, and must
 738                    # rebuild the child as it was rather than from whatever this
 739                    # actor's settings have become since.
 740                    cls = actor_class
 741                    kw = dict(kwargs)
 742                    mc = self._mqtt_client
 743                    mb = self._mqtt_broker
 744                    mp = self._mqtt_port
 745                    papi = self._persistence_api
 746
 747                    async def _child_factory() -> Actor:
 748                        c = cls(**kw)
 749                        c._mqtt_client = mc
 750                        c._mqtt_broker = mb
 751                        c._mqtt_port = mp
 752                        if papi is not None:
 753                            try:
 754                                from .persistence import (
 755                                    PersistenceAPI,
 756                                    get_db,
 757                                    get_pickle_store,
 758                                )
 759
 760                                db = get_db()
 761                                pkl = get_pickle_store()
 762                                if db and pkl:
 763                                    c._persistence_api = PersistenceAPI(db, pkl, c.name)
 764                            except ImportError:
 765                                pass
 766                        return c
 767
 768                    supervisor.supervise(
 769                        child.name,
 770                        _child_factory,
 771                        strategy=SupervisorStrategy.ONE_FOR_ONE,
 772                        max_restarts=5,
 773                        restart_window=60.0,
 774                        restart_delay=2.0,
 775                    )
 776                    # Point spec.actor at the already-running child so the watch loop
 777                    # starts monitoring immediately without a redundant restart.
 778                    supervisor._specs[child.name].actor = child
 779                    if child.name not in supervisor._order:
 780                        supervisor._order.append(child.name)
 781                    child.supervisor_id = str(id(supervisor))
 782                    logger.info(
 783                        "[%s] Child '%s' auto-registered under Supervisor.", self.name, child.name
 784                    )
 785        except Exception as _sup_err:
 786            # Never let supervision registration crash the spawn itself
 787            logger.warning(
 788                "[%s] Could not auto-supervise child '%s': %s", self.name, child.name, _sup_err
 789            )
 790
 791        # Immediately announce to monitor - don't wait for heartbeat loop
 792        await child._publish_status()
 793        await child._mqtt_publish(
 794            f"agents/{child.actor_id}/heartbeat",
 795            child._build_heartbeat(),
 796        )
 797        await child._mqtt_publish(
 798            f"agents/{child.actor_id}/metrics",
 799            child._build_metrics(),
 800        )
 801
 802        # Notify parent's topic that it spawned a child
 803        await self._mqtt_publish(
 804            f"agents/{self.actor_id}/spawned",
 805            {"child_id": child.actor_id, "child_name": child.name, "timestamp": time.time()},
 806        )
 807        logger.info("[%s] Spawned: %s (%s)", self.name, child.name, child.actor_id[:8])
 808        return child

 810    # ─── Persistence ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 811
 812    async def _save_persistent_state(self):
 813        """Save state to disk. Called on stop() after on_stop()."""
 814        if self._persistence_api is not None:
 815            # New path: state is written per-key via persist(), nothing to batch-save.
 816            # But keep pickle save for agent.state (arbitrary objects) backward compat.
 817            return
 818        # Legacy pickle path
 819        try:
 820            write_pickle(self._persistence_dir / "state.pkl", self._persistent_state)
 821        except Exception as e:
 822            logger.error("[%s] Failed to save state: %s", self.name, e)
 823
 824    async def _load_persistent_state(self):
 825        """Load state from disk. Called on start() before on_start()."""
 826        if self._persistence_api is not None:
 827            # New path: state is loaded per-key via recall(), nothing to batch-load.
 828            # But load legacy pickle for backward compat if it exists.
 829            path = self._persistence_dir / "state.pkl"
 830            if path.exists():
 831                try:
 832                    with open(path, "rb") as f:
 833                        self._persistent_state = pickle.load(f)
 834                    logger.info(
 835                        "[%s] Loaded legacy persistent state (will migrate on first persist).",
 836                        self.name,
 837                    )
 838                except Exception as e:
 839                    self._keep_unreadable_state(path, e)
 840            return
 841        # Legacy pickle path
 842        path = self._persistence_dir / "state.pkl"
 843        if path.exists():
 844            try:
 845                with open(path, "rb") as f:
 846                    self._persistent_state = pickle.load(f)
 847                logger.info("[%s] Loaded persistent state.", self.name)
 848            except Exception as e:
 849                self._keep_unreadable_state(path, e)
 850
 851    def _keep_unreadable_state(self, path: Path, exc: Exception) -> None:
 852        """Move a state file we could not read out of the next save's way.
 853
 854        Starting empty is the right call — the agent must come up — but the very
 855        next `persist` would write over the file, so the only record of what was
 856        lost has to be taken out of that path first.
 857        """
 858        kept = quarantine_unreadable(path)
 859        logger.error(
 860            "[%s] Failed to load state: %s — %s",
 861            self.name,
 862            exc,
 863            f"kept at {kept}" if kept else "the file could not be preserved",
 864        )
 865
 866    def persist(self, key: str, value: Any):
 867        """Persist a key-value pair. Routes to the correct backend:
 868          - Known structured keys → SQLite
 869          - Known ephemeral keys → process memory
 870          - Everything else → Pickle
 871
 872        If the new PersistenceAPI is not available, falls back to legacy
 873        pickle behavior (writes entire dict to disk on every call).
 874        """
 875        if self._persistence_api is not None:
 876            self._persistence_api.set(key, value)
 877            return
 878
 879        # Legacy pickle path — the whole dict goes to disk on every call, so an
 880        # interrupted write here would lose every key, not just this one.
 881        self._persistent_state[key] = value
 882        try:
 883            write_pickle(self._persistence_dir / "state.pkl", self._persistent_state)
 884        except Exception as e:
 885            logger.warning("[%s] persist write failed for %r: %s", self.name, key, e)
 886
 887    def recall(self, key: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
 888        """Recall a persisted value. Routes to the correct backend.
 889        Returns default if the key doesn't exist.
 890        """
 891        if self._persistence_api is not None:
 892            # Check new store first, then fall back to legacy in-memory dict
 893            # (handles migration period where some keys are in pickle, some in new store)
 894            result = self._persistence_api.get(key)
 895            if result is not None:
 896                return result
 897            # Fallback: check legacy in-memory state (loaded from old .pkl)
 898            return self._persistent_state.get(key, default)
 899
 900        # Legacy pickle path
 901        return self._persistent_state.get(key, default)
 902
 903    # ─── MQTT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 904
 905    async def _mqtt_publish(self, topic: str, payload: Any, retain: bool = False, qos: int = 0):
 906        if self._mqtt_client:
 907            try:
 908                # Stamp telemetry frames with the agent's own name. logs/spawned
 909                # payloads carry only the topic id, and while an agent is being
 910                # spawned or installing deps it isn't in any registry yet — but it
 911                # always knows self.name, so the feed can attribute the row.
 912                if isinstance(payload, dict) and (topic.endswith(("/logs", "/spawned"))):
 913                    payload.setdefault("name", self.name)
 914                # Empty bytes = clear a retained message (MQTT spec)
 915                # Must send raw empty bytes, not JSON-encoded
 916                if payload == b"" or (payload is None and retain):
 917                    encoded = b""
 918                elif isinstance(payload, (bytes, bytearray)):
 919                    encoded = payload
 920                else:
 921                    encoded = json.dumps(payload)
 922                await self._mqtt_client.publish(topic, encoded, retain=retain, qos=qos)
 923            except Exception as e:
 924                logger.debug("[%s] MQTT publish failed: %s", self.name, e)
 925
 926    async def _publish_status(self):
 927        await self._mqtt_publish(f"agents/{self.actor_id}/status", self.get_status())
 928
 929    async def notify_user(self, text: str, **extra):
 930        """Push a user-facing chat message to the UI from this actor, OUTSIDE the
 931        synchronous request/reply turn.
 932
 933        The monitor forwards agents/{id}/chat messages to the chat panel as live
 934        chat frames, so use this for autonomous notifications the user should see
 935        in chat without having just asked for them: a long delegated task
 936        finishing after the reply already returned, sensor alerts, scheduled
 937        output, reactive automations, etc.
 938        """
 939        payload = {
 940            "from": self.name,
 941            "to": "user",
 942            "content": str(text),
 943            "timestamp": time.time(),
 944        }
 945        if extra:
 946            payload.update(extra)
 947        await self._mqtt_publish(f"agents/{self.actor_id}/chat", payload)
 948

 951    def get_status(self) -> dict:
 952        """This actor's identity, state and counters, as the dashboard shows them."""
 953        return {
 954            "actor_id": self.actor_id,
 955            "name": self.name,
 956            "state": self.state.value,
 957            "uptime": self.metrics.uptime,
 958            "messages_processed": self.metrics.messages_processed,
 959            "restart_count": self.metrics.restart_count,
 960            "supervised": self.supervisor_id is not None,
 961        }

 967
 968    async def publish_manifest(
 969        self,
 970        description: str = "",
 971        publishes: list[str] | None = None,
 972        capabilities: list[str] | None = None,
 973        input_schema: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
 974        output_schema: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
 975    ) -> None:
 976        """Publish a capability manifest so main's topic registry can discover this actor.
 977        Call from on_start() in any actor that wants to be discoverable.
 978        Manifests are retained — main sees them immediately even after restart.
 979
 980        input_schema / output_schema — dicts describing expected payload fields, e.g.:
 981            input_schema  = {"city": "str — city name to fetch weather for"}
 982            output_schema = {"temp_c": "float", "condition": "str", "humidity": "int"}
 983        """
 984        manifest = {
 985            "name": self.name,
 986            "actor_id": self.actor_id,
 987            "description": description,
 988            "publishes": publishes or [],
 989            "capabilities": capabilities or [],
 990            "input_schema": input_schema or {},
 991            "output_schema": output_schema or {},
 992            "timestamp": time.time(),
 993        }
 994        await self._mqtt_publish(f"agents/{self.actor_id}/manifest", manifest, retain=True)

async def start(self): 
238    async def start(self):
239        """Start the actor's event loop."""
240        self.state = ActorState.RUNNING
241        self.metrics.start_time = time.time()
242        await self._load_persistent_state()
243        # Restore the message count from a previous run — but only into a fresh
244        # instance. The supervisor restarts by building a new actor, whose count
245        # is zero; the start command restarts *this* object, whose count is
246        # already the live total. Adding the persisted value there counts every
247        # message twice, and again on each subsequent stop/start.
248        if self.metrics.messages_processed == 0:
249            saved_msgs = self.recall("_messages_processed", {})
250            if isinstance(saved_msgs, dict) and saved_msgs.get("count"):
251                self.metrics.messages_processed = int(saved_msgs["count"])
252        await self.on_start()
253        self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._message_loop()))
254        self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._heartbeat_loop()))
255        self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._command_listener()))
256        await self._publish_status()
257        logger.info("[%s] Actor started.", self.name)

Start the actor's event loop.

async def stop(self): 
259    async def stop(self):
260        """Gracefully stop the actor."""
261        self.state = ActorState.STOPPED
262        await self._wind_down_tasks()
263        # Shield cleanup from CancelledError — chat tasks run as fire-and-forget
264        # asyncio tasks outside actor._tasks and get cancelled by asyncio.run()
265        # cleanup BEFORE these awaits if we don't shield them.
266        #
267        # A cancellation arriving here belongs to whoever is *calling* stop(),
268        # not to this cleanup: `shield` keeps the inner coroutine running and
269        # raises in the awaiting task. Discarding it told that caller its
270        # cancellation had been honoured when it had not — the supervisor's watch
271        # loop resumed polling, and `Supervisor.stop()` waited forever on a task
272        # already marked cancelling. So it is remembered, both steps still run,
273        # and it is re-raised once cleanup is done.
274        cancelled = False
275        try:
276            await asyncio.shield(self.on_stop())
277        except asyncio.CancelledError:
278            cancelled = True
279        except Exception:
280            pass
281        try:
282            await asyncio.shield(self._save_persistent_state())
283        except asyncio.CancelledError:
284            cancelled = True
285        except Exception:
286            pass
287
288        # ── Persist message count so overview survives restarts ──────────
289        if self.metrics.messages_processed > 0:
290            self.persist("_messages_processed", {"count": self.metrics.messages_processed})
291
292        # ── Persist final cost metrics (for LLM-backed agents) ─────────
293        # Cost data lives in-memory and dies with the agent object.
294        # Persist it so the UI can show lifetime costs for deleted agents.
295        if hasattr(self, "total_cost_usd") and getattr(self, "total_cost_usd", 0) > 0:
296            self.persist(
297                "_final_cost",
298                {
299                    "input_tokens": getattr(self, "total_input_tokens", 0),
300                    "output_tokens": getattr(self, "total_output_tokens", 0),
301                    "cost_usd": round(getattr(self, "total_cost_usd", 0), 6),
302                    "name": self.name,
303                    "stopped_at": time.time(),
304                },
305            )
306
307        # ── Publish final metrics before the agent disappears ──────────
308        # The heartbeat loop is already cancelled at this point, so this
309        # is the UI's last chance to capture cost/usage data.
310        try:
311            final_metrics = self._build_metrics()
312            final_metrics["final"] = True  # signals UI this is the last message
313            await self._mqtt_publish(
314                f"agents/{self.actor_id}/metrics",
315                final_metrics,
316            )
317        except Exception:
318            pass
319
320        await self._publish_status()
321        # ── Unregister from TopicBus ───────────────────────────────────
322        # Remove this agent's TopicContract so the planner doesn't wire
323        # against topics from stopped/deleted/replaced agents.
324        try:
325            from .topic_bus import get_topic_bus
326
327            bus = get_topic_bus()
328            if bus:
329                bus.unregister(self.name)
330        except Exception:
331            pass  # TopicBus not initialised or unavailable — not fatal
332        logger.info("[%s] Actor stopped.", self.name)
333        # Deferred to here rather than raised where it arrived: the shield exists
334        # so cleanup completes, and stopping half way through would defeat it.
335        # The caller still learns its cancellation was real.
336        if cancelled:
337            raise asyncio.CancelledError

TASK_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT = 5.0
LIFECYCLE_COMMANDS = ('start', 'stop', 'delete')
async def apply_command(self, command: str) -> bool: 
585    async def apply_command(self, command: str) -> bool:
586        """Run a lifecycle command on this actor. Returns whether it took effect.
587
588        These are not a dispatch table, which is why they live here rather than
589        in the transport below: ``stop`` must release from supervision first, and
590        ``delete`` also clears the spawn registry and unregisters. A caller that
591        holds the actor and simply awaits ``stop()`` gets it restarted half a
592        minute later by the watchdog.
593
594        Every entry point routes through this — the broker listener, and the web
595        layer when the actor is local — so the two cannot drift apart.
596
597        Returns ``False`` when the command was refused -- ``delete`` on a
598        protected actor, ``stop`` on an essential one -- or unknown, so a caller
599        can report that rather than claim success.
600        """
601        if forbidden(command, protected=self.protected, essential=self.essential):
602            logger.warning("[%s] Ignoring %r — refused by policy.", self.name, command)
603            return False
604
605        if command == "start":
606            if self.state != ActorState.STOPPED:
607                logger.warning("[%s] Ignoring 'start' — actor is %s.", self.name, self.state.value)
608                return False
609            await self.start()
610            self._resume_supervision()
611        elif command == "stop":
612            self._release_from_supervision()
613            await self.stop()
614        elif command == "delete":
615            self._release_from_supervision()
616            if self._registry:
617                main = self._registry.find_by_name("main")
618                if main and hasattr(main, "_remove_from_spawn_registry"):
619                    main._remove_from_spawn_registry(self.name)  # pyright: ignore[reportAttributeAccessIssue]
620                await self._registry.unregister(self.actor_id)
621            await self.stop()
622        else:
623            logger.warning("[%s] Unknown command: %r", self.name, command)
624            return False
625        return True

Run a lifecycle command on this actor. Returns whether it took effect.

These are not a dispatch table, which is why they live here rather than in the transport below: stop must release from supervision first, and delete also clears the spawn registry and unregisters. A caller that holds the actor and simply awaits stop() gets it restarted half a minute later by the watchdog.

Every entry point routes through this — the broker listener, and the web layer when the actor is local — so the two cannot drift apart.

Returns False when the command was refused -- delete on a protected actor, stop on an essential one -- or unknown, so a caller can report that rather than claim success.

669    async def send(self, target_id: str, msg_type: MessageType, payload: Any = None) -> bool:

671        if self._registry is None:
672            logger.warning("[%s] No registry attached, cannot send messages.", self.name)
673            return False
674        msg = Message(type=msg_type, sender_id=self.actor_id, payload=payload)
675        return await self._registry.deliver(target_id, msg)

async def spawn( self, actor_class: type[Actor], **kwargs: Any) -> Actor: 
688    async def spawn(self, actor_class: type[Actor], **kwargs: Any) -> Actor:
689        """Spawn a child actor. The child inherits:
690        - MQTT client (so it can publish heartbeats/status)
691        - Registry (so it can send/receive messages)
692        - Persistence dir defaults to same root
693        - Persistence API (SQLite/memory/Pickle routing)
694
695        Erlang/OTP supervision: if the owning ActorSystem has a Supervisor,
696        the child is automatically registered under it with ONE_FOR_ONE so it
697        will be restarted if it crashes — no child is an orphan.
698        """
699        # Default persistence to same root as parent
700        kwargs.setdefault("persistence_dir", str(self._persistence_dir.parent))
701
702        child = actor_class(**kwargs)
703
704        # Inherit everything from parent
705        child._mqtt_client = self._mqtt_client  # MQTT publish connection
706        child._mqtt_broker = self._mqtt_broker  # broker address for command listener
707        child._mqtt_port = self._mqtt_port  # broker port
708        child._registry = self._registry  # message routing
709
710        # Inherit persistence API if available
711        if self._persistence_api is not None:
712            try:
713                from .persistence import PersistenceAPI, get_db, get_pickle_store
714
715                db = get_db()
716                pkl = get_pickle_store()
717                if db and pkl:
718                    child._persistence_api = PersistenceAPI(db, pkl, child.name)
719            except ImportError:
720                pass
721
722        # Register in registry
723        if self._registry:
724            await self._registry.register(child)
725
726        # Start the child
727        await child.start()
728
729        # ── Erlang/OTP: register child under Supervisor so it's never an orphan ──
730        # We reach into the registry to find the ActorSystem's supervisor.
731        # If no supervisor is available this is a safe no-op.
732        try:
733            if self._registry and hasattr(self._registry, "_supervisor_ref"):
734                supervisor = self._registry._supervisor_ref
735                if supervisor is not None and child.name not in supervisor._specs:
736                    # Snapshot what the child was built from. The factory runs
737                    # again on every restart, possibly much later, and must
738                    # rebuild the child as it was rather than from whatever this
739                    # actor's settings have become since.
740                    cls = actor_class
741                    kw = dict(kwargs)
742                    mc = self._mqtt_client
743                    mb = self._mqtt_broker
744                    mp = self._mqtt_port
745                    papi = self._persistence_api
746
747                    async def _child_factory() -> Actor:
748                        c = cls(**kw)
749                        c._mqtt_client = mc
750                        c._mqtt_broker = mb
751                        c._mqtt_port = mp
752                        if papi is not None:
753                            try:
754                                from .persistence import (
755                                    PersistenceAPI,
756                                    get_db,
757                                    get_pickle_store,
758                                )
759
760                                db = get_db()
761                                pkl = get_pickle_store()
762                                if db and pkl:
763                                    c._persistence_api = PersistenceAPI(db, pkl, c.name)
764                            except ImportError:
765                                pass
766                        return c
767
768                    supervisor.supervise(
769                        child.name,
770                        _child_factory,
771                        strategy=SupervisorStrategy.ONE_FOR_ONE,
772                        max_restarts=5,
773                        restart_window=60.0,
774                        restart_delay=2.0,
775                    )
776                    # Point spec.actor at the already-running child so the watch loop
777                    # starts monitoring immediately without a redundant restart.
778                    supervisor._specs[child.name].actor = child
779                    if child.name not in supervisor._order:
780                        supervisor._order.append(child.name)
781                    child.supervisor_id = str(id(supervisor))
782                    logger.info(
783                        "[%s] Child '%s' auto-registered under Supervisor.", self.name, child.name
784                    )
785        except Exception as _sup_err:
786            # Never let supervision registration crash the spawn itself
787            logger.warning(
788                "[%s] Could not auto-supervise child '%s': %s", self.name, child.name, _sup_err
789            )
790
791        # Immediately announce to monitor - don't wait for heartbeat loop
792        await child._publish_status()
793        await child._mqtt_publish(
794            f"agents/{child.actor_id}/heartbeat",
795            child._build_heartbeat(),
796        )
797        await child._mqtt_publish(
798            f"agents/{child.actor_id}/metrics",
799            child._build_metrics(),
800        )
801
802        # Notify parent's topic that it spawned a child
803        await self._mqtt_publish(
804            f"agents/{self.actor_id}/spawned",
805            {"child_id": child.actor_id, "child_name": child.name, "timestamp": time.time()},
806        )
807        logger.info("[%s] Spawned: %s (%s)", self.name, child.name, child.actor_id[:8])
808        return child

Spawn a child actor. The child inherits:

  • MQTT client (so it can publish heartbeats/status)
  • Registry (so it can send/receive messages)
  • Persistence dir defaults to same root
  • Persistence API (SQLite/memory/Pickle routing)

Erlang/OTP supervision: if the owning ActorSystem has a Supervisor, the child is automatically registered under it with ONE_FOR_ONE so it will be restarted if it crashes — no child is an orphan.

def persist(self, key: str, value: Any): 
866    def persist(self, key: str, value: Any):
867        """Persist a key-value pair. Routes to the correct backend:
868          - Known structured keys → SQLite
869          - Known ephemeral keys → process memory
870          - Everything else → Pickle
871
872        If the new PersistenceAPI is not available, falls back to legacy
873        pickle behavior (writes entire dict to disk on every call).
874        """
875        if self._persistence_api is not None:
876            self._persistence_api.set(key, value)
877            return
878
879        # Legacy pickle path — the whole dict goes to disk on every call, so an
880        # interrupted write here would lose every key, not just this one.
881        self._persistent_state[key] = value
882        try:
883            write_pickle(self._persistence_dir / "state.pkl", self._persistent_state)
884        except Exception as e:
885            logger.warning("[%s] persist write failed for %r: %s", self.name, key, e)

Persist a key-value pair. Routes to the correct backend:

  • Known structured keys → SQLite
  • Known ephemeral keys → process memory
  • Everything else → Pickle

If the new PersistenceAPI is not available, falls back to legacy pickle behavior (writes entire dict to disk on every call).

def recall(self, key: str, default: Any = None) -> Any: 
887    def recall(self, key: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
888        """Recall a persisted value. Routes to the correct backend.
889        Returns default if the key doesn't exist.
890        """
891        if self._persistence_api is not None:
892            # Check new store first, then fall back to legacy in-memory dict
893            # (handles migration period where some keys are in pickle, some in new store)
894            result = self._persistence_api.get(key)
895            if result is not None:
896                return result
897            # Fallback: check legacy in-memory state (loaded from old .pkl)
898            return self._persistent_state.get(key, default)
899
900        # Legacy pickle path
901        return self._persistent_state.get(key, default)

Recall a persisted value. Routes to the correct backend. Returns default if the key doesn't exist.

933        The monitor forwards agents/{id}/chat messages to the chat panel as live
934        chat frames, so use this for autonomous notifications the user should see

947        await self._mqtt_publish(f"agents/{self.actor_id}/chat", payload)

969        self,
970        description: str = "",
971        publishes: list[str] | None = None,
972        capabilities: list[str] | None = None,
973        input_schema: dict[str, Any] | None = None,

class ActorRegistry: 
 84class ActorRegistry:
 85    """Maintains a map of all living actors and routes messages between them."""
 86
 87    def __init__(self) -> None:
 88        self._actors: dict[str, Actor] = {}
 89        self._lock = asyncio.Lock()
 90        # Back-reference to the Supervisor — set by ActorSystem after creating both.
 91        # Allows Actor.spawn() to auto-register children under supervision.
 92        self._supervisor_ref: Supervisor | None = None
 93
 94    async def register(self, actor: Actor) -> None:
 95        """Add an actor, replacing any earlier one holding the same id."""
 96        superseded: Actor | None = None
 97        async with self._lock:
 98            existing = self._actors.get(actor.actor_id)
 99            if existing is not None and existing is not actor:
100                if getattr(existing, "protected", False):
101                    # Because actor_id is a uuid5 of the name, an actor named
102                    # after a system agent does not collide with it — it lands
103                    # on the same id and the replacement below would stop the
104                    # original. The orchestrator would go down and the spawn
105                    # would report success. Callers reach this by any route, so
106                    # the refusal belongs here rather than only at the spawn path.
107                    raise ProtectedActorCollision(
108                        f"'{actor.name}' resolves to the same actor id as the running "
109                        f"protected actor '{existing.name}' ({actor.actor_id[:8]}); "
110                        f"registering it would stop the original. Use a different name."
111                    )
112                # Same deterministic actor_id (uuid5 of name) is being re-registered.
113                # The old instance's tasks (message loop, heartbeat loop, aiomqtt
114                # subscribe listeners spawned from setup()) are STILL RUNNING.
115                # If we just overwrite the dict entry, the old listener stays alive
116                # and we get duplicate MQTT message delivery — every published event
117                # invokes both callbacks. Stop the old instance asynchronously so
118                # its background tasks (and any aiomqtt subscriptions) shut down.
119                logger.warning(
120                    "[Registry] Overwriting existing actor '%s' (%s) — stopping old instance to prevent duplicate listeners / double MQTT delivery.",
121                    existing.name,
122                    actor.actor_id[:8],
123                )
124                # Stopped outside this lock to avoid re-entrancy: stop()
125                # acquires no shared lock but may await tasks that do.
126                superseded = existing
127            actor._registry = self
128            self._actors[actor.actor_id] = actor
129            logger.info("[Registry] Registered %s (%s)", actor.name, actor.actor_id[:8])
130
131        if superseded is not None:
132            # Awaited, not fired and forgotten. `create_task` here kept no
133            # reference, so the task could be garbage-collected mid-stop, and an
134            # exception inside it went to nobody — the failure mode being the one
135            # this code exists to prevent: an old instance still subscribed, so
136            # every published event is delivered twice.
137            try:
138                await superseded.stop()
139            except Exception as exc:
140                logger.error(
141                    "[Registry] Stopping the superseded '%s' failed — its listeners may still be live: %s",
142                    superseded.name,
143                    exc,
144                )
145
146    async def unregister(self, actor_id: str) -> None:
147        """Remove an actor. Does not stop it — the caller owns that."""
148        async with self._lock:
149            if actor_id in self._actors:
150                del self._actors[actor_id]
151                logger.info("[Registry] Unregistered %s", actor_id[:8])
152
153    async def deliver(self, target_id: str, msg: Message) -> bool:
154        """Put a message in one actor's mailbox. False if no such actor."""
155        actor = self._actors.get(target_id)
156        if actor is None:
157            logger.warning("[Registry] Unknown target: %s", target_id[:8])
158            return False
159        await actor.receive(msg)
160        return True
161
162    async def broadcast(self, sender_id: str, msg_type: MessageType, payload: Any = None) -> None:
163        """Send a message to every registered actor except the sender."""
164        msg = Message(type=msg_type, sender_id=sender_id, payload=payload)
165        for actor_id, actor in list(self._actors.items()):
166            if actor_id != sender_id:
167                await actor.receive(msg)
168
169    def get(self, actor_id: str) -> Actor | None:
170        """The actor with this id, or None."""
171        return self._actors.get(actor_id)
172
173    def all_actors(self) -> list[Actor]:
174        """Every registered actor."""
175        return list(self._actors.values())
176
177    def find_by_name(self, name: str) -> Actor | None:
178        """The first actor with this name, or None. Names are not unique."""
179        for actor in self._actors.values():
180            if actor.name == name:
181                return actor
182        return None
183
184    def __len__(self) -> int:
185        return len(self._actors)

Maintains a map of all living actors and routes messages between them.

class ActorSystem: 
648class ActorSystem:
649    """Top-level orchestrator."""
650
651    def __init__(
652        self, mqtt_broker: str = "localhost", mqtt_port: int = 1883, state_dir: str | None = None
653    ):
654        self.registry = ActorRegistry()
655        self._mqtt_broker = mqtt_broker
656        self._mqtt_port = mqtt_port
657        self._mqtt_client = None
658        self._running = False
659        self._supervisor: Supervisor | None = None
660        self._state_dir = resolve_state_dir(state_dir)
661        # Created in start(), which is the first point an MQTT client exists to
662        # give it. Declared here so the attribute is not conjured into being
663        # halfway through the object's life.
664        self.topic_bus = None
665
666    def _inject(self, actor: Actor):
667        """Inject MQTT client + broker/port into an actor so it can publish and subscribe."""
668        actor._mqtt_client = self._mqtt_client
669        actor._mqtt_broker = self._mqtt_broker
670        actor._mqtt_port = self._mqtt_port
671
672    @property
673    def supervisor(self) -> Supervisor:
674        """Lazy-create the Supervisor bound to this system's registry and inject function."""
675        if self._supervisor is None:
676            self._supervisor = Supervisor(self.registry, self._inject)
677            # Give the registry a back-reference so Actor.spawn() children are auto-supervised
678            self.registry._supervisor_ref = self._supervisor
679        return self._supervisor
680
681    def mqtt_status(self) -> dict:
682        """Return current MQTT publisher health — useful for dashboard and /nodes."""
683        if self._mqtt_client is None:
684            return {"connected": False, "queue_depth": 0, "available": False}
685        return {
686            "connected": getattr(self._mqtt_client, "connected", False),
687            "queue_depth": getattr(self._mqtt_client, "queue_depth", 0),
688            "available": getattr(self._mqtt_client, "_available", False),
689            "client_id": getattr(self._mqtt_client, "_client_id", "?"),
690        }
691
692    async def start(self, *initial_actors: Actor):
693        """Bring the system up: MQTT, topic bus, the given actors, supervision."""
694        self._running = True
695
696        os.makedirs(self._state_dir, exist_ok=True)
697        db_path = os.path.join(self._state_dir, "mqtt_outbox.db")
698        self._mqtt_client = await MQTTPublisher.create(
699            self._mqtt_broker, self._mqtt_port, db_path=db_path
700        )
701
702        # ── Initialise TopicBus (reactive pub/sub coordination layer) ─────
703        from .topic_bus import init_topic_bus
704
705        self.topic_bus = init_topic_bus(
706            mqtt_client=self._mqtt_client,
707            mqtt_broker=self._mqtt_broker,
708            mqtt_port=self._mqtt_port,
709        )
710        logger.info("[ActorSystem] TopicBus initialised")
711
712        for actor in initial_actors:
713            self._inject(actor)
714            await self.registry.register(actor)
715            await actor.start()
716
717        logger.info("[ActorSystem] Started with %s actors.", len(initial_actors))
718
719    async def spawn(self, actor_class: type[Actor], **kwargs) -> Actor:
720        """Spawn and register a new actor in the system."""
721        actor = actor_class(**kwargs)
722        self._inject(actor)
723        await self.registry.register(actor)
724        await actor.start()
725        return actor
726
727    async def stop_all(self):
728        """Shut everything down in reverse: supervisor, actors, then MQTT."""
729        self._running = False
730        # Stop supervisor first so it doesn't try to restart actors we're about to stop
731        if self._supervisor:
732            await self._supervisor.stop()
733        actors = self.registry.all_actors()
734        await asyncio.gather(*[a.stop() for a in actors], return_exceptions=True)
735        if self._mqtt_client:
736            await self._mqtt_client.disconnect()
737            self._mqtt_client = None  # drop ref so GC can collect paho client now
738        gc.collect()  # break aiomqtt↔paho ref cycle while loop is open
739        logger.info("[ActorSystem] All actors stopped.")
740
741    async def run_forever(self):
742        """Block until the system is stopped or interrupted."""
743        try:
744            while self._running:
745                await asyncio.sleep(1)
746        except (KeyboardInterrupt, asyncio.CancelledError):
747            logger.info("[ActorSystem] Shutdown signal received.")
748            await self.stop_all()
