class DynamicAgent(wactorz.Actor): 
 44class DynamicAgent(Actor):
 45    """Generic actor shell. Core behavior is provided as Python source code strings.
 46    The LLM writes setup/process/handle_task functions; this class runs them.
 47    """
 48
 49    def __init__(
 50        self,
 51        code: str,  # LLM-generated Python source
 52        poll_interval: float = 1.0,  # seconds between process() calls
 53        description: str = "",  # what this agent does
 54        input_schema: dict[str, Any] | None = None,  # expected task payload fields
 55        output_schema: dict[str, Any] | None = None,  # returned result fields
 56        llm_provider: Any = None,  # optional LLM for agent.llm.chat()
 57        trusted: bool = False,  # True = catalog agent, skip safety validator
 58        **kwargs: Any,
 59    ) -> None:
 60        super().__init__(**kwargs)
 61        self._code = code
 62        self.poll_interval = poll_interval
 63        self.description = description
 64        self.input_schema = input_schema or {}
 65        self.output_schema = output_schema or {}
 66        self._llm_provider = llm_provider
 67        self._trusted = trusted  # catalog agents bypass safety checks
 68
 69        # Compiled functions — populated in on_start
 70        self._fn_setup = None
 71        self._fn_process = None
 72        self._fn_handle_task = None
 73
 74        # Namespace shared across all calls (agent can store state here)
 75        self._ns: dict = {}
 76
 77        # Cost tracking (populated by LLMInterface if LLM is used)
 78        self.total_input_tokens = 0
 79        self.total_output_tokens = 0
 80        self.total_cost_usd = 0.0
 81        self._last_period_cost_usd = 0.0
 82
 83        # Error tracking for health classification
 84        self._consecutive_errors: int = 0
 85        self._error_threshold: int = 3  # DEGRADED after this many
 86        self._last_error_time: float = 0.0
 87        self._error_phase: str = ""  # compile|setup|process|handle_task
 88
 89        # Public API exposed to generated code via `agent` parameter
 90        # Owned here rather than grafted on by AgentAPI at first use: a
 91        # collaborator creating attributes on its host hides them from every
 92        # reader and from the type checker.
 93        #: Per-topic timestamp of the last callback error, for backoff.
 94        self._cb_error_last: dict[str, float] = {}
 95        #: Per-topic count of consecutive callback errors.
 96        self._cb_error_count: dict[str, int] = {}
 97        #: (topic, callback id) pairs already subscribed, to refuse duplicates.
 98        self._subscribed_topics: dict[tuple[str, int], Any] = {}
 99        #: The last contract this agent declared, published in its manifest.
100        self._topic_contract: Any = None
101        self._api = AgentAPI(self)
102
103    # ── Lifecycle ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
104
105    async def on_start(self) -> None:
106        # ── Compile with LLM self-correction on syntax errors ─────────────
107        current_code = self._code
108        error_msg = self._compile_code(current_code)
109
110        if error_msg:
111            for attempt in range(1, self._MAX_COMPILE_RETRIES + 1):
112                logger.warning("[%s] Compile error (attempt %s): %s", self.name, attempt, error_msg)
113                fixed = await self._fix_syntax_with_llm(current_code, error_msg)
114                if fixed is None:
115                    # LLM unavailable — no point retrying
116                    break
117                self._ns = {}  # fresh namespace for retry
118                new_err = self._compile_code(fixed)
119                if new_err is None:
120                    # Fix worked — update stored code so restarts use the good version
121                    self._code = fixed
122                    error_msg = None
123                    logger.info("[%s] Code fixed by LLM after %s attempt(s).", self.name, attempt)
124                    # ── Write fixed code back to spawn registry so restart uses it ──
125                    self._persist_fixed_code(fixed)
126                    await self._mqtt_publish(
127                        f"agents/{self.actor_id}/logs",
128                        {
129                            "type": "log",
130                            "message": f"Syntax error fixed by LLM after {attempt} attempt(s).",
131                            "timestamp": time.time(),
132                        },
133                    )
134                    break
135                # Fix compiled but still broken — feed it back for the next attempt
136                current_code = fixed
137                error_msg = new_err
138
139        if error_msg:
140            # All attempts exhausted — publish fatal and stop
141            err_exc = SyntaxError(error_msg)
142            logger.error("[%s] Code compilation failed permanently: %s", self.name, error_msg)
143            # ── Erlang/OTP: mark FAILED so Supervisor's watch_loop detects us ──
144            self.state = ActorState.FAILED
145            await self._publish_error(
146                phase="compile", error=err_exc, traceback_str=error_msg, fatal=True
147            )
148            return
149
150        # ── setup() ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
151        if self._fn_setup:
152            # Run setup as a background task so long-running loops (e.g. aiomqtt
153            # subscriptions) don't block on_start() and prevent heartbeats from firing.
154            self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._run_setup()))
155        else:
156            if self._fn_process:
157                self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._process_loop()))
158
159        # Publish manifest immediately so main's registry knows this agent exists
160        # even if it never calls publish() (pure handle_task agents, etc.)
161        await self._api._publish_manifest()
162
163    async def _publish_final_metrics(self) -> None:
164        """The last metrics before the heartbeat loop stops, flagged final."""
165        try:
166            await self._mqtt_publish(
167                f"agents/{self.actor_id}/metrics",
168                self._build_metrics()
169                if hasattr(self, "_build_metrics")
170                else {
171                    "actor_id": self.actor_id,
172                    "input_tokens": getattr(self, "total_input_tokens", 0),
173                    "output_tokens": getattr(self, "total_output_tokens", 0),
174                    "cost_usd": round(getattr(self, "total_cost_usd", 0.0), 6),
175                    "messages_processed": self.metrics.messages_processed,
176                    "errors": self.metrics.errors,
177                    "uptime": self.metrics.uptime,
178                    "final": True,  # signals UI this is the last metrics msg
179                },
180            )
181        except Exception as exc:
182            logger.debug("[%s] Final metrics publish failed: %s", self.name, exc)
183
184    def _unregister_from_bus(self) -> None:
185        """Drop this agent's contracts so stale ones do not accumulate."""
186        try:
187            from ...core.topic_bus import get_topic_bus
188
189            bus = get_topic_bus()
190            if bus:
191                bus.unregister(self.name)
192                logger.debug("[%s] Unregistered from TopicBus", self.name)
193        except Exception as exc:
194            logger.debug("[%s] Could not unregister from TopicBus: %s", self.name, exc)
195
196    async def _run_generated_cleanup(self) -> None:
197        """Give the generated code its chance to let go, under a timeout."""
198        cleanup = self._ns.get("cleanup")
199        if cleanup:
200            try:
201                await asyncio.wait_for(cleanup(self._api), timeout=10.0)
202            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
203                logger.warning("[%s] cleanup() timed out after 10s", self.name)
204            except Exception as e:
205                logger.warning("[%s] cleanup() error: %s", self.name, e)
206
207    async def on_stop(self) -> None:
208        # ── Persist final cost metrics so they survive agent deletion ──────
209        # Without this, cost data dies with the agent object and the UI
210        # can't show lifetime costs for deleted agents.
211        if hasattr(self, "total_cost_usd") and self.total_cost_usd > 0:
212            self.persist(
213                "_final_cost",
214                {
215                    "input_tokens": self.total_input_tokens,
216                    "output_tokens": self.total_output_tokens,
217                    "cost_usd": round(self.total_cost_usd, 6),
218                    "name": self.name,
219                    "stopped_at": time.time(),
220                },
221            )
222
223        await self._publish_final_metrics()
224
225        self._unregister_from_bus()
226
227        await self._run_generated_cleanup()
228
229        release_open_resources(self._api, self._ns, self.name)
230
231        # ── Cancel any tasks spawned inside setup/process code ─────────────
232        # Generated code may have called asyncio.create_task() directly without
233        # adding to _tasks. We can't track those, but we can ensure all tasks
234        # we DO track are properly cancelled and awaited.
235        for task in self._tasks:
236            if not task.done():
237                task.cancel()
238        # Give cancelled tasks a moment to actually stop
239        if self._tasks:
240            await asyncio.gather(*self._tasks, return_exceptions=True)
241
242    # ── Code compilation ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
243
244    # Max times on_start will ask the LLM to fix a syntax error before giving up
245    _MAX_COMPILE_RETRIES = 2
246
247    # ── Pre-exec safety validator ──────────────────────────────────────────
248    # Scans sanitized code for dangerous patterns BEFORE exec().
249    # This is NOT a sandbox — it's a best-effort blocklist.
250    # For true isolation, run DynamicAgents in a subprocess or container.
251
252    # Patterns that are suspicious but allowed — just logged as warnings
253
254    # Patterns checked specifically inside process() body — cause 120s timeout crashes
255
256    _sanitize_code = staticmethod(sanitize_code)
257    _extract_function_body = staticmethod(extract_function_body)
258
259    def _validate_code_safety(self, code: str) -> str | None:
260        return validate_code_safety(code, self.name)
261
262    def _compile_code(self, code: str | None = None) -> str | None:
263        """Sanitize, validate safety, then compile LLM-generated code into self._ns.
264
265        Returns the error message string if compilation fails, None on success.
266        Callers use the error string to ask the LLM to fix the code and retry
267        (see on_start / _fix_syntax_with_llm).
268
269        Trusted agents (from the catalog) skip the safety validator — their code
270        is pre-built and tested, and may legitimately use __import__, subprocess,
271        etc. that the safety validator would block.
272        """
273        source = code if code is not None else self._code
274        clean = self._sanitize_code(source) if not self._trusted else source
275
276        # ── Safety check before exec (skipped for trusted/catalog agents) ──
277        if not self._trusted:
278            safety_error = self._validate_code_safety(clean)
279            if safety_error:
280                return safety_error
281        else:
282            logger.info("[%s] Trusted agent — skipping safety validator", self.name)
283
284        # Pre-inject the LLM shim so generated code can call agent.llm directly
285        def _get_llm_shim(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
286            from ...llm_factory import provider_for
287
288            # The shim hands generated code the agent's own interface, which
289            # answers the same calls without being an LLMProvider subclass.
290            return provider_for("dynamic", cast("LLMProvider | None", self._api.llm))
291
292        self._ns["get_llm"] = _get_llm_shim
293        self._ns["setup_llm"] = _get_llm_shim
294        self._ns["create_llm"] = _get_llm_shim
295
296        # ── cv2 shim: wrap VideoCapture with retry + release-before-reopen ──
297        # Only injected when the agent code actually references cv2 — no-op for
298        # chat agents, schedulers, or anything else that doesn't use the camera.
299        # LLM code uses `_cap = cv2.VideoCapture(0)` as a global. On Windows
300        # (MSMF backend) the previous session's handle may not be fully released
301        # by the OS yet, so the first open succeeds but grabFrame() immediately
302        # fails with -1072873821. The shim retries with increasing delays so the
303        # agent recovers without manual intervention.
304
305        if re.search(r"\bcv2\b", clean):
306            shim = resilient_cv2_module(self.name)
307            if shim is not None:
308                self._ns["cv2"] = shim
309
310        try:
311            exec(compile(clean, f"<{self.name}>", "exec"), self._ns)
312            self._fn_setup = self._ns.get("setup")
313            self._fn_process = self._ns.get("process")
314            self._fn_handle_task = self._ns.get("handle_task")
315            fns = [f for f in ["setup", "process", "handle_task", "cleanup"] if f in self._ns]
316            logger.info("[%s] Code compiled OK. Functions: %s", self.name, fns)
317            if not fns:
318                logger.warning("[%s] No functions found in compiled code.", self.name)
319        except Exception as e:
320            return f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
321        else:
322            return None  # success
323
324    async def _fix_syntax_with_llm(self, bad_code: str, error_msg: str) -> str | None:
325        """Ask the configured LLM to fix a syntax error in agent code.
326
327        Returns the (possibly still-broken) code string from the LLM, or None
328        only if the LLM is completely unavailable (no provider, API error).
329        The caller is responsible for verifying the fix with _compile_code().
330        """
331        if self._llm_provider is None:
332            return None
333
334        prompt = (
335            "The following Python code has a syntax error.\n"
336            f"Error: {error_msg}\n\n"
337            "Fix ONLY the syntax error. Do not change logic or add features.\n"
338            "Return ONLY the corrected Python code — no explanations, "
339            "no markdown fences, no commentary.\n\n"
340            f"```python\n{bad_code}\n```"
341        )
342        logger.info("[%s] Asking LLM to fix syntax error: %s", self.name, error_msg[:120])
343        await self._mqtt_publish(
344            f"agents/{self.actor_id}/logs",
345            {
346                "type": "log",
347                "message": f"Syntax error — asking LLM to fix: {error_msg[:120]}",
348                "timestamp": time.time(),
349            },
350        )
351        try:
352            response, usage = await self._llm_provider.complete(
353                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
354                system="You are a Python syntax expert. Return only valid Python code.",
355                max_tokens=4096,
356            )
357            # Track cost
358            if hasattr(self, "total_input_tokens"):
359                self._accrue_usage(usage)
360
361            # Strip markdown fences the LLM may add despite instructions
362            fixed = response.strip()
363            if fixed.startswith("```"):
364                fixed = "\n".join(
365                    ln for ln in fixed.split("\n") if not ln.strip().startswith("```")
366                ).strip()
367
368        except Exception as e:
369            logger.warning("[%s] LLM fix call failed: %s", self.name, e)
370            return None  # only None when LLM is truly unreachable
371        else:
372            return fixed  # caller validates with _compile_code()
373
374    # ── Setup wrapper ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
375
376    # Max times _run_setup will ask the LLM to fix a runtime error before giving up
377    _MAX_SETUP_RETRIES = 2
378
379    async def _attempt_setup_with_repair(self, setup: Any, current_code: str) -> Any:
380        """Run setup(), asking the model to repair the code between attempts."""
381        last_error = None
382        for attempt in range(1 + self._MAX_SETUP_RETRIES):
383            try:
384                await setup(self._api)
385                if attempt > 0:
386                    logger.info("[%s] setup() succeeded after %s fix(es).", self.name, attempt)
387                    # ── Write fixed code back to spawn registry so restart uses it ──
388                    self._persist_fixed_code(self._code)
389                    await self._mqtt_publish(
390                        f"agents/{self.actor_id}/logs",
391                        {
392                            "type": "log",
393                            "message": f"setup() runtime error fixed by LLM after {attempt} attempt(s).",
394                            "timestamp": time.time(),
395                        },
396                    )
397                else:
398                    logger.info("[%s] setup() completed.", self.name)
399                last_error = None
400                break
401            except asyncio.CancelledError:
402                return None
403            except Exception as e:
404                last_error = e
405                err = traceback.format_exc()
406                logger.exception("[%s] setup() failed (attempt %s)", self.name, attempt + 1)
407
408                if attempt >= self._MAX_SETUP_RETRIES:
409                    break  # exhausted retries
410
411                # Ask LLM to fix the runtime error
412                fixed = await self._fix_runtime_with_llm(current_code, str(e), err)
413                if fixed is None:
414                    logger.warning("[%s] LLM unavailable — cannot fix setup() error", self.name)
415                    break
416
417                # Recompile the fixed code
418                self._ns = {}
419                compile_err = self._compile_code(fixed)
420                if compile_err:
421                    logger.warning(
422                        "[%s] LLM fix introduced compile error: %s", self.name, compile_err
423                    )
424                    # Try to fix the compile error too
425                    fixed2 = await self._fix_syntax_with_llm(fixed, compile_err)
426                    if fixed2:
427                        self._ns = {}
428                        compile_err2 = self._compile_code(fixed2)
429                        if compile_err2:
430                            break  # can't fix compile error either
431                        fixed = fixed2
432                    else:
433                        break
434                else:
435                    # compile_err is None — code is good
436                    pass
437
438                self._code = fixed
439                current_code = fixed
440                logger.info(
441                    "[%s] Retrying setup() with LLM-fixed code (attempt %s)...",
442                    self.name,
443                    attempt + 1,
444                )
445        return last_error
446
447    async def _run_setup(self) -> None:
448        """Run setup() as a background task with LLM self-correction on failure.
449
450        If setup() raises a runtime error (e.g. TypeError from await on sync call,
451        NameError, AttributeError), the LLM is asked to fix the code and the whole
452        compile-then-setup cycle is retried up to _MAX_SETUP_RETRIES times.
453
454        - If process() is also defined, it is started AFTER setup() returns.
455          For agents whose setup() never returns (e.g. aiomqtt subscription loops),
456          process() is simply not started — the subscription loop IS the process.
457        """
458        current_code = self._code
459
460        setup = self._fn_setup
461        if setup is None:  # the caller checks this; kept so the type is honest
462            return
463
464        last_error = await self._attempt_setup_with_repair(setup, current_code)
465
466        if last_error is not None:
467            err = traceback.format_exc()
468            logger.error("[%s] setup() failed permanently: %s", self.name, last_error)
469            # ── Erlang/OTP: mark FAILED so Supervisor's watch_loop can see us ──
470            self.state = ActorState.FAILED
471            await self._publish_error(
472                phase="setup", error=last_error, traceback_str=err, fatal=True
473            )
474            return
475
476        # setup() returned cleanly — start process() loop if defined
477        if self._fn_process and self.state not in (ActorState.STOPPED, ActorState.FAILED):
478            self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._process_loop()))
479
480    async def _fix_runtime_with_llm(
481        self, code: str, error_msg: str, traceback_str: str
482    ) -> str | None:
483        """Ask the LLM to fix a runtime error in agent code (setup/process).
484
485        Similar to _fix_syntax_with_llm but provides the traceback and
486        explicit guidance about the agent API (sync vs async methods).
487        """
488        if self._llm_provider is None:
489            return None
490
491        prompt = (
492            "The following Python code raised a RUNTIME ERROR when executed.\n\n"
493            f"Error: {error_msg}\n"
494            f"Traceback (last 800 chars):\n{traceback_str[-800:]}\n\n"
495            "IMPORTANT API RULES — these are the most common mistakes:\n"
496            "  - agent.subscribe(topic, callback) is SYNCHRONOUS — do NOT use await\n"
497            "  - agent.window(topic, seconds=N) is SYNCHRONOUS — do NOT use await\n"
498            "  - agent.persist(key, val) is SYNCHRONOUS — do NOT use await\n"
499            "  - agent.recall(key) is SYNCHRONOUS — do NOT use await\n"
500            "  - agent.declare_contract(...) is SYNCHRONOUS — do NOT use await\n"
501            "  - agent.agents() is SYNCHRONOUS — do NOT use await\n"
502            "  - await agent.publish(topic, data) — this IS async, use await\n"
503            "  - await agent.log(msg) — this IS async, use await\n"
504            "  - await agent.alert(msg) — this IS async, use await\n"
505            "  - await agent.send_to(name, payload) — this IS async, use await\n"
506            "  - await agent.mqtt_get(topic) — this IS async, use await\n\n"
507            "STREAMWINDOW API — w = agent.window('topic', seconds=N):\n"
508            "  StreamWindow is NOT a dict. Use methods, not dict-style access.\n"
509            "  Methods: count(), mean('field'), min('field'), max('field'),\n"
510            "           values('field'), latest(), rising('field', threshold=X),\n"
511            "           falling(), stable(), absent_for(seconds),\n"
512            "           event_count(key='k', value=V, seconds=N)\n"
513            "  WRONG: w.get('temp')        — StreamWindow is not a dict\n"
514            "  WRONG: w['temp']            — no __getitem__ by key intended\n"
515            "  RIGHT: w.latest()           — returns latest payload dict (or None)\n"
516            "  RIGHT: w.values('temp')     — list of all 'temp' values in window\n"
517            "  RIGHT: w.mean('temp')       — average of 'temp' over window\n\n"
518            "Fix the error. Return ONLY the corrected Python code — no explanations, "
519            "no markdown fences, no commentary.\n\n"
520            f"```python\n{code}\n```"
521        )
522        logger.info("[%s] Asking LLM to fix runtime error: %s", self.name, error_msg[:120])
523        await self._mqtt_publish(
524            f"agents/{self.actor_id}/logs",
525            {
526                "type": "log",
527                "message": f"Runtime error — asking LLM to fix: {error_msg[:120]}",
528                "timestamp": time.time(),
529            },
530        )
531        try:
532            response, usage = await self._llm_provider.complete(
533                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
534                system=(
535                    "You are a Python runtime-error expert for an async agent framework. "
536                    "Return only valid Python code."
537                ),
538                max_tokens=4096,
539            )
540            if hasattr(self, "total_input_tokens"):
541                self._accrue_usage(usage)
542
543            fixed = response.strip()
544            if fixed.startswith("```"):
545                fixed = "\n".join(
546                    ln for ln in fixed.split("\n") if not ln.strip().startswith("```")
547                ).strip()
548
549        except Exception as e:
550            logger.warning("[%s] LLM runtime-fix call failed: %s", self.name, e)
551            return None
552        else:
553            return fixed
554
555    # ── Process loop ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
556
557    # Max time a single process() or handle_task() call can take before
558    # we assume it's stuck in a blocking call and cancel it.
559    _PROCESS_TIMEOUT = 120.0  # seconds
560    _HANDLE_TASK_TIMEOUT = 60.0
561
562    # ── How many consecutive process() errors before we attempt LLM self-fix ──
563    _PROCESS_LLM_FIX_THRESHOLD = 3  # try to fix after this many errors in a row
564    # How many consecutive process() errors trigger state=FAILED (Supervisor sees this)
565    _PROCESS_FAIL_THRESHOLD = 5
566
567    async def _run_process_forever(self, process: Any) -> None:
568        """Call process() on each tick until the agent stops or fails."""
569        _llm_fix_attempted = False
570        while self.state not in (ActorState.STOPPED, ActorState.FAILED):
571            try:
572                await asyncio.wait_for(
573                    process(self._api),
574                    timeout=self._PROCESS_TIMEOUT,
575                )
576                self._reset_error_count()
577                _llm_fix_attempted = False  # reset after a clean run
578            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
579                self.metrics.errors += 1
580                logger.exception(
581                    "[%s] process() timed out after %ss — likely a blocking call without run_in_executor",
582                    self.name,
583                    self._PROCESS_TIMEOUT,
584                )
585                await self._publish_error(
586                    phase="process",
587                    error=TimeoutError(f"process() exceeded {self._PROCESS_TIMEOUT}s"),
588                    traceback_str=f"process() did not return within {self._PROCESS_TIMEOUT}s. "
589                    f"Wrap blocking calls (cv2, torch) in: "
590                    f"await asyncio.get_event_loop().run_in_executor(None, fn)",
591                )
592                # Erlang: escalate to FAILED after too many timeouts — Supervisor takes over
593                if self._consecutive_errors >= self._PROCESS_FAIL_THRESHOLD:
594                    logger.critical(
595                        "[%s] process() timed out %sx — setting FAILED so Supervisor can restart cleanly.",
596                        self.name,
597                        self._consecutive_errors,
598                    )
599                    self.state = ActorState.FAILED
600                    return
601                backoff = min(2**self._consecutive_errors, 30)
602                await asyncio.sleep(backoff)
603            except asyncio.CancelledError:
604                break
605            except Exception as e:
606                self.metrics.errors += 1
607                tb = traceback.format_exc()
608                logger.exception("[%s] process() error", self.name)
609                await self._publish_error(phase="process", error=e, traceback_str=tb)
610
611                # ── LLM self-healing: try to fix the code in-place ────────────
612                if (
613                    not _llm_fix_attempted
614                    and self._consecutive_errors >= self._PROCESS_LLM_FIX_THRESHOLD
615                    and self._llm_provider is not None
616                ):
617                    _llm_fix_attempted = True
618                    logger.warning(
619                        "[%s] %s consecutive process() errors — asking LLM to fix code in-place.",
620                        self.name,
621                        self._consecutive_errors,
622                    )
623                    fixed = await self._fix_runtime_with_llm(self._code, str(e), tb)
624                    if fixed is not None:
625                        self._ns = {}
626                        compile_err = self._compile_code(fixed)
627                        if compile_err is None:
628                            self._code = fixed
629                            self._consecutive_errors = 0  # give the fixed code a clean slate
630                            # ── Write fixed code back to spawn registry so restart uses it ──
631                            self._persist_fixed_code(fixed)
632                            logger.info(
633                                "[%s] LLM fixed process() code — resuming with patched version.",
634                                self.name,
635                            )
636                            await self._mqtt_publish(
637                                f"agents/{self.actor_id}/logs",
638                                {
639                                    "type": "log",
640                                    "message": "process() runtime error fixed by LLM in-place.",
641                                    "timestamp": time.time(),
642                                },
643                            )
644                            await asyncio.sleep(self.poll_interval)
645                            continue
646                        logger.warning(
647                            "[%s] LLM fix introduced compile error: %s", self.name, compile_err
648                        )
649
650                # ── Erlang: too many errors → FAILED → Supervisor restarts us ──
651                if self._consecutive_errors >= self._PROCESS_FAIL_THRESHOLD:
652                    logger.critical(
653                        "[%s] %s consecutive process() errors — setting FAILED so Supervisor can restart cleanly.",
654                        self.name,
655                        self._consecutive_errors,
656                    )
657                    self.state = ActorState.FAILED
658                    await self._publish_error(
659                        phase="process", error=e, traceback_str=tb, fatal=True
660                    )
661                    return
662
663                backoff = min(2**self._consecutive_errors, 30)
664                await asyncio.sleep(backoff)
665
666            await asyncio.sleep(self.poll_interval)
667
668    async def _process_loop(self) -> None:
669        """Continuously call the generated process() function.
670
671        Erlang/OTP semantics:
672        - Each error increments _consecutive_errors.
673        - At _PROCESS_LLM_FIX_THRESHOLD consecutive errors, ask the LLM to fix the code
674          and recompile in-place (self-healing).
675        - At _PROCESS_FAIL_THRESHOLD consecutive errors (or after LLM fix fails),
676          set state=FAILED — the Supervisor's _watch_loop will detect this and restart us.
677          This is the "let it crash" principle: don't spin in degraded mode forever.
678        """
679        process = self._fn_process
680        if process is None:  # the caller checks this; kept so the type is honest
681            return
682
683        _llm_fix_attempted = False  # only try the LLM fix once per process_loop lifetime
684
685        await self._run_process_forever(process)
686
687    # ── Message handling ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
688
689    async def _invoke_handle_task(
690        self, msg: Message, _incoming: Any, _corr: Any, _with_corr: Any
691    ) -> Any:
692        """Call the generated handle_task(), tagging the reply with its id."""
693        if self._fn_handle_task:
694            try:
695                result = await asyncio.wait_for(
696                    self._fn_handle_task(self._api, msg.payload or {}),
697                    timeout=self._HANDLE_TASK_TIMEOUT,
698                )
699                if msg.sender_id and result is not None:
700                    await self.send(msg.sender_id, MessageType.RESULT, _with_corr(result))
701            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
702                logger.exception(
703                    "[%s] handle_task() timed out after %ss", self.name, self._HANDLE_TASK_TIMEOUT
704                )
705                await self._publish_error(
706                    phase="handle_task",
707                    error=TimeoutError(f"handle_task() exceeded {self._HANDLE_TASK_TIMEOUT}s"),
708                    traceback_str="",
709                )
710                if msg.sender_id:
711                    await self.send(
712                        msg.sender_id,
713                        MessageType.RESULT,
714                        _with_corr(
715                            {
716                                "result": (
717                                    f"I gave up on that: it was still running after "
718                                    f"{self._HANDLE_TASK_TIMEOUT}s."
719                                ),
720                                "error": f"handle_task() timed out after {self._HANDLE_TASK_TIMEOUT}s",
721                                "error_phase": "handle_task",
722                                "agent": self.name,
723                            }
724                        ),
725                    )
726            except Exception as e:
727                tb = traceback.format_exc()
728                logger.exception("[%s] handle_task() error", self.name)
729                await self._publish_error(phase="handle_task", error=e, traceback_str=tb)
730                if msg.sender_id:
731                    await self.send(
732                        msg.sender_id,
733                        MessageType.RESULT,
734                        _with_corr(
735                            {
736                                # `result` so this reaches a person as a sentence:
737                                # a reply carrying none of the keys the chat reads
738                                # is printed as a Python repr.
739                                "result": f"That went wrong while I was handling it: {e}",
740                                "error": str(e),
741                                "error_phase": "handle_task",
742                                "agent": self.name,
743                            }
744                        ),
745                    )
746        else:
747            if msg.sender_id:
748                await self.send(
749                    msg.sender_id,
750                    MessageType.RESULT,
751                    _with_corr(
752                        {
753                            "result": (
754                                f"I cannot answer questions: {self.name} was written "
755                                f"without a handle_task, so there is nothing here to "
756                                f"take a request."
757                            ),
758                            "info": f"{self.name} has no handle_task defined",
759                        }
760                    ),
761                )
762        return None
763
764    async def _handle_task_message(self, msg: Message) -> Any:
765        """Run one task through the generated handle_task(), or explain why not."""
766        if msg.type == MessageType.TASK:
767            self.metrics.messages_processed += 1
768
769            # Correlation id for request/reply. main.delegate_task() and
770            # AgentAPI.send_to() tag the TASK with "_task_id" and then block on a
771            # future keyed by it; the reply MUST echo that id or the caller's
772            # future never resolves. Without this, recipe/dynamic agents (e.g.
773            # manual-agent) run handle_task and log everything but their RESULT
774            # is un-correlatable, so the user sees no response. LLMAgent already
775            # echoes it — this brings DynamicAgent to parity.
776            _incoming = msg.payload if isinstance(msg.payload, dict) else {}
777            _corr = _incoming.get("_task_id")
778
779            def _with_corr(r: Any) -> Any:
780                if _corr is None:
781                    return r
782                if isinstance(r, dict):
783                    return r if "_task_id" in r else {**r, "_task_id": _corr}
784                # non-dict result (str/number) — wrap so the id can ride along
785                return {"result": r, "_task_id": _corr}
786
787            return await self._invoke_handle_task(msg, _incoming, _corr, _with_corr)
788        return None
789
790    async def handle_message(self, msg: Message) -> Any:
791        if msg.type == MessageType.TASK:
792            # ``handle_task`` may await ``agent.send_to()``. Its RESULT must be
793            # consumed by this actor's mailbox, so keep that mailbox free while
794            # the generated handler is running.
795            if self._fn_handle_task:
796                task = asyncio.create_task(self._handle_task_message(msg))
797                self._tasks.append(task)
798                task.add_done_callback(
799                    lambda done: self._tasks.remove(done) if done in self._tasks else None
800                )
801                return None
802            return await self._handle_task_message(msg)
803        return None
804
805    async def _publish_error(
806        self,
807        phase: str,
808        error: Exception,
809        traceback_str: str = "",
810        fatal: bool = False,
811    ) -> None:
812        """Publish a structured error event to agents/{id}/errors AND send
813        a direct actor message to MonitorAgent so it works without MQTT.
814        """
815        self._consecutive_errors += 1
816        self._last_error_time = time.time()
817        self._error_phase = phase
818        severity = (
819            "critical" if fatal or self._consecutive_errors >= self._error_threshold else "warning"
820        )
821        event = {
822            "actor_id": self.actor_id,
823            "name": self.name,
824            "phase": phase,
825            "error": str(error),
826            "traceback": traceback_str[-1200:] if traceback_str else "",
827            "consecutive": self._consecutive_errors,
828            "fatal": fatal,
829            "severity": severity,
830            "degraded": self._consecutive_errors >= self._error_threshold,
831            "timestamp": time.time(),
832        }
833        await self._mqtt_publish(f"agents/{self.actor_id}/errors", event)
834        # Direct actor message to monitor (works without MQTT broker)
835        if self._registry:
836            monitor = self._registry.find_by_name("monitor")
837            if monitor and monitor.actor_id != self.actor_id:
838                try:
839                    await self.send(
840                        monitor.actor_id,
841                        MessageType.TASK,
842                        {
843                            **event,
844                            "_monitor_error_event": True,
845                        },
846                    )
847                except Exception as exc:
848                    logger.debug(
849                        "[%s] Could not publish the monitor error event: %s", self.name, exc
850                    )
851        # Mirror to /alert so the dashboard picks it up immediately
852        await self._mqtt_publish(
853            f"agents/{self.actor_id}/alert",
854            {
855                "actor_id": self.actor_id,
856                "name": self.name,
857                "message": f"[{phase}] {error}",
858                "severity": severity,
859                "timestamp": time.time(),
860            },
861        )
862
863    def _reset_error_count(self) -> None:
864        """Reset the process()/setup() error counter after a clean run.
865
866        Deliberately does NOT touch _cb_error_count / _cb_error_last — those
867        track subscribe callback errors which are independent of process().
868        A successful process() call doesn't mean the callback is fixed.
869        """
870        if self._consecutive_errors > 0:
871            logger.info("[%s] Recovered — resetting error counter.", self.name)
872            self._consecutive_errors = 0
873            self._error_phase = ""
874
875    def _persist_fixed_code(self, fixed_code: str) -> Any:
876        """Write the LLM-fixed code back to:
877          1. main's spawn registry  — so system restarts use the fixed code
878          2. Supervisor's factory   — so Supervisor-driven restarts use the fixed code
879
880        When the LLM fixes a runtime/syntax error it updates self._code in memory,
881        but both the spawn registry (on disk) and the Supervisor factory closure
882        (in memory) still reference the original broken code.  This method patches
883        both atomically the moment a fix is confirmed working.
884        """
885        try:
886            # ── 1. Persist to spawn registry (survives system restart) ─────
887            if self._registry:
888                main = find_main_actor(self._registry)
889                if main is not None:
890                    reg = main._get_spawn_registry()
891                    if self.name in reg:
892                        entry = dict(reg[self.name])
893                        if entry.get("code") != fixed_code:
894                            entry["code"] = fixed_code
895                            entry["_code_fixed_at"] = time.time()
896                            main._save_to_spawn_registry(entry)
897                            logger.info(
898                                "[%s] Fixed code written to spawn registry (%s chars).",
899                                self.name,
900                                len(fixed_code),
901                            )
902
903            # ── 2. Update Supervisor factory (survives Supervisor-driven restart) ─
904            # The factory closure captures the original kwargs including the old code.
905            # Replace it with a new closure that uses fixed_code so the next
906            # Supervisor restart spawns a working agent.
907            if self._registry and hasattr(self._registry, "_supervisor_ref"):
908                supervisor = self._registry._supervisor_ref
909                if supervisor is not None and self.name in supervisor._specs:
910                    spec = supervisor._specs[self.name]
911                    # Build a new factory that injects the fixed code
912                    _fixed = fixed_code
913                    _old_factory = spec.factory
914                    _name = self.name
915                    _mqtt_client = self._mqtt_client
916                    _mqtt_broker = self._mqtt_broker
917                    _mqtt_port = self._mqtt_port
918                    _registry = self._registry
919
920                    async def _fixed_factory(
921                        old_f: Any = _old_factory,
922                        code: Any = _fixed,
923                        mc: Any = _mqtt_client,
924                        mb: Any = _mqtt_broker,
925                        mp: Any = _mqtt_port,
926                    ) -> Any:
927                        # Call the original factory to get a correctly configured instance
928                        actor = await old_f() if inspect.iscoroutinefunction(old_f) else old_f()
929                        # Patch in the fixed code before the actor starts
930                        actor._code = code
931                        return actor
932
933                    spec.factory = _fixed_factory
934                    logger.info("[%s] Supervisor factory updated with fixed code.", self.name)
935
936        except Exception as exc:
937            logger.warning("[%s] Could not persist fixed code: %s", self.name, exc)
938
939    def get_status(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
940        s = super().get_status()
941        s["description"] = self.description
942        s["code"] = self._code
943        s["agent_type"] = "dynamic"
944        return s
945
946    def _build_heartbeat(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
947        hb = super()._build_heartbeat()
948        hb["code"] = self._code  # include code in every heartbeat
949        hb["description"] = self.description
950        hb["agent_type"] = "dynamic"
951        return hb
952
953    def _current_task_description(self) -> str:
954        return self.description or "running dynamic code"
955
956    def _accrue_usage(self, usage: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
957        if not isinstance(usage, dict):
958            return
959        self.total_input_tokens += usage.get("input_tokens", 0)
960        self.total_output_tokens += usage.get("output_tokens", 0)
961        self.total_cost_usd += usage.get("cost_usd", 0.0)
962        delta = self.total_cost_usd - self._last_period_cost_usd
963        if delta > 0:
964            accumulate_global_cost(delta)
965            self._last_period_cost_usd = self.total_cost_usd

Generic actor shell. Core behavior is provided as Python source code strings. The LLM writes setup/process/handle_task functions; this class runs them.

DynamicAgent( code: str, poll_interval: float = 1.0, description: str = '', input_schema: dict[str, typing.Any] | None = None, output_schema: dict[str, typing.Any] | None = None, llm_provider: Any = None, trusted: bool = False, **kwargs: Any) 
 49    def __init__(
 50        self,
 51        code: str,  # LLM-generated Python source
 52        poll_interval: float = 1.0,  # seconds between process() calls
 53        description: str = "",  # what this agent does
 54        input_schema: dict[str, Any] | None = None,  # expected task payload fields
 55        output_schema: dict[str, Any] | None = None,  # returned result fields
 56        llm_provider: Any = None,  # optional LLM for agent.llm.chat()
 57        trusted: bool = False,  # True = catalog agent, skip safety validator
 58        **kwargs: Any,
 59    ) -> None:
 60        super().__init__(**kwargs)
 61        self._code = code
 62        self.poll_interval = poll_interval
 63        self.description = description
 64        self.input_schema = input_schema or {}
 65        self.output_schema = output_schema or {}
 66        self._llm_provider = llm_provider
 67        self._trusted = trusted  # catalog agents bypass safety checks
 68
 69        # Compiled functions — populated in on_start
 70        self._fn_setup = None
 71        self._fn_process = None
 72        self._fn_handle_task = None
 73
 74        # Namespace shared across all calls (agent can store state here)
 75        self._ns: dict = {}
 76
 77        # Cost tracking (populated by LLMInterface if LLM is used)
 78        self.total_input_tokens = 0
 79        self.total_output_tokens = 0
 80        self.total_cost_usd = 0.0
 81        self._last_period_cost_usd = 0.0
 82
 83        # Error tracking for health classification
 84        self._consecutive_errors: int = 0
 85        self._error_threshold: int = 3  # DEGRADED after this many
 86        self._last_error_time: float = 0.0
 87        self._error_phase: str = ""  # compile|setup|process|handle_task
 88
 89        # Public API exposed to generated code via `agent` parameter
 90        # Owned here rather than grafted on by AgentAPI at first use: a
 91        # collaborator creating attributes on its host hides them from every
 92        # reader and from the type checker.
 93        #: Per-topic timestamp of the last callback error, for backoff.
 94        self._cb_error_last: dict[str, float] = {}
 95        #: Per-topic count of consecutive callback errors.
 96        self._cb_error_count: dict[str, int] = {}
 97        #: (topic, callback id) pairs already subscribed, to refuse duplicates.
 98        self._subscribed_topics: dict[tuple[str, int], Any] = {}
 99        #: The last contract this agent declared, published in its manifest.
100        self._topic_contract: Any = None
101        self._api = AgentAPI(self)

async def on_start(self) -> None: 
105    async def on_start(self) -> None:
106        # ── Compile with LLM self-correction on syntax errors ─────────────
107        current_code = self._code
108        error_msg = self._compile_code(current_code)
109
110        if error_msg:
111            for attempt in range(1, self._MAX_COMPILE_RETRIES + 1):
112                logger.warning("[%s] Compile error (attempt %s): %s", self.name, attempt, error_msg)
113                fixed = await self._fix_syntax_with_llm(current_code, error_msg)
114                if fixed is None:
115                    # LLM unavailable — no point retrying
116                    break
117                self._ns = {}  # fresh namespace for retry
118                new_err = self._compile_code(fixed)
119                if new_err is None:
120                    # Fix worked — update stored code so restarts use the good version
121                    self._code = fixed
122                    error_msg = None
123                    logger.info("[%s] Code fixed by LLM after %s attempt(s).", self.name, attempt)
124                    # ── Write fixed code back to spawn registry so restart uses it ──
125                    self._persist_fixed_code(fixed)
126                    await self._mqtt_publish(
127                        f"agents/{self.actor_id}/logs",
128                        {
129                            "type": "log",
130                            "message": f"Syntax error fixed by LLM after {attempt} attempt(s).",
131                            "timestamp": time.time(),
132                        },
133                    )
134                    break
135                # Fix compiled but still broken — feed it back for the next attempt
136                current_code = fixed
137                error_msg = new_err
138
139        if error_msg:
140            # All attempts exhausted — publish fatal and stop
141            err_exc = SyntaxError(error_msg)
142            logger.error("[%s] Code compilation failed permanently: %s", self.name, error_msg)
143            # ── Erlang/OTP: mark FAILED so Supervisor's watch_loop detects us ──
144            self.state = ActorState.FAILED
145            await self._publish_error(
146                phase="compile", error=err_exc, traceback_str=error_msg, fatal=True
147            )
148            return
149
150        # ── setup() ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
151        if self._fn_setup:
152            # Run setup as a background task so long-running loops (e.g. aiomqtt
153            # subscriptions) don't block on_start() and prevent heartbeats from firing.
154            self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._run_setup()))
155        else:
156            if self._fn_process:
157                self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._process_loop()))
158
159        # Publish manifest immediately so main's registry knows this agent exists
160        # even if it never calls publish() (pure handle_task agents, etc.)
161        await self._api._publish_manifest()

Called when actor starts. Override for init logic.

async def on_stop(self) -> None: 
207    async def on_stop(self) -> None:
208        # ── Persist final cost metrics so they survive agent deletion ──────
209        # Without this, cost data dies with the agent object and the UI
210        # can't show lifetime costs for deleted agents.
211        if hasattr(self, "total_cost_usd") and self.total_cost_usd > 0:
212            self.persist(
213                "_final_cost",
214                {
215                    "input_tokens": self.total_input_tokens,
216                    "output_tokens": self.total_output_tokens,
217                    "cost_usd": round(self.total_cost_usd, 6),
218                    "name": self.name,
219                    "stopped_at": time.time(),
220                },
221            )
222
223        await self._publish_final_metrics()
224
225        self._unregister_from_bus()
226
227        await self._run_generated_cleanup()
228
229        release_open_resources(self._api, self._ns, self.name)
230
231        # ── Cancel any tasks spawned inside setup/process code ─────────────
232        # Generated code may have called asyncio.create_task() directly without
233        # adding to _tasks. We can't track those, but we can ensure all tasks
234        # we DO track are properly cancelled and awaited.
235        for task in self._tasks:
236            if not task.done():
237                task.cancel()
238        # Give cancelled tasks a moment to actually stop
239        if self._tasks:
240            await asyncio.gather(*self._tasks, return_exceptions=True)

Called when actor stops. Override for cleanup.

class HomeAssistantActuatorAgent(wactorz.Actor): 
154class HomeAssistantActuatorAgent(Actor):
155    """Reactive actuator that subscribes to MQTT topics and calls HA services.
156
157    One instance per external automation.  Lifecycle:
158      on_start → open persistent HA WebSocket + subscribe to MQTT topics
159      detection → filter → cooldown → conditions → call_service × N
160      on_stop  → persist counters
161
162    Spawn via actor.spawn(HomeAssistantActuatorAgent, config=config).
163    """
164
165    def __init__(self, config: ActuatorConfig, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
166        kwargs.setdefault("name", f"actuator-{config.automation_id[:20]}")
167        super().__init__(**kwargs)
168
169        self.config = config
170        self.ha_url = (CONFIG.ha_url or "").rstrip("/")
171        self.ha_token = (CONFIG.ha_token or "").strip()
172        self.ha_ws_url = normalize_ha_ws_url(self.ha_url)
173
174        self._ha: HAWebSocketClient | None = None
175        self._ws_ready: asyncio.Event = asyncio.Event()  # set when HA WS is connected
176        self._last_actuation_time: float = 0.0
177        self._actuations_count: int = 0
178
179    # ── Lifecycle ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
180
181    async def on_start(self) -> None:
182        self._last_actuation_time = float(self.recall("last_actuation_time", 0.0))
183        self._actuations_count = int(self.recall("actuations_count", 0))
184        self.persist("config", self.config.to_dict())
185
186        await self.publish_manifest(
187            description=self.config.description or f"Actuator for {self.config.automation_id}",
188            capabilities=["ha_actuator"],
189            input_schema={"payload": "dict — detection event from sensor agent"},
190        )
191
192        self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._ws_keepalive()))
193        self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._mqtt_listener()))
194
195        logger.info(
196            "[%s] started — topics=%r actions=%d conditions=%d",
197            self.name,
198            self.config.mqtt_topics,
199            len(self.config.actions),
200            len(self.config.conditions),
201        )
202
203    async def on_stop(self) -> None:
204        self.persist("last_actuation_time", self._last_actuation_time)
205        self.persist("actuations_count", self._actuations_count)
206
207    # ── HA WebSocket keepalive ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
208
209    async def _ws_keepalive(self) -> None:
210        """Maintain a persistent HA WebSocket connection for service calls and state checks."""
211        if not self.ha_ws_url or not self.ha_token:
212            logger.warning(
213                "[%s] HA URL/token not configured — conditions will be skipped", self.name
214            )
215            return
216
217        while self.state not in (ActorState.STOPPED, ActorState.FAILED):
218            try:
219                async with HAWebSocketClient(self.ha_ws_url, self.ha_token) as ha:
220                    self._ha = ha
221                    self._ws_ready.set()
222                    logger.info("[%s] HA WebSocket connected", self.name)
223                    # Hold the connection open until the actor stops or the WS drops
224                    while self.state not in (ActorState.STOPPED, ActorState.FAILED):
225                        await asyncio.sleep(30)
226            except asyncio.CancelledError:
227                break
228            except Exception as exc:
229                self._ha = None
230                self._ws_ready.clear()
231                logger.warning("[%s] HA WebSocket error: %s — reconnecting in 5s", self.name, exc)
232                if self.state not in (ActorState.STOPPED, ActorState.FAILED):
233                    await asyncio.sleep(5)
234        self._ha = None
235
236    # ── MQTT listener ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
237
238    async def _mqtt_listener(self) -> None:
239        """Subscribe to configured MQTT topics and dispatch each message."""
240        try:
241            import aiomqtt  # noqa: F401
242        except ImportError:
243            logger.error("[%s] aiomqtt not installed — MQTT listener disabled", self.name)
244            return
245
246        while self.state not in (ActorState.STOPPED, ActorState.FAILED):
247            try:
248                async with mqtt_client(self._mqtt_broker, self._mqtt_port) as client:
249                    for topic in self.config.mqtt_topics:
250                        await client.subscribe(topic)
251                    logger.info("[%s] subscribed to %r", self.name, self.config.mqtt_topics)
252
253                    async for message in client.messages:
254                        if self.state in (ActorState.STOPPED, ActorState.FAILED):
255                            break
256                        try:
257                            import json
258
259                            payload = json.loads(message.payload.decode())
260                            await self._on_detection(payload)
261                        except Exception as exc:
262                            logger.error("[%s] Failed to process message: %s", self.name, exc)
263
264            except asyncio.CancelledError:
265                break
266            except Exception as exc:
267                if self.state not in (ActorState.STOPPED, ActorState.FAILED):
268                    logger.warning(
269                        "[%s] MQTT listener error: %s — reconnecting in 5s", self.name, exc
270                    )
271                    await asyncio.sleep(5)
272
273    # ── Detection processing ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
274
275    async def _on_detection(self, payload: dict) -> None:
276        """Process one incoming MQTT message through filter → cooldown → conditions → actions."""
277        if not self._matches_filter(payload):
278            return
279
280        now = time.time()
281        if now - self._last_actuation_time < self.config.cooldown_seconds:
282            logger.debug("[%s] Cooldown active — skipping", self.name)
283            return
284
285        if not await self._all_conditions_met():
286            logger.debug("[%s] Conditions not met — skipping", self.name)
287            return
288
289        for action in self.config.actions:
290            await self._call_service(action)
291
292        self._last_actuation_time = now
293        self._actuations_count += 1
294        self.metrics.tasks_completed += 1
295
296        await self._mqtt_publish(
297            f"agents/{self.actor_id}/actuations",
298            {
299                "automation_id": self.config.automation_id,
300                "actions": [a.to_dict() for a in self.config.actions],
301                "timestamp": now,
302                "trigger_payload": payload,
303            },
304        )
305
306    def _matches_filter(self, payload: dict) -> bool:
307        """Return True if all detection_filter entries match the payload.
308
309        Values can be literals (equality) or operator dicts e.g. {"gt": 0.8}.
310        Supported operators: eq, ne, gt, lt, gte, lte.
311        """
312        if not self.config.detection_filter:
313            return True
314        for key, expected in self.config.detection_filter.items():
315            actual = payload.get(key)
316            if isinstance(expected, dict):
317                op_name, op_val = next(iter(expected.items()))
318                cmp = _OPERATORS.get(op_name)
319                if cmp is None or actual is None:
320                    return False
321                try:
322                    if not cmp(actual, op_val):
323                        return False
324                except TypeError:
325                    return False
326            else:
327                if actual != expected:
328                    return False
329        return True
330
331    async def _all_conditions_met(self) -> bool:
332        """Return True if all ActuatorConditions pass (AND logic)."""
333        if not self.config.conditions:
334            return True
335        if self._ha is None:
336            logger.warning(
337                "[%s] No HA connection — skipping condition checks (fail-open)", self.name
338            )
339            return True
340
341        for condition in self.config.conditions:
342            try:
343                entity_state = await self._ha.get_entity_state(condition.entity_id)
344                if entity_state is None:
345                    logger.warning(
346                        "[%s] Entity %r not found — condition fails", self.name, condition.entity_id
347                    )
348                    return False
349                if not condition.evaluate(entity_state):
350                    return False
351            except Exception as exc:
352                logger.error(
353                    "[%s] Condition check error for %r: %s", self.name, condition.entity_id, exc
354                )
355                return False
356
357        return True
358
359    async def _call_service(self, action: ActuatorAction) -> None:
360        """Call a HA service via the persistent WebSocket connection.
361        Waits up to 10 seconds for the connection to be ready before giving up.
362        """
363        if self._ha is None:
364            try:
365                await asyncio.wait_for(self._ws_ready.wait(), timeout=10.0)
366            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
367                logger.error(
368                    "[%s] No HA connection after 10s — cannot call service %s.%s",
369                    self.name,
370                    action.domain,
371                    action.service,
372                )
373                return
374        ha = self._ha
375        if ha is None:
376            # Re-read after the wait rather than trusting it: the event only
377            # says the connection attempt finished, and it can fire before the
378            # client is assigned. Nothing checked this, so that race crashed.
379            logger.error(
380                "[%s] HA connection signalled ready but is not available — "
381                "cannot call service %s.%s",
382                self.name,
383                action.domain,
384                action.service,
385            )
386            return
387        try:
388            await ha.call_service(
389                action.domain,
390                action.service,
391                action.entity_id,
392                **action.service_data,
393            )
394            logger.info(
395                "[%s] Called %s.%s on %s (data=%r)",
396                self.name,
397                action.domain,
398                action.service,
399                action.entity_id,
400                action.service_data,
401            )
402        except Exception as exc:
403            logger.error("[%s] Service call failed: %s", self.name, exc)
404            self.metrics.tasks_failed += 1
405
406    # ── Actor overrides ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
407
408    def _spoken_status(self) -> str:
409        """What this agent is, said to whoever just asked it something.
410
411        There is no conversation here: it waits on a topic and calls a service.
412        Saying so is more use than answering with the state of the automation,
413        which is what a question used to get -- the same state whatever was
414        asked, because the question was never read.
415        """
416        topics = ", ".join(self.config.mqtt_topics) or "no topic"
417        if self._actuations_count:
418            when = time.strftime("%H:%M", time.localtime(self._last_actuation_time))
419            how_often = "once" if self._actuations_count == 1 else f"{self._actuations_count} times"
420            fired = f"It has fired {how_often}, most recently at {when}."
421        else:
422            fired = "It has not fired yet."
423        reachable = (
424            "Home Assistant is reachable."
425            if self._ha is not None
426            else "Home Assistant is not connected, so it cannot act right now."
427        )
428        return (
429            f"I cannot answer questions. I act when a topic fires: "
430            f"{self.config.description} I am watching {topics}. {fired} {reachable}"
431        )
432
433    async def handle_message(self, msg: Message) -> None:
434        if msg.type != MessageType.TASK:
435            return
436        # `result` first, and it is not decoration: the chat surface reads a
437        # reply by looking for reply/message/text/content/result and printing
438        # `str(payload)` when it finds none. Without it this dict reached people
439        # as a Python repr. The structured fields stay for callers that delegate
440        # here and read them.
441        status = {
442            "result": self._spoken_status(),
443            "automation_id": self.config.automation_id,
444            "description": self.config.description,
445            "mqtt_topics": self.config.mqtt_topics,
446            "actuations_count": self._actuations_count,
447            "last_actuation_time": self._last_actuation_time,
448            "ha_connected": self._ha is not None,
449        }
450        if msg.sender_id:
451            await self.send(msg.sender_id, MessageType.RESULT, status)
452
453    def _current_task_description(self) -> str:
454        topics = ", ".join(self.config.mqtt_topics)
455        return f"listening on [{topics}] ({self._actuations_count} actuations)"

Reactive actuator that subscribes to MQTT topics and calls HA services.

One instance per external automation. Lifecycle: on_start → open persistent HA WebSocket + subscribe to MQTT topics detection → filter → cooldown → conditions → call_service × N on_stop → persist counters
