class MainActor(wactorz.LLMAgent, wactorz.agents.mixins.spawning.SpawnMixin, wactorz.agents.main.memory.MemoryMixin, wactorz.agents.main.routing.RoutingMixin, wactorz.agents.main.planning.PlanningMixin): 
 112class MainActor(LLMAgent, SpawnMixin, MemoryMixin, RoutingMixin, PlanningMixin):
 113    DESCRIPTION = "Main orchestrator: spawns agents, routes tasks, manages the multi-agent system"
 114    CAPABILITIES: ClassVar[list[str]] = [
 115        "spawn_agent",
 116        "list_agents",
 117        "list_nodes",
 118        "list_topics",
 119        "orchestration",
 120    ]
 121
 122    #: Most queued system notices to carry. They are prepended to the next chat
 123    #: reply, so the newest are what matter and a long backlog would bury the
 124    #: answer itself. Oldest are dropped first.
 125    MAX_PENDING_NOTIFICATIONS = 50
 126
 127    def __init__(
 128        self,
 129        llm_provider: LLMProvider | None = None,
 130        **kwargs: Any,
 131    ) -> None:
 132        kwargs.setdefault("name", "main")
 133        kwargs.setdefault("system_prompt", ORCHESTRATOR_PROMPT)
 134        super().__init__(llm_provider=llm_provider, **kwargs)
 135        self._result_futures: dict[str, asyncio.Future] = {}
 136        # Queued monitor notifications — prepended to next user response, and
 137        # capped at MAX_PENDING_NOTIFICATIONS: they drain only when someone
 138        # chats, so on an idle system with a failing agent nothing empties them.
 139        self._pending_notifications: list[dict] = []
 140        self.protected = True
 141        # Stopping main leaves chat unanswered, which is the surface a user
 142        # would reach for to start it again.
 143        self.essential = True
 144        # Remote node tracking: node_name → {"last_seen": float, "agents": [...]}
 145        self.manifests = ManifestRegistry(self)
 146        self.nodes = NodeManager(self, self.manifests)
 147        self.migration = Migration(self, self.nodes)
 148        self.llm_bridge = LLMBridge(self)
 149        self.spawns = SpawnService(self)
 150        self.delegation = DelegationManager(self)
 151        self.lifecycle = LifecycleService(self)
 152
 153    def _current_interface_source(self) -> str:
 154        """Return the task-local interface excluded from delegation this turn."""
 155        return _INTERFACE_SOURCE.get()
 156
 157    def _current_interface_history(self) -> tuple[dict, ...]:
 158        """Return recent structured turns supplied by the active interface."""
 159        return _INTERFACE_HISTORY.get()
 160
 161    def _current_interface_is_voice(self) -> bool:
 162        """Return whether the active interface used speech recognition."""
 163        return bool(_INTERFACE_VOICE.get())
 164
 165    def _current_interface_context(self) -> dict:
 166        """Return the sanitized capabilities of the active interface."""
 167        return dict(_INTERFACE_CONTEXT.get() or {})
 168
 169    def _is_interface_source(self, agent_name: str) -> bool:
 170        """Return whether an agent name resolves to the active interface."""
 171        source = self._current_interface_source()
 172        return bool(source) and _normalize_agent_name(agent_name) == _normalize_agent_name(source)
 173
 174    @staticmethod
 175    def _sanitize_interface_context(raw_context: Any, source: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
 176        """Keep bounded display metadata and explicit action allow-lists."""
 177        if not isinstance(raw_context, dict):
 178            return {}
 179        display_name = str(raw_context.get("display_name") or source or "interface")[:80]
 180        kind = str(raw_context.get("kind") or "interface")[:80]
 181        capabilities: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {}
 182        raw_capabilities = raw_context.get("capabilities")
 183        if isinstance(raw_capabilities, dict):
 184            for raw_command, raw_options in list(raw_capabilities.items())[:12]:
 185                command = str(raw_command).strip().lower()
 186                if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}", command):
 187                    continue
 188                if not isinstance(raw_options, (list, tuple)):
 189                    continue
 190                options = []
 191                for raw_option in list(raw_options)[:20]:
 192                    option = str(raw_option).strip().lower()
 193                    if re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}", option):
 194                        options.append(option)
 195                if options:
 196                    capabilities[command] = tuple(dict.fromkeys(options))
 197        prompt_note = " ".join(str(raw_context.get("prompt_note") or "").split())[:400]
 198        if prompt_note and not prompt_note.endswith(" "):
 199            prompt_note += " "
 200        return {
 201            "display_name": display_name,
 202            "kind": kind,
 203            "capabilities": capabilities,
 204            "prompt_note": prompt_note,
 205        }
 206
 207    def _extract_interface_actions(self, response: str) -> tuple[str, list[dict[str, str]]]:
 208        """Remove action blocks and validate them against the interface allow-list."""
 209        capabilities = self._current_interface_context().get("capabilities") or {}
 210        actions: list[dict[str, str]] = []
 211        for match in _INTERFACE_ACTION_RE.finditer(str(response or "")):
 212            if len(actions) >= 3:
 213                break
 214            try:
 215                candidate = json.loads(match.group(1))
 216            except json.JSONDecodeError:
 217                continue
 218            if not isinstance(candidate, dict):
 219                continue
 220            command = str(candidate.get("cmd") or candidate.get("action") or "").lower()
 221            name = str(candidate.get("name") or "").lower()
 222            if command and name and name in capabilities.get(command, ()):
 223                actions.append({"cmd": command, "name": name})
 224        clean = _INTERFACE_ACTION_RE.sub("", str(response or ""))
 225        return re.sub(r"\n{3,}", "\n\n", clean).strip(), actions
 226
 227    def _replace_latest_interface_reply(self, raw_reply: str, clean_reply: str) -> None:
 228        """Keep interface protocol blocks out of durable conversation history."""
 229        if raw_reply == clean_reply:
 230            return
 231        for item in reversed(self._conversation_history):
 232            if item.get("role") == "assistant" and item.get("content") == raw_reply:
 233                item["content"] = clean_reply
 234                self.persist("conversation_history", self._conversation_history)
 235                return
 236
 237    # ── Lifecycle ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 238
 239    async def on_start(self) -> None:
 240        await super().on_start()
 241        await self._restore_spawned_agents()
 242        # Listen for remote node heartbeats so we know what's online
 243        self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._node_heartbeat_listener()))
 244        # Detect nodes that go silent and clean up their agents
 245        self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._node_offline_watcher()))
 246        # Listen for agent capability manifests to build topic registry
 247        self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._manifest_listener()))
 248        # LLM bridge — lets remote agents call agent.ask_llm() / agent.chat()
 249        self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._llm_bridge_listener()))
 250        # Observe real MQTT payloads from remote agents to populate observed_samples
 251        self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._remote_observed_samples_listener()))
 252        # Receive state + config from remote nodes during remote→local migration
 253        self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._state_return_listener()))
 254        # Inject persisted user facts into system prompt
 255        self._inject_user_facts_into_prompt()
 256
 257    # ── Spawn registry ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 258
 259    def _get_spawn_registry(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
 260        return self.spawns._get_spawn_registry()
 261
 262    def _restore_earned_trust(self, agent_name: str, local_cfg: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
 263        """Re-attach a migrating agent's ``trusted`` flag from our own registry.
 264
 265        A config coming back from a node arrives over MQTT, where a publisher
 266        can claim anything, so it is not evidence of anything. Our registry
 267        entry is: it was written here when the agent was sent out. Reading the
 268        flag from that record rather than from the wire is what lets a catalog
 269        agent migrate home without meeting a validator its recipe was never
 270        written to pass, while a node's claim of trust still buys nothing.
 271
 272        Returns whether the flag was earned, for the caller to pass as
 273        ``from_registry``. A claim that was not earned is left in place rather
 274        than removed here, so the spawn path strips it and says so.
 275        """
 276        if not self._get_spawn_registry().get(agent_name, {}).get("trusted"):
 277            return False
 278        local_cfg["trusted"] = True
 279        return True
 280
 281    def _save_to_spawn_registry(self, config: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
 282        self.spawns._save_to_spawn_registry(config)
 283
 284    def _remove_from_spawn_registry(self, name: str) -> None:
 285        self.spawns._remove_from_spawn_registry(name)
 286
 287    async def _clear_agent_manifest(self, name: str, actor_id: str | None = None) -> None:
 288        await self.lifecycle._clear_agent_manifest(name, actor_id)
 289
 290    def _record_agent_deletion(self, name: str, reason: str = "user request") -> None:
 291        self.lifecycle._record_agent_deletion(name, reason)
 292
 293    def get_notification_urls(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
 294        """Return persisted notification webhook URLs (discord, telegram, slack, etc.)"""
 295        return self.recall("_notification_urls") or {}
 296
 297    # ── User facts ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 298    # Key facts extracted from conversation: HA URL, entity names, preferences,
 299    # user name, webhook URLs, etc. Stored separately from history so they
 300    # survive summarization and persist indefinitely.
 301
 302    async def _restore_spawned_agents(self) -> None:
 303        await self.spawns._restore_spawned_agents()
 304
 305    # ── Message handling ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
 306
 307    async def handle_message(self, msg: Message) -> None:
 308        if msg.type == MessageType.TASK:
 309            # Intercept monitor notifications BEFORE passing to LLM _handle_task
 310            if isinstance(msg.payload, dict) and msg.payload.get("_monitor_notification"):
 311                self._queue_notification(msg.payload)
 312                logger.info(
 313                    "[%s] Monitor alert queued: %s", self.name, msg.payload.get("message", "")[:80]
 314                )
 315                return
 316            await self._handle_task(msg)
 317
 318    async def _handle_task(self, msg: Message) -> None:
 319        """Route interface tasks through the full orchestrator without blocking replies."""
 320        payload = msg.payload if isinstance(msg.payload, dict) else {}
 321        if payload.get("_via_interface"):
 322            task = asyncio.create_task(self._handle_interface_request(payload, msg))
 323            self._tasks.append(task)
 324            task.add_done_callback(
 325                lambda done: self._tasks.remove(done) if done in self._tasks else None
 326            )
 327            return
 328        await super()._handle_task(msg)
 329
 330    async def _handle_interface_request(self, payload: dict[str, Any], msg: Message) -> None:
 331        """Process one interface turn and reply on its correlation address."""
 332        text = str(
 333            payload.get("text")
 334            or payload.get("message")
 335            or payload.get("query")
 336            or payload.get("task")
 337            or ""
 338        ).strip()
 339        task_id = payload.get("_task_id")
 340        reply_to = payload.get("_reply_to") or msg.reply_to or msg.sender_id
 341        history = []
 342        raw_history = payload.get("_interface_history")
 343        if isinstance(raw_history, list):
 344            for item in raw_history[-4:]:
 345                if not isinstance(item, dict):
 346                    continue
 347                transcript = str(item.get("transcript") or "").strip()
 348                response = str(item.get("response") or "").strip()
 349                if transcript or response:
 350                    history.append({"transcript": transcript[:1000], "response": response[:2000]})
 351        source_value = str(payload.get("_interface_source") or "")
 352        interface_context = self._sanitize_interface_context(
 353            payload.get("_interface_context"), source_value
 354        )
 355        source_token = _INTERFACE_SOURCE.set(source_value)
 356        history_token = _INTERFACE_HISTORY.set(tuple(history))
 357        voice_token = _INTERFACE_VOICE.set(bool(payload.get("_interface_voice")))
 358        context_token = _INTERFACE_CONTEXT.set(interface_context)
 359        source = self._current_interface_source()
 360        logger.info("[%s] interface request from %s: %r", self.name, source or "unknown", text[:80])
 361        try:
 362            try:
 363                reply = await self.process_user_input(text) if text else ""
 364                clean_reply, interface_actions = self._extract_interface_actions(reply)
 365                if interface_actions and not clean_reply:
 366                    clean_reply = "Okay."
 367                self._replace_latest_interface_reply(reply, clean_reply)
 368                reply = clean_reply
 369            except Exception as exc:
 370                logger.warning("[%s] interface request failed: %s", self.name, exc)
 371                reply = f"[error] {exc}"
 372                interface_actions = []
 373        finally:
 374            _INTERFACE_CONTEXT.reset(context_token)
 375            _INTERFACE_VOICE.reset(voice_token)
 376            _INTERFACE_HISTORY.reset(history_token)
 377            _INTERFACE_SOURCE.reset(source_token)
 378        if reply_to:
 379            result: dict[str, Any] = {
 380                "text": reply,
 381                "result": reply,
 382                "task": text,
 383                "agent": "main",
 384                "interface_actions": interface_actions,
 385                "interface_display_name": interface_context.get("display_name", source),
 386            }
 387            if task_id:
 388                result["_task_id"] = task_id
 389            await self.send(reply_to, MessageType.RESULT, result)
 390
 391    # ── User input ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 392
 393    async def chat(self, user_message: str, attachments: list[dict] | None = None) -> str:
 394        response = await super().chat(user_message, attachments)
 395        # Fire-and-forget fact extraction — strip auto-injected context first
 396        clean_msg = _strip_live_context(user_message)
 397        asyncio.create_task(self._extract_and_save_facts(clean_msg, response))
 398        return response
 399
 400    async def chat_stream(
 401        self, user_message: str, attachments: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None
 402    ) -> AsyncGenerator[str | dict[str, Any]]:
 403        full_response = []
 404        got_usage = False
 405        async for chunk in super().chat_stream(user_message, attachments):
 406            if isinstance(chunk, dict):
 407                got_usage = True
 408                yield chunk
 409            else:
 410                full_response.append(chunk)
 411                yield chunk
 412        # Only extract facts when a real LLM response was received (usage dict present).
 413        # Skips early-exit cases like cost-limit errors so no extra LLM call is made.
 414        if full_response and got_usage:
 415            clean_msg = _strip_live_context(user_message)
 416            asyncio.create_task(self._extract_and_save_facts(clean_msg, "".join(full_response)))
 417
 418    async def _record_external_exchange(self, user_message: str, assistant_response: str) -> None:
 419        """Record a turn that was handled OUTSIDE self.chat() / self.chat_stream() —
 420        i.e. by the HA, ACTUATE, or PIPELINE branches that return before the LLM
 421        is called on main. Without this, those exchanges vanish from history and
 422        future turns have no memory of them.
 423
 424        Mirrors what LLMAgent.chat() does for OTHER turns:
 425          - append user + assistant to _conversation_history
 426          - run rolling summarization if needed
 427          - persist history to disk
 428          - trigger fact extraction
 429        """
 430        if not user_message or assistant_response is None:
 431            return
 432        try:
 433            self.metrics.messages_processed += 1
 434            self._conversation_history.append({"role": "user", "content": user_message})
 435            self._conversation_history.append(
 436                {"role": "assistant", "content": str(assistant_response)}
 437            )
 438            # Same summarization + persistence path that LLMAgent.chat() uses
 439            await self._maybe_summarize()
 440            self.persist("conversation_history", self._conversation_history)
 441        except Exception as e:
 442            logger.warning("[%s] Failed to record external exchange: %s", self.name, e)
 443        # Fire-and-forget fact extraction — same as chat()
 444        asyncio.create_task(self._extract_and_save_facts(user_message, str(assistant_response)))
 445
 446    def _queue_notification(self, notice: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
 447        """Queue a system notice for the next chat reply, keeping the newest.
 448
 449        The queue drains only when someone chats, so an idle system with a
 450        failing agent has nothing emptying it. Dropping from the front keeps
 451        the most recent notices, which are the ones still worth reading.
 452        """
 453        self._pending_notifications.append(notice)
 454        excess = len(self._pending_notifications) - self.MAX_PENDING_NOTIFICATIONS
 455        if excess > 0:
 456            del self._pending_notifications[:excess]
 457
 458    def _drain_notifications(self) -> str:
 459        """Pop queued monitor notifications as a formatted prefix string."""
 460        if not self._pending_notifications:
 461            return ""
 462        icons = {"critical": "\U0001f534", "warning": "\U0001f7e1", "info": "\u2705"}
 463        lines = []
 464        for n in self._pending_notifications:
 465            icon = icons.get(n.get("severity", "warning"), "\u26a0\ufe0f")
 466            lines.append(f"{icon} **System:** {n.get('message', '').strip()}")
 467        self._pending_notifications.clear()
 468        return "\n".join(lines) + "\n\n---\n\n"
 469
 470    def _restore_unprefixed_turn(self, prefixed_text: str, text: str) -> None:
 471        """Put the user's own words back into history after the model saw more.
 472
 473        The model is given the live agent list ahead of the message, because it
 474        trusts what is in the message over what is in the system prompt. History
 475        keeps what was actually typed: left prefixed, every turn would carry the
 476        agent list of the moment it was sent, and the context window would fill
 477        with stale copies of it.
 478
 479        Searched from the end because that is where this turn is, and only the
 480        first match is replaced — the same question asked twice should not have
 481        its earlier answer rewritten.
 482        """
 483        for entry in reversed(self._conversation_history):
 484            if entry.get("role") == "user" and entry.get("content") == prefixed_text:
 485                entry["content"] = text
 486                break
 487        self.persist("conversation_history", self._conversation_history)
 488
 489    async def process_user_input(self, text: str) -> str:
 490        note_prefix = self._drain_notifications()
 491
 492        # ── Pending-plan response detection ─────────────────────────────────
 493        # If there's a dry-run plan waiting for approval and the user's message
 494        # looks like "yes"/"no", handle it BEFORE any other processing. This
 495        # must come first so a bare "yes" doesn't accidentally hit the intent
 496        # classifier or get treated as a new prompt. Slash commands and other
 497        # explicit prefixes are NOT intercepted (the user might want to inspect
 498        # /plans or /registry while a plan is pending).
 499        if not text.strip().startswith("/") and not text.strip().startswith("@"):
 500            plan_response = await self._handle_pending_plan_response(text)
 501            if plan_response is not None:
 502                # Record the exchange so history reflects the approval/rejection
 503                await self._record_external_exchange(text, plan_response)
 504                return note_prefix + plan_response
 505
 506            # Pending-plan ambiguity guard: if the user has a plan pending
 507            # and now types something that looks like another spawn / pipeline
 508            # request, we'd otherwise silently create the new agents AND
 509            # later spawn the pending ones too — duplicates galore. Warn
 510            # the user and ask them to resolve the pending plan first.
 511            warn = self._warn_if_pending_plan_collision(text)
 512            if warn:
 513                await self._record_external_exchange(text, warn)
 514                return note_prefix + warn
 515
 516        # ── Direct API intercepts — handle without LLM round-trip ──────────
 517        stripped = text.strip().rstrip("()")
 518
 519        # ── Commands ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 520        # Every command lives in the registry; registration order is dispatch
 521        # order, so a command answers where the chain this replaced answered it.
 522        found = command_registry.find(stripped)
 523        if found is not None:
 524            handler, argument = found[0].handler, found[1]
 525            return note_prefix + await handler(CommandContext(actor=self), argument)
 526
 527        # ── Webhook / notification URL management ───────────────────────────
 528
 529        # Auto-detect webhook URLs in any message and persist them
 530        _webhook_match = re.search(
 531            r"https?://(?:discord\.com/api/webhooks|hooks\.slack\.com|api\.telegram\.org)/\S+", text
 532        )
 533        if _webhook_match:
 534            url = _webhook_match.group(0).rstrip(".,;!)'\"")
 535            urls = self.recall("_notification_urls") or {}
 536            if "discord" in url:
 537                urls["discord"] = url
 538            elif "slack" in url:
 539                urls["slack"] = url
 540            elif "telegram" in url:
 541                urls["telegram"] = url
 542            self.persist("_notification_urls", urls)
 543            logger.info("[%s] Auto-saved webhook URL from message", self.name)
 544
 545        # ── @mention direct routing ─────────────────────────────────────────
 546        if text.startswith("@"):
 547            return note_prefix + await self.delegation.route_mention(text)
 548
 549        # Explicit planner prefix always wins
 550        lowered = text.lower()
 551        if any(lowered.startswith(p) for p in PLANNER_PREFIXES):
 552            result = await self._run_planner(text)
 553            response = result or "Planner did not return a result. Please retry."
 554            await self._record_external_exchange(text, response)
 555            return note_prefix + response
 556
 557        # Single LLM call classifies intent: ACTUATE, HA, PIPELINE (reactive rule), OTHER
 558        intent = await self._classify_intent(text)
 559        logger.info("[%s] Intent: %s — %s", self.name, intent, text[:60])
 560
 561        if intent == "PIPELINE":
 562            response = await self._propose_or_execute_pipeline(text)
 563            await self._record_external_exchange(text, response)
 564            return note_prefix + response
 565
 566        if intent == "ACTUATE":
 567            response = await self._handle_actuate_intent(text)
 568            await self._record_external_exchange(text, response)
 569            return note_prefix + response
 570
 571        if intent == "HA":
 572            response = await self.delegation.ask_home_assistant(text)
 573            await self._record_external_exchange(text, response)
 574            return note_prefix + response
 575
 576        # Refresh the system prompt with live registry + facts before any LLM call.
 577        # This ensures the LLM never answers from a stale view of which agents exist.
 578        self._rebuild_system_prompt()
 579
 580        # Belt-and-braces: also inject the live agent list as a prefix on the
 581        # user message itself. Models trust in-message context over system-prompt
 582        # claims, so this is the strongest signal we can give without using a tool.
 583        # We send the prefixed text to the LLM but replace it with the clean
 584        # original in conversation history afterward — otherwise stale prefixes
 585        # would accumulate across turns and bloat the context window.
 586        prefixed_text = self._prefix_with_live_context(text)
 587        response = await self.chat(prefixed_text)
 588        # Find the most recent user message in history that matches the prefixed
 589        # text and replace it with the user's original. The assistant turn after
 590        # it remains unchanged.
 591        self._restore_unprefixed_turn(prefixed_text, text)
 592
 593        # If the LLM wrote agent code but forgot the <spawn> wrapper, remind it once
 594        has_spawn = "<spawn>" in response
 595        has_code = "async def handle_task" in response or "async def setup" in response
 596        asked_spawn = any(
 597            w in text.lower() for w in ("spawn", "create", "make", "build", "add", "agent")
 598        )
 599        if has_code and not has_spawn and asked_spawn:
 600            logger.info("[%s] Code written without <spawn> — prompting to wrap it", self.name)
 601            response = await self.chat(
 602                "You wrote agent code but forgot to wrap it in a <spawn> block. "
 603                "Please output the complete spawn block now with that exact code inside it. "
 604                "Output ONLY the <spawn>...</spawn> block, nothing else."
 605            )
 606
 607        clean, spawned = await self._process_spawn_commands(response)
 608
 609        # Process any <delete>{"name": "..."}</delete> blocks the LLM produced.
 610        # This is the orchestrator-side counterpart of <spawn> — lets the LLM
 611        # remove agents in response to user requests like "delete the math agent".
 612        clean, deleted, missing = await self._process_delete_commands(clean)
 613
 614        # Execute structured <delegate>{...}</delegate> blocks — the preferred,
 615        # unambiguous delegation form. Results are spliced in-place.
 616        clean, _delegate_results = await self._process_delegate_commands(clean)
 617
 618        # Execute any looser @agent-name delegation patterns the LLM produced
 619        clean = await self._execute_llm_delegations(clean)
 620
 621        await self._mqtt_publish(
 622            f"agents/{self.actor_id}/logs",
 623            {"type": "user_interaction", "input": text[:100], "response": clean[:200]},
 624        )
 625
 626        summary = TurnActions(tuple(spawned), tuple(deleted), tuple(missing)).summary(response)
 627        if summary:
 628            clean += f"\n\n[System: {summary}]"
 629
 630        return note_prefix + clean
 631
 632    # Delegation allow-list for social channels. A deny-list won't hold: any
 633    # DynamicAgent or code-agent runs code, so delegating to one launders code
 634    # execution. Allow only bounded native agents; fail closed.
 635
 636    @staticmethod
 637    def _neutralize_action_blocks(response: str) -> tuple[str, bool]:
 638        """Strip <spawn>/<delete> blocks without running them; return (cleaned, had_any)."""
 639        had = bool(re.search(r"<(spawn|delete)>", response))
 640        cleaned = re.sub(r"<spawn>.*?</spawn>", "", response, flags=re.DOTALL)
 641        cleaned = re.sub(r"<delete>.*?</delete>", "", cleaned, flags=re.DOTALL)
 642        return cleaned.strip(), had
 643
 644    async def process_user_input_restricted(self, text: str) -> str:
 645        """Social-channel (Discord/Telegram) entry point — the untrusted-surface
 646        counterpart of process_user_input.
 647
 648        Conversation, device control (ACTUATE), and HA queries only. Spawning,
 649        deleting, code, pipelines, admin commands, and delegation to
 650        non-allowlisted agents are blocked — at the action, not by classifying
 651        the text, so it can't be talked around.
 652        """
 653        note_prefix = self._drain_notifications()
 654        stripped = text.strip()
 655
 656        # Slash commands and the bypass markers are the admin surface — not
 657        # exposed here. Every marker the planner honours is refused, not just
 658        # the first: a guard that catches one spelling of a family reads as
 659        # covering the family.
 660        if stripped.startswith("/") or starts_with_bypass(stripped):
 661            reply = (
 662                "Admin commands aren't available on this channel — just talk to me "
 663                "normally. I can answer questions, tell you what's going on, and "
 664                "control your devices. (Spawning, deleting, and running code stay "
 665                "on the dashboard.)"
 666            )
 667            await self._record_external_exchange(text, reply)
 668            return note_prefix + reply
 669
 670        # Reuse the main intent classifier; PIPELINE (creates rules/agents) is refused.
 671        intent = await self._classify_intent(text)
 672        logger.info("[%s] Intent (restricted): %s — %s", self.name, intent, text[:60])
 673
 674        if intent == "PIPELINE":
 675            reply = (
 676                "I can't create automations or new agents from a social channel — "
 677                "set those up on the dashboard. I can still answer questions and "
 678                "control your devices from here."
 679            )
 680            await self._record_external_exchange(text, reply)
 681            return note_prefix + reply
 682
 683        if intent == "ACTUATE":
 684            # Everyday devices only. The actuator executes the domain/service the
 685            # LLM picked, so without this gate "control my devices" reaches
 686            # shell_command/python_script/hassio and becomes code execution.
 687            response = await self._handle_actuate_intent(
 688                text, allowed_domains=SOCIAL_ACTUATE_DOMAINS
 689            )
 690            await self._record_external_exchange(text, response)
 691            return note_prefix + response
 692
 693        if intent == "HA":
 694            response = await self.delegation.ask_home_assistant(text)
 695            await self._record_external_exchange(text, response)
 696            return note_prefix + response
 697
 698        # OTHER: converse, but run no action executors.
 699        self._rebuild_system_prompt()
 700        prefixed_text = self._prefix_with_live_context(text)
 701        response = await self.chat(prefixed_text)
 702        self._restore_unprefixed_turn(prefixed_text, text)
 703
 704        # The prose around a spawn/delete block asserts the action happened, so
 705        # stripping the block would leave a false claim. Discard the whole reply.
 706        clean, had_actions = self._neutralize_action_blocks(response)
 707        if had_actions:
 708            reply = (
 709                "I can't create or delete agents from this channel — that's a "
 710                "dashboard-only action. I'm happy to chat, answer questions, or "
 711                "control your devices instead."
 712            )
 713            await self._record_external_exchange(text, reply)
 714            return note_prefix + reply
 715
 716        # Structured delegation only (allow-listed, no spawn); skip loose @mentions.
 717        clean, _ = await self._process_delegate_commands(clean, restricted=True)
 718        return note_prefix + clean.strip()
 719
 720    async def process_user_input_stream(
 721        self, text: str, attachments: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None
 722    ) -> AsyncGenerator[Any]:
 723        """Streaming version of process_user_input().
 724        Yields text chunks as the LLM generates them, then a final dict:
 725          {"done": True, "spawned": [...names...], "system_msg": "..."}
 726
 727        The CLI calls this and prints chunks immediately.
 728        REST/Discord/WhatsApp should use process_user_input() instead.
 729
 730        `attachments` are content blocks for this turn. They reach the model on
 731        the branch below that calls the LLM; a turn answered without one — a
 732        command, an actuation, a pipeline plan, a delegation to the Home
 733        Assistant agent — does not read them.
 734        """
 735        # Drain monitor notifications first
 736        note_prefix = self._drain_notifications()
 737        if note_prefix:
 738            yield note_prefix
 739
 740        # ── Pending-plan response detection (same as non-streaming path) ─────
 741        if not text.strip().startswith("/") and not text.strip().startswith("@"):
 742            plan_response = await self._handle_pending_plan_response(text)
 743            if plan_response is not None:
 744                await self._record_external_exchange(text, plan_response)
 745                yield plan_response
 746                yield {"done": True, "spawned": [], "system_msg": ""}
 747                return
 748
 749            # Collision guard — see process_user_input for rationale
 750            warn = self._warn_if_pending_plan_collision(text)
 751            if warn:
 752                await self._record_external_exchange(text, warn)
 753                yield warn
 754                yield {"done": True, "spawned": [], "system_msg": ""}
 755                return
 756
 757        # All slash-commands and direct API intercepts are handled by process_user_input
 758        # Route them there to avoid duplicating all that logic here
 759        _stripped = text.strip().rstrip("()")
 760        _is_command = _stripped.startswith(("/", "@")) or _stripped in (
 761            "list_nodes",
 762            "main.list_nodes",
 763            "rules",
 764        )
 765        if _is_command:
 766            # /deploy is the one slash command that needs to stream progress
 767            # messages mid-execution (subnet scan, deploy phases). Other commands
 768            # go through process_user_input which is request/response.
 769            if _stripped.startswith("/deploy"):
 770                async for chunk in self._slash_deploy_stream(_stripped):
 771                    yield chunk
 772                yield {"done": True, "spawned": [], "system_msg": ""}
 773                return
 774            result = await self.process_user_input(text)
 775            yield result
 776            yield {"done": True, "spawned": [], "system_msg": ""}
 777            return
 778
 779        # Explicit planner prefix always wins
 780        _lowered = text.lower()
 781        if any(_lowered.startswith(p) for p in PLANNER_PREFIXES):
 782            result = await self._run_planner(text)
 783            response = result or "Planner did not return a result. Please retry."
 784            await self._record_external_exchange(text, response)
 785            yield response
 786            yield {"done": True, "spawned": [], "system_msg": ""}
 787            return
 788
 789        # Single LLM call classifies intent: ACTUATE, HA, PIPELINE, or OTHER
 790        intent = await self._classify_intent(text)
 791        logger.info("[%s] Intent: %s — %s", self.name, intent, text[:60])
 792
 793        if intent == "PIPELINE":
 794            response = await self._propose_or_execute_pipeline(text)
 795            await self._record_external_exchange(text, response)
 796            yield response
 797            yield {"done": True, "spawned": [], "system_msg": ""}
 798            return
 799
 800        if intent == "ACTUATE":
 801            response = await self._handle_actuate_intent(text)
 802            await self._record_external_exchange(text, response)
 803            yield response
 804            yield {"done": True, "spawned": [], "system_msg": ""}
 805            return
 806
 807        if intent == "HA":
 808            response = await self.delegation.ask_home_assistant(text)
 809            await self._record_external_exchange(text, response)
 810            yield response
 811            yield {"done": True, "spawned": [], "system_msg": ""}
 812            return
 813
 814        # Refresh the system prompt with live registry + facts before any LLM call.
 815        # This ensures the LLM never answers from a stale view of which agents exist.
 816        self._rebuild_system_prompt()
 817
 818        # Belt-and-braces: inject live agent list as a prefix on the user message.
 819        # Same as the non-streaming path — see _prefix_with_live_context for why.
 820        prefixed_text = self._prefix_with_live_context(text)
 821
 822        # Stream the LLM response chunk by chunk
 823        full_chunks = []
 824        async for chunk in self.chat_stream(prefixed_text, attachments):
 825            if isinstance(chunk, dict):
 826                break  # usage dict — discard, already tracked inside chat_stream
 827            full_chunks.append(chunk)
 828            yield chunk
 829
 830        # Replace the prefixed user message in history with the clean original
 831        # so future turns aren't polluted with stale prefixes.
 832        self._restore_unprefixed_turn(prefixed_text, text)
 833
 834        full_response = "".join(full_chunks)
 835
 836        # Process any <spawn> blocks in the completed response
 837        _, spawned = await self._process_spawn_commands(full_response)
 838
 839        # Process any <delete> blocks — orchestrator-side counterpart of <spawn>
 840        _, deleted, missing = await self._process_delete_commands(full_response)
 841
 842        # Execute structured <delegate>{...}</delegate> blocks first (preferred
 843        # form). The raw block was already streamed to the user above, so append
 844        # each result as an additional chunk — same approach as @mention results.
 845        full_response, _delegate_results = await self._process_delegate_commands(full_response)
 846        for _r in _delegate_results:
 847            yield "\n" + _r
 848
 849        # Execute any looser @agent-name delegation patterns the LLM produced.
 850        # If delegations ran, yield the results as an additional chunk.
 851        delegated = await self._execute_llm_delegations(full_response)
 852        if delegated != full_response:
 853            # Find what changed and yield just the new parts
 854            results = re.findall(r"[✅❌]\s+\S+.*", delegated)
 855            if results:
 856                yield "\n" + "\n".join(results)
 857        full_response = delegated
 858
 859        system_msg = TurnActions(tuple(spawned), tuple(deleted), tuple(missing)).summary(
 860            full_response
 861        )
 862
 863        # Also surface the concrete spawn/delete outcome for stream consumers
 864        # that ignore the final done dict.
 865        if system_msg:
 866            yield f"\n\n_ℹ️ {system_msg}_"
 867
 868        await self._mqtt_publish(
 869            f"agents/{self.actor_id}/logs",
 870            {"type": "user_interaction", "input": text[:100], "response": full_response[:200]},
 871        )
 872
 873        yield {"done": True, "spawned": spawned, "system_msg": system_msg}
 874

 877    def _match_catalog_recipe(self, name: str, capabilities: list[str] | None = None) -> str | None:
 878        """Return the name of a catalog recipe that already covers this request.
 879
 880        Used to stop the LLM from reimplementing an agent that the catalog
 881        already provides (e.g. it writes a fresh 'smart-energy-agent' when the
 882        catalog has 'smart-energy'). Matching is by normalised name only —
 883        the safest signal. Capability overlap is intentionally NOT used here
 884        because it produces false positives that would block genuinely new
 885        agents.
 886
 887        Checks two sources so it doesn't depend on manifest-injection timing
 888        (the catalog injects its recipe manifests into main on startup, but
 889        that races with main coming up — if it lost the race, the manifests
 890        wouldn't be here yet). The live catalog actor is the real source of
 891        truth and is consulted as a fallback.
 892        """
 893        want = _normalize_agent_name(name)
 894        if not want:
 895            return None
 896
 897        # 1. Injected manifests (fast path)
 898        for recipe_name, manifest in self._agent_manifests.items():
 899            if not (manifest.get("spawnable") and manifest.get("catalog")):
 900                continue
 901            if _normalize_agent_name(recipe_name) == want:
 902                return recipe_name
 903
 904        # 2. Live catalog actor — authoritative, immune to injection races
 905        if self._registry:
 906            cat = self._registry.find_by_name("catalog")
 907            if cat and hasattr(cat, "list_recipes"):
 908                try:
 909                    for recipe_name in cat.list_recipes():  # pyright: ignore[reportAttributeAccessIssue]
 910                        if _normalize_agent_name(recipe_name) == want:
 911                            return recipe_name
 912                except Exception as exc:
 913                    logger.debug("[%s] Catalog recipe lookup failed: %s", self.name, exc)
 914
 915        return None
 916

1019    def list_topics(self, keyword: str = "") -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
1020        """Return all known MQTT topics published by agents, optionally filtered by keyword.
1021        Each entry: {"topic": str, "agents": [{"name", "node", "description"}, ...]}
1022
1023        Example:
1024            list_topics("cpu")     → topics containing "cpu"
1025            list_topics("temp")    → topics containing "temp"
1026            list_topics()          → all topics
1027        """
1028        results = []
1029        kw = keyword.lower()
1030        for topic, manifests in self._topic_registry.items():
1031            if kw and kw not in topic.lower():
1032                continue
1033            results.append(
1034                {
1035                    "topic": topic,
1036                    "agents": [
1037                        {
1038                            "name": m.get("name"),
1039                            "node": m.get("node"),
1040                            "description": m.get("description", ""),
1041                        }
1042                        for m in manifests
1043                    ],
1044                }
1045            )
1046        return sorted(results, key=lambda x: x["topic"])
1047
1048    def list_capabilities(self, keyword: str = "") -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
1049        """Return all known agents with their full capability profile:
1050        name, description, capabilities, input_schema, output_schema.
1051
1052        Includes remote agents — they appear in _agent_manifests via the
1053        manifest listener (remote agents publish retained manifests just like
1054        local ones). The `running` flag is True for both local registry actors
1055        AND agents currently listed in a live node's heartbeat.
1056        """
1057        remote_running = self.nodes.running_agents()
1058
1059        results = []
1060        kw = keyword.lower().strip()
1061        kw_words = kw.split() if kw else []
1062        for name, manifest in self._agent_manifests.items():
1063            desc = manifest.get("description", "")
1064            caps = manifest.get("capabilities", [])
1065            if kw_words:
1066                haystack = desc.lower() + " " + " ".join(caps).lower() + " " + name.lower()
1067                if not any(w in haystack for w in kw_words):
1068                    continue
1069            local_running = bool(self._registry and self._registry.find_by_name(name))
1070            results.append(
1071                {
1072                    "name": name,
1073                    "node": manifest.get("node"),
1074                    "description": desc,
1075                    "capabilities": caps,
1076                    "input_schema": manifest.get("input_schema", {}),
1077                    "output_schema": manifest.get("output_schema", {}),
1078                    "spawnable": manifest.get("spawnable", False),
1079                    "running": local_running or name in remote_running,
1080                    "remote": name in remote_running and not local_running,
1081                }
1082            )
1083        return sorted(results, key=lambda x: x["name"])
1084

1093    async def _slash_deploy_stream(self, stripped: str) -> AsyncGenerator[str]:
1094        """Async generator implementing /deploy. Yields progress strings.
1095
1096        Accepts one form only::
1097
1098            /deploy <node>
1099
1100        where ``<node>`` names a target configured in the environment
1101        (``DEPLOY_TARGETS`` plus a ``DEPLOY_<NODE>_*`` block). The older
1102        ``/deploy <node> <host> <user> <password> [broker]`` form is refused:
1103        the password reached the reply stream and the persisted conversation
1104        history, and running with no host port-scanned the local /24 for SSH.
1105        """
1106        parts = stripped.split()
1107        if len(parts) < 2:
1108            names = deploy_target_names()
1109            listing = "\n".join(f"  {n}" for n in names) or "  (none configured)"
1110            yield f"[usage] /deploy <node-name>\nConfigured targets:\n{listing}"
1111            return
1112
1113        node_name = parts[1]
1114        if len(parts) > 2:
1115            # Do not echo parts[2:] — the old form put a live SSH password there
1116            # and this reply is recorded into conversation history.
1117            yield (
1118                "[error] /deploy takes a node name only — host and SSH credentials "
1119                "now come from the environment, not from chat.\n\n" + deploy_target_help(node_name)
1120            )
1121            return
1122
1123        target = deploy_target(node_name)
1124        if target is None:
1125            yield "[error] " + deploy_target_help(node_name)
1126            return
1127
1128        host = target.host
1129        if not host:
1130            # A single name lookup, not a sweep — it asks about one host and
1131            # learns nothing about any other machine on the network.
1132            yield f"[discover] No host configured for '{node_name}' — trying mDNS..."
1133            try:
1134                host = await asyncio.to_thread(socket.gethostbyname, f"{node_name}.local")
1135            except OSError:
1136                host = ""
1137            if not host:
1138                yield (
1139                    f"[error] Could not resolve '{node_name}.local'.\n"
1140                    f"Set {deploy_env_prefix(node_name)}_HOST in your environment."
1141                )
1142                return
1143            yield f"[discover] Found via mDNS: {node_name}.local → {host}"
1144
1145        if not hasattr(self, "delegate_to_installer"):
1146            yield "[error] Installer agent not available."
1147            return
1148
1149        yield (
1150            f"[deploy] Deploying to {target.user}@{host} as node '{node_name}'...\n"
1151            f"(This may take 20-60 seconds while packages install on the remote machine)"
1152        )
1153        try:
1154            result = await self.delegate_to_installer(
1155                {
1156                    "action": "node_deploy",
1157                    "host": host,
1158                    "node_name": target.name,
1159                    "broker": target.broker or "localhost",
1160                    "port": target.broker_port,
1161                },
1162                timeout=120.0,
1163            )
1164        except Exception as exc:
1165            logger.exception("[main] /deploy failed for node %r", node_name)
1166            yield f"[FAIL] Deploy failed: {exc}"
1167            return
1168
1169        if result.get("success"):
1170            yield (
1171                f"[OK] Node '{node_name}' is live! It will appear in /nodes within ~15 seconds.\n\n"
1172                f"Spawn agents on it:\n"
1173                f'  "spawn a CPU monitor agent on {node_name}"\n'
1174                f'  "spawn a temperature sensor on {node_name}"'
1175            )
1176        else:
1177            yield f"[FAIL] Deploy failed: {result.get('error', result)}"
1178

136        # Queued monitor notifications — prepended to next user response, and
137        # capped at MAX_PENDING_NOTIFICATIONS: they drain only when someone
138        # chats, so on an idle system with a failing agent nothing empties them.

async def on_start(self) -> None:

240        await super().on_start()

242        # Listen for remote node heartbeats so we know what's online
243        self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._node_heartbeat_listener()))
244        # Detect nodes that go silent and clean up their agents
245        self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._node_offline_watcher()))
246        # Listen for agent capability manifests to build topic registry
247        self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._manifest_listener()))
248        # LLM bridge — lets remote agents call agent.ask_llm() / agent.chat()
249        self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._llm_bridge_listener()))
250        # Observe real MQTT payloads from remote agents to populate observed_samples
251        self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._remote_observed_samples_listener()))
252        # Receive state + config from remote nodes during remote→local migration
253        self._tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._state_return_listener()))
254        # Inject persisted user facts into system prompt
255        self._inject_user_facts_into_prompt()

async def chat_stream( self, user_message: str, attachments: list[dict[str, typing.Any]] | None = None) -> AsyncGenerator[str | dict[str, typing.Any]]: 
400    async def chat_stream(
401        self, user_message: str, attachments: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None
402    ) -> AsyncGenerator[str | dict[str, Any]]:
403        full_response = []
404        got_usage = False
405        async for chunk in super().chat_stream(user_message, attachments):
406            if isinstance(chunk, dict):
407                got_usage = True
408                yield chunk
409            else:
410                full_response.append(chunk)
411                yield chunk
412        # Only extract facts when a real LLM response was received (usage dict present).
413        # Skips early-exit cases like cost-limit errors so no extra LLM call is made.
414        if full_response and got_usage:
415            clean_msg = _strip_live_context(user_message)
416            asyncio.create_task(self._extract_and_save_facts(clean_msg, "".join(full_response)))

async def process_user_input(self, text: str) -> str: 
489    async def process_user_input(self, text: str) -> str:
490        note_prefix = self._drain_notifications()
491
492        # ── Pending-plan response detection ─────────────────────────────────
493        # If there's a dry-run plan waiting for approval and the user's message
494        # looks like "yes"/"no", handle it BEFORE any other processing. This
495        # must come first so a bare "yes" doesn't accidentally hit the intent
496        # classifier or get treated as a new prompt. Slash commands and other
497        # explicit prefixes are NOT intercepted (the user might want to inspect
498        # /plans or /registry while a plan is pending).
499        if not text.strip().startswith("/") and not text.strip().startswith("@"):
500            plan_response = await self._handle_pending_plan_response(text)
501            if plan_response is not None:
502                # Record the exchange so history reflects the approval/rejection
503                await self._record_external_exchange(text, plan_response)
504                return note_prefix + plan_response
505
506            # Pending-plan ambiguity guard: if the user has a plan pending
507            # and now types something that looks like another spawn / pipeline
508            # request, we'd otherwise silently create the new agents AND
509            # later spawn the pending ones too — duplicates galore. Warn
510            # the user and ask them to resolve the pending plan first.
511            warn = self._warn_if_pending_plan_collision(text)
512            if warn:
513                await self._record_external_exchange(text, warn)
514                return note_prefix + warn
515
516        # ── Direct API intercepts — handle without LLM round-trip ──────────
517        stripped = text.strip().rstrip("()")
518
519        # ── Commands ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
520        # Every command lives in the registry; registration order is dispatch
521        # order, so a command answers where the chain this replaced answered it.
522        found = command_registry.find(stripped)
523        if found is not None:
524            handler, argument = found[0].handler, found[1]
525            return note_prefix + await handler(CommandContext(actor=self), argument)
526
527        # ── Webhook / notification URL management ───────────────────────────
528
529        # Auto-detect webhook URLs in any message and persist them
530        _webhook_match = re.search(
531            r"https?://(?:discord\.com/api/webhooks|hooks\.slack\.com|api\.telegram\.org)/\S+", text
532        )
533        if _webhook_match:
534            url = _webhook_match.group(0).rstrip(".,;!)'\"")
535            urls = self.recall("_notification_urls") or {}
536            if "discord" in url:
537                urls["discord"] = url
538            elif "slack" in url:
539                urls["slack"] = url
540            elif "telegram" in url:
541                urls["telegram"] = url
542            self.persist("_notification_urls", urls)
543            logger.info("[%s] Auto-saved webhook URL from message", self.name)
544
545        # ── @mention direct routing ─────────────────────────────────────────
546        if text.startswith("@"):
547            return note_prefix + await self.delegation.route_mention(text)
548
549        # Explicit planner prefix always wins
550        lowered = text.lower()
551        if any(lowered.startswith(p) for p in PLANNER_PREFIXES):
552            result = await self._run_planner(text)
553            response = result or "Planner did not return a result. Please retry."
554            await self._record_external_exchange(text, response)
555            return note_prefix + response
556
557        # Single LLM call classifies intent: ACTUATE, HA, PIPELINE (reactive rule), OTHER
558        intent = await self._classify_intent(text)
559        logger.info("[%s] Intent: %s — %s", self.name, intent, text[:60])
560
561        if intent == "PIPELINE":
562            response = await self._propose_or_execute_pipeline(text)
563            await self._record_external_exchange(text, response)
564            return note_prefix + response
565
566        if intent == "ACTUATE":
567            response = await self._handle_actuate_intent(text)
568            await self._record_external_exchange(text, response)
569            return note_prefix + response
570
571        if intent == "HA":
572            response = await self.delegation.ask_home_assistant(text)
573            await self._record_external_exchange(text, response)
574            return note_prefix + response
575
576        # Refresh the system prompt with live registry + facts before any LLM call.
577        # This ensures the LLM never answers from a stale view of which agents exist.
578        self._rebuild_system_prompt()
579
580        # Belt-and-braces: also inject the live agent list as a prefix on the
581        # user message itself. Models trust in-message context over system-prompt
582        # claims, so this is the strongest signal we can give without using a tool.
583        # We send the prefixed text to the LLM but replace it with the clean
584        # original in conversation history afterward — otherwise stale prefixes
585        # would accumulate across turns and bloat the context window.
586        prefixed_text = self._prefix_with_live_context(text)
587        response = await self.chat(prefixed_text)
588        # Find the most recent user message in history that matches the prefixed
589        # text and replace it with the user's original. The assistant turn after
590        # it remains unchanged.
591        self._restore_unprefixed_turn(prefixed_text, text)
592
593        # If the LLM wrote agent code but forgot the <spawn> wrapper, remind it once
594        has_spawn = "<spawn>" in response
595        has_code = "async def handle_task" in response or "async def setup" in response
596        asked_spawn = any(
597            w in text.lower() for w in ("spawn", "create", "make", "build", "add", "agent")
598        )
599        if has_code and not has_spawn and asked_spawn:
600            logger.info("[%s] Code written without <spawn> — prompting to wrap it", self.name)
601            response = await self.chat(
602                "You wrote agent code but forgot to wrap it in a <spawn> block. "
603                "Please output the complete spawn block now with that exact code inside it. "
604                "Output ONLY the <spawn>...</spawn> block, nothing else."
605            )
606
607        clean, spawned = await self._process_spawn_commands(response)
608
609        # Process any <delete>{"name": "..."}</delete> blocks the LLM produced.
610        # This is the orchestrator-side counterpart of <spawn> — lets the LLM
611        # remove agents in response to user requests like "delete the math agent".
612        clean, deleted, missing = await self._process_delete_commands(clean)
613
614        # Execute structured <delegate>{...}</delegate> blocks — the preferred,
615        # unambiguous delegation form. Results are spliced in-place.
616        clean, _delegate_results = await self._process_delegate_commands(clean)
617
618        # Execute any looser @agent-name delegation patterns the LLM produced
619        clean = await self._execute_llm_delegations(clean)
620
621        await self._mqtt_publish(
622            f"agents/{self.actor_id}/logs",
623            {"type": "user_interaction", "input": text[:100], "response": clean[:200]},
624        )
625
626        summary = TurnActions(tuple(spawned), tuple(deleted), tuple(missing)).summary(response)
627        if summary:
628            clean += f"\n\n[System: {summary}]"
629
630        return note_prefix + clean
async def process_user_input_restricted(self, text: str) -> str: 
644    async def process_user_input_restricted(self, text: str) -> str:
645        """Social-channel (Discord/Telegram) entry point — the untrusted-surface
646        counterpart of process_user_input.
647
648        Conversation, device control (ACTUATE), and HA queries only. Spawning,
649        deleting, code, pipelines, admin commands, and delegation to
650        non-allowlisted agents are blocked — at the action, not by classifying
651        the text, so it can't be talked around.
652        """
653        note_prefix = self._drain_notifications()
654        stripped = text.strip()
655
656        # Slash commands and the bypass markers are the admin surface — not
657        # exposed here. Every marker the planner honours is refused, not just
658        # the first: a guard that catches one spelling of a family reads as
659        # covering the family.
660        if stripped.startswith("/") or starts_with_bypass(stripped):
661            reply = (
662                "Admin commands aren't available on this channel — just talk to me "
663                "normally. I can answer questions, tell you what's going on, and "
664                "control your devices. (Spawning, deleting, and running code stay "
665                "on the dashboard.)"
666            )
667            await self._record_external_exchange(text, reply)
668            return note_prefix + reply
669
670        # Reuse the main intent classifier; PIPELINE (creates rules/agents) is refused.
671        intent = await self._classify_intent(text)
672        logger.info("[%s] Intent (restricted): %s — %s", self.name, intent, text[:60])
673
674        if intent == "PIPELINE":
675            reply = (
676                "I can't create automations or new agents from a social channel — "
677                "set those up on the dashboard. I can still answer questions and "
678                "control your devices from here."
679            )
680            await self._record_external_exchange(text, reply)
681            return note_prefix + reply
682
683        if intent == "ACTUATE":
684            # Everyday devices only. The actuator executes the domain/service the
685            # LLM picked, so without this gate "control my devices" reaches
686            # shell_command/python_script/hassio and becomes code execution.
687            response = await self._handle_actuate_intent(
688                text, allowed_domains=SOCIAL_ACTUATE_DOMAINS
689            )
690            await self._record_external_exchange(text, response)
691            return note_prefix + response
692
693        if intent == "HA":
694            response = await self.delegation.ask_home_assistant(text)
695            await self._record_external_exchange(text, response)
696            return note_prefix + response
697
698        # OTHER: converse, but run no action executors.
699        self._rebuild_system_prompt()
700        prefixed_text = self._prefix_with_live_context(text)
701        response = await self.chat(prefixed_text)
702        self._restore_unprefixed_turn(prefixed_text, text)
703
704        # The prose around a spawn/delete block asserts the action happened, so
705        # stripping the block would leave a false claim. Discard the whole reply.
706        clean, had_actions = self._neutralize_action_blocks(response)
707        if had_actions:
708            reply = (
709                "I can't create or delete agents from this channel — that's a "
710                "dashboard-only action. I'm happy to chat, answer questions, or "
711                "control your devices instead."
712            )
713            await self._record_external_exchange(text, reply)
714            return note_prefix + reply
715
716        # Structured delegation only (allow-listed, no spawn); skip loose @mentions.
717        clean, _ = await self._process_delegate_commands(clean, restricted=True)
718        return note_prefix + clean.strip()

Social-channel (Discord/Telegram) entry point — the untrusted-surface counterpart of process_user_input.

Conversation, device control (ACTUATE), and HA queries only. Spawning, deleting, code, pipelines, admin commands, and delegation to non-allowlisted agents are blocked — at the action, not by classifying the text, so it can't be talked around.

async def process_user_input_stream( self, text: str, attachments: list[dict[str, typing.Any]] | None = None) -> AsyncGenerator[typing.Any]: 
720    async def process_user_input_stream(
721        self, text: str, attachments: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None
722    ) -> AsyncGenerator[Any]:
723        """Streaming version of process_user_input().
724        Yields text chunks as the LLM generates them, then a final dict:
725          {"done": True, "spawned": [...names...], "system_msg": "..."}
726
727        The CLI calls this and prints chunks immediately.
728        REST/Discord/WhatsApp should use process_user_input() instead.
729
730        `attachments` are content blocks for this turn. They reach the model on
731        the branch below that calls the LLM; a turn answered without one — a
732        command, an actuation, a pipeline plan, a delegation to the Home
733        Assistant agent — does not read them.
734        """
735        # Drain monitor notifications first
736        note_prefix = self._drain_notifications()
737        if note_prefix:
738            yield note_prefix
739
740        # ── Pending-plan response detection (same as non-streaming path) ─────
741        if not text.strip().startswith("/") and not text.strip().startswith("@"):
742            plan_response = await self._handle_pending_plan_response(text)
743            if plan_response is not None:
744                await self._record_external_exchange(text, plan_response)
745                yield plan_response
746                yield {"done": True, "spawned": [], "system_msg": ""}
747                return
748
749            # Collision guard — see process_user_input for rationale
750            warn = self._warn_if_pending_plan_collision(text)
751            if warn:
752                await self._record_external_exchange(text, warn)
753                yield warn
754                yield {"done": True, "spawned": [], "system_msg": ""}
755                return
756
757        # All slash-commands and direct API intercepts are handled by process_user_input
758        # Route them there to avoid duplicating all that logic here
759        _stripped = text.strip().rstrip("()")
760        _is_command = _stripped.startswith(("/", "@")) or _stripped in (
761            "list_nodes",
762            "main.list_nodes",
763            "rules",
764        )
765        if _is_command:
766            # /deploy is the one slash command that needs to stream progress
767            # messages mid-execution (subnet scan, deploy phases). Other commands
768            # go through process_user_input which is request/response.
769            if _stripped.startswith("/deploy"):
770                async for chunk in self._slash_deploy_stream(_stripped):
771                    yield chunk
772                yield {"done": True, "spawned": [], "system_msg": ""}
773                return
774            result = await self.process_user_input(text)
775            yield result
776            yield {"done": True, "spawned": [], "system_msg": ""}
777            return
778
779        # Explicit planner prefix always wins
780        _lowered = text.lower()
781        if any(_lowered.startswith(p) for p in PLANNER_PREFIXES):
782            result = await self._run_planner(text)
783            response = result or "Planner did not return a result. Please retry."
784            await self._record_external_exchange(text, response)
785            yield response
786            yield {"done": True, "spawned": [], "system_msg": ""}
787            return
788
789        # Single LLM call classifies intent: ACTUATE, HA, PIPELINE, or OTHER
790        intent = await self._classify_intent(text)
791        logger.info("[%s] Intent: %s — %s", self.name, intent, text[:60])
792
793        if intent == "PIPELINE":
794            response = await self._propose_or_execute_pipeline(text)
795            await self._record_external_exchange(text, response)
796            yield response
797            yield {"done": True, "spawned": [], "system_msg": ""}
798            return
799
800        if intent == "ACTUATE":
801            response = await self._handle_actuate_intent(text)
802            await self._record_external_exchange(text, response)
803            yield response
804            yield {"done": True, "spawned": [], "system_msg": ""}
805            return
806
807        if intent == "HA":
808            response = await self.delegation.ask_home_assistant(text)
809            await self._record_external_exchange(text, response)
810            yield response
811            yield {"done": True, "spawned": [], "system_msg": ""}
812            return
813
814        # Refresh the system prompt with live registry + facts before any LLM call.
815        # This ensures the LLM never answers from a stale view of which agents exist.
816        self._rebuild_system_prompt()
817
818        # Belt-and-braces: inject live agent list as a prefix on the user message.
819        # Same as the non-streaming path — see _prefix_with_live_context for why.
820        prefixed_text = self._prefix_with_live_context(text)
821
822        # Stream the LLM response chunk by chunk
823        full_chunks = []
824        async for chunk in self.chat_stream(prefixed_text, attachments):
825            if isinstance(chunk, dict):
826                break  # usage dict — discard, already tracked inside chat_stream
827            full_chunks.append(chunk)
828            yield chunk
829
830        # Replace the prefixed user message in history with the clean original
831        # so future turns aren't polluted with stale prefixes.
832        self._restore_unprefixed_turn(prefixed_text, text)
833
834        full_response = "".join(full_chunks)
835
836        # Process any <spawn> blocks in the completed response
837        _, spawned = await self._process_spawn_commands(full_response)
838
839        # Process any <delete> blocks — orchestrator-side counterpart of <spawn>
840        _, deleted, missing = await self._process_delete_commands(full_response)
841
842        # Execute structured <delegate>{...}</delegate> blocks first (preferred
843        # form). The raw block was already streamed to the user above, so append
844        # each result as an additional chunk — same approach as @mention results.
845        full_response, _delegate_results = await self._process_delegate_commands(full_response)
846        for _r in _delegate_results:
847            yield "\n" + _r
848
849        # Execute any looser @agent-name delegation patterns the LLM produced.
850        # If delegations ran, yield the results as an additional chunk.
851        delegated = await self._execute_llm_delegations(full_response)
852        if delegated != full_response:
853            # Find what changed and yield just the new parts
854            results = re.findall(r"[✅❌]\s+\S+.*", delegated)
855            if results:
856                yield "\n" + "\n".join(results)
857        full_response = delegated
858
859        system_msg = TurnActions(tuple(spawned), tuple(deleted), tuple(missing)).summary(
860            full_response
861        )
862
863        # Also surface the concrete spawn/delete outcome for stream consumers
864        # that ignore the final done dict.
865        if system_msg:
866            yield f"\n\n_ℹ️ {system_msg}_"
867
868        await self._mqtt_publish(
869            f"agents/{self.actor_id}/logs",
870            {"type": "user_interaction", "input": text[:100], "response": full_response[:200]},
871        )
872
873        yield {"done": True, "spawned": spawned, "system_msg": system_msg}

Streaming version of process_user_input(). Yields text chunks as the LLM generates them, then a final dict: {"done": True, "spawned": [...names...], "system_msg": "..."}

The CLI calls this and prints chunks immediately. REST/Discord/WhatsApp should use process_user_input() instead.

attachments are content blocks for this turn. They reach the model on the branch below that calls the LLM; a turn answered without one — a command, an actuation, a pipeline plan, a delegation to the Home Assistant agent — does not read them.

def list_topics(self, keyword: str = '') -> list[dict[str, typing.Any]]: 
1019    def list_topics(self, keyword: str = "") -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
1020        """Return all known MQTT topics published by agents, optionally filtered by keyword.
1021        Each entry: {"topic": str, "agents": [{"name", "node", "description"}, ...]}
1022
1023        Example:
1024            list_topics("cpu")     → topics containing "cpu"
1025            list_topics("temp")    → topics containing "temp"
1026            list_topics()          → all topics
1027        """
1028        results = []
1029        kw = keyword.lower()
1030        for topic, manifests in self._topic_registry.items():
1031            if kw and kw not in topic.lower():
1032                continue
1033            results.append(
1034                {
1035                    "topic": topic,
1036                    "agents": [
1037                        {
1038                            "name": m.get("name"),
1039                            "node": m.get("node"),
1040                            "description": m.get("description", ""),
1041                        }
1042                        for m in manifests
1043                    ],
1044                }
1045            )
1046        return sorted(results, key=lambda x: x["topic"])

def list_capabilities(self, keyword: str = '') -> list[dict[str, typing.Any]]: 
1048    def list_capabilities(self, keyword: str = "") -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
1049        """Return all known agents with their full capability profile:
1050        name, description, capabilities, input_schema, output_schema.
1051
1052        Includes remote agents — they appear in _agent_manifests via the
1053        manifest listener (remote agents publish retained manifests just like
1054        local ones). The `running` flag is True for both local registry actors
1055        AND agents currently listed in a live node's heartbeat.
1056        """
1057        remote_running = self.nodes.running_agents()
1058
1059        results = []
1060        kw = keyword.lower().strip()
1061        kw_words = kw.split() if kw else []
1062        for name, manifest in self._agent_manifests.items():
1063            desc = manifest.get("description", "")
1064            caps = manifest.get("capabilities", [])
1065            if kw_words:
1066                haystack = desc.lower() + " " + " ".join(caps).lower() + " " + name.lower()
1067                if not any(w in haystack for w in kw_words):
1068                    continue
1069            local_running = bool(self._registry and self._registry.find_by_name(name))
1070            results.append(
1071                {
1072                    "name": name,
1073                    "node": manifest.get("node"),
1074                    "description": desc,
1075                    "capabilities": caps,
1076                    "input_schema": manifest.get("input_schema", {}),
1077                    "output_schema": manifest.get("output_schema", {}),
1078                    "spawnable": manifest.get("spawnable", False),
1079                    "running": local_running or name in remote_running,
1080                    "remote": name in remote_running and not local_running,
1081                }
1082            )
1083        return sorted(results, key=lambda x: x["name"])

Return all known agents with their full capability profile: name, description, capabilities, input_schema, output_schema.

Includes remote agents — they appear in _agent_manifests via the manifest listener (remote agents publish retained manifests just like local ones). The running flag is True for both local registry actors AND agents currently listed in a live node's heartbeat.
