class PlannerAgent(wactorz.Actor, wactorz.agents.mixins.spawning.SpawnMixin, wactorz.agents.planner.context.ContextMixin, wactorz.agents.planner.execution.ExecutionMixin, wactorz.agents.planner.pipeline.PipelineMixin): 
 54class PlannerAgent(Actor, SpawnMixin, ContextMixin, ExecutionMixin, PipelineMixin):
 55    """On-demand orchestrator. Spawned per complex task, self-terminates when done."""
 56
 57    #: Hard cap on a planner's life. A caller awaiting its reply must not wait
 58    #: longer than this plus delivery: once the cap fires the planner is gone
 59    #: and no reply can follow, so any remaining wait is spent on nothing.
 60    DEFAULT_MAX_LIFETIME_S = 90.0
 61
 62    def __init__(
 63        self,
 64        llm_provider: LLMProvider | None = None,
 65        task: str = "",
 66        reply_to_id: str = "",
 67        reply_task_id: str = "",
 68        auto_terminate: bool = True,
 69        plan_only: bool = False,
 70        approved_plan: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
 71        max_lifetime_s: float = DEFAULT_MAX_LIFETIME_S,
 72        **kwargs: Any,
 73    ) -> None:
 74        kwargs.setdefault("name", "planner")
 75        super().__init__(**kwargs)
 76        self.llm = llm_provider
 77        self._task = task
 78        self._reply_to_id = reply_to_id
 79        self._reply_task_id = reply_task_id
 80        self._auto_terminate = auto_terminate
 81        # Dry-run support:
 82        #   plan_only=True       → produce a plan, return it as JSON, do NOT spawn.
 83        #   approved_plan=<dict> → skip planning, execute the supplied plan directly.
 84        # These are mutually exclusive in practice. If both are somehow set,
 85        # approved_plan takes precedence (it is checked first in _run_plan) and
 86        # the plan is executed; plan_only is ignored. on_start() enforces this
 87        # and logs it so the behaviour is never silent.
 88        self._plan_only = plan_only
 89        self._approved_plan = approved_plan
 90        self._result_futures: dict[str, asyncio.Future] = {}
 91        self._spawned_by_planner: list[str] = []  # agents we created this run
 92        # Per-agent spawn outcome: name → {"ok": bool, "error": str|None}
 93        # Sent back to main in the RESULT payload so it knows what actually happened.
 94        self._spawn_results: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
 95
 96        # Lifecycle: a planner must never outlive its task. _max_lifetime_s is a
 97        # hard cap after which the planner self-removes regardless of state, so
 98        # proposal/pipeline/approved planners don't accumulate until an app
 99        # restart. _terminated guards against double-teardown; _lifetime_task
100        # holds the watchdog so normal completion can cancel it.
101        self._max_lifetime_s: float = max_lifetime_s
102        self._terminated: bool = False
103        self._lifetime_task: asyncio.Task | None = None
104
105        # Cost tracking — accumulated across all llm.complete() calls this session
106        self.total_input_tokens: int = 0
107        self.total_output_tokens: int = 0
108        self.total_cost_usd: float = 0.0
109        self._last_period_cost_usd: float = 0.0
110
111    def _current_task_description(self) -> str:
112        return self._task[:60] if self._task else "waiting for task"
113
114    # ── Lifecycle ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
115
116    async def on_start(self) -> None:
117        await self._log(f"Planner ready. Task: {self._task[:80]}")
118
119        # Enforce documented precedence: approved_plan wins over plan_only.
120        if self._approved_plan and self._plan_only:
121            await self._log(
122                "Both approved_plan and plan_only set — approved_plan takes "
123                "precedence; ignoring plan_only."
124            )
125            self._plan_only = False
126
127        # Hard lifetime cap so planners never pile up until a restart.
128        self._lifetime_task = asyncio.create_task(self._lifetime_watchdog())
129
130        if self._task:
131            asyncio.create_task(self._report_plan(self._task))
132
133    async def on_stop(self) -> None:
134        """Persist final cost metrics so lifetime spend survives agent termination."""
135        if self.total_cost_usd > 0:
136            self.persist(
137                "_final_cost",
138                {
139                    "input_tokens": self.total_input_tokens,
140                    "output_tokens": self.total_output_tokens,
141                    "cost_usd": round(self.total_cost_usd, 6),
142                    "name": self.name,
143                    "stopped_at": time.time(),
144                },
145            )
146        try:
147            await self._mqtt_publish(
148                f"agents/{self.actor_id}/metrics",
149                self._build_metrics(),
150            )
151        except Exception as exc:
152            logger.debug("[%s] Final metrics publish failed: %s", self.name, exc)
153
154    def _build_metrics(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
155        m = super()._build_metrics()
156        m["input_tokens"] = self.total_input_tokens
157        m["output_tokens"] = self.total_output_tokens
158        m["cost_usd"] = round(self.total_cost_usd, 6)
159        return m
160
161    def _accrue_usage(self, usage: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
162        """Accumulate token/cost usage returned by any llm.complete() call."""
163        self.total_input_tokens += usage.get("input_tokens", 0)
164        self.total_output_tokens += usage.get("output_tokens", 0)
165        self.total_cost_usd += usage.get("cost_usd", 0.0)
166        delta = self.total_cost_usd - self._last_period_cost_usd
167        if delta > 0:
168            accumulate_global_cost(delta)
169            self._last_period_cost_usd = self.total_cost_usd
170
171    def _now_context(self) -> str:
172        """Live date/time block for planning prompts. Resolves the user's timezone
173        from main's facts (same source the scheduler uses) so a "tomorrow at 3pm"
174        request is decomposed against the correct calendar date and zone.
175        """
176        user_tz = None
177        if self._registry:
178            main = find_main_actor(self._registry)
179            if main:
180                try:
181                    user_tz = main.get_user_facts().get("pref_timezone")
182                except Exception as exc:
183                    logger.debug("[%s] No user timezone available: %s", self.name, exc)
184        from ..llm_agent import current_time_context
185
186        return current_time_context(user_tz)
187
188    # ── Message handling ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
189
190    async def handle_message(self, msg: Message) -> None:
191        if msg.type == MessageType.TASK:
192            payload = msg.payload if isinstance(msg.payload, dict) else {"text": str(msg.payload)}
193            task_text = payload.get("text") or payload.get("task") or str(msg.payload)
194            self._reply_to_id = (
195                payload.get("_reply_to") or msg.reply_to or msg.sender_id or self._reply_to_id
196            )
197            task_id = payload.get("_task_id")
198            await self._log(f"Received task: {task_text[:80]}")
199            result = await self._run_plan(task_text)
200            if self._reply_to_id:
201                # Use the initiating task_id (from main) so the future resolves,
202                # falling back to the message-level task_id if present
203                resolve_id = self._reply_task_id or task_id
204                reply: dict[str, Any] = {"result": result, "text": result}
205                if resolve_id:
206                    reply["_task_id"] = resolve_id
207                if self._spawned_by_planner:
208                    reply["spawned"] = self._spawned_by_planner
209                await self.send(self._reply_to_id, MessageType.RESULT, reply)
210
211    # ── Report wrapper (on_start path) ────────────────────────────────────
212
213    async def _report_plan(self, task: str) -> None:
214        """Run the plan and report the result back to main (used when task set at spawn time)."""
215        result = await self._run_plan(task)
216        if self._reply_to_id:
217            reply = {
218                "result": result,
219                "text": result,
220                "spawn_results": self._spawn_results,  # per-agent outcome dict
221            }
222            if self._reply_task_id:
223                reply["_task_id"] = self._reply_task_id
224            if self._spawned_by_planner:
225                reply["spawned"] = self._spawned_by_planner
226            await self.send(self._reply_to_id, MessageType.RESULT, reply)
227
228    # ── Pipeline registry ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
229    # Each pipeline rule is stored here so users can list / delete them later.
230    # Stored in persistent state under key "_pipeline_rules".
231    #
232    # Schema per rule:
233    # {
234    #   "rule_id":    str,       # unique slug
235    #   "task":       str,       # original user request
236    #   "agents":     [str],     # names of spawned agents for this rule
237    #   "created_at": float,
238    # }
239
240    # ── Pipeline detection & dispatch ──────────────────────────────────────
241
242    async def _prune_stale_contracts(self) -> None:
243        """Drop TopicBus contracts for agents that are no longer running.
244
245        Planning reads the registry to decide what to reuse, so a contract
246        left behind by a dead agent would offer a topic nobody publishes.
247        """
248        try:
249            from ...core.topic_bus import get_topic_bus
250
251            bus = get_topic_bus()
252            if bus and self._registry:
253                live = {a.name for a in self._registry.all_actors()}
254                # Add remotely-running agents from main's known_nodes
255                main = find_main_actor(self._registry)
256                if main:
257                    for nd in main._known_nodes.values():
258                        if time.time() - nd.get("last_seen", 0) < 30:
259                            live.update(nd.get("agents", []))
260                pruned = bus.registry.prune_stale(live)
261                if pruned:
262                    await self._log(f"Pruned {len(pruned)} stale TopicBus contract(s): {pruned}")
263        except Exception as exc:
264            logger.debug("[%s] Contract prune skipped: %s", self.name, exc)
265
266    async def _run_plan(self, task: str) -> str:
267        workers = self._discover_workers()
268        await self._log(f"Workers available: {[w['name'] for w in workers]}")
269
270        # ── Prune stale TopicBus contracts ────────────────────────────────
271        # Remove contracts for agents that are no longer running so the
272        # planner doesn't wire against dead topics.
273        # IMPORTANT: include remote agents from live node heartbeats — they
274        # are not in the local registry but their contracts are valid and
275        # must NOT be pruned.
276        await self._prune_stale_contracts()
277
278        # ── Approved-plan execution: skip planning entirely ────────────────
279        # Set when main is calling us back to execute a previously-approved
280        # proposal. Route directly to the pipeline executor since approved
281        # plans are by definition pipeline plans (they were generated in
282        # plan_only mode through _run_pipeline).
283        if self._approved_plan:
284            return await self._run_pipeline(task, workers)
285
286        # Detect pipeline vs one-shot
287        is_pipeline = is_pipeline_request(task)
288        if is_pipeline:
289            await self._log("Pipeline request detected — spawning persistent agents...")
290            return await self._run_pipeline(task, workers)
291
292        # ── Dry-run guard for one-shot path ────────────────────────────────
293        # The one-shot path can still produce persistent agents via
294        # _ensure_agents (it spawns missing ones declared by _decompose).
295        # If main asked for plan_only, we MUST honor it here too — otherwise
296        # any task that doesn't trip the pipeline heuristic silently spawns,
297        # bypassing approval. Force the pipeline path so we get the same
298        # approval flow regardless of which heuristic branch was taken.
299        if self._plan_only:
300            await self._log(
301                "plan_only=True on one-shot path — routing through pipeline planner for approval flow"
302            )
303            return await self._run_pipeline(task, workers)
304
305        # ── 1. Check cache ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
306        cache_key = task_hash(task)
307        cached = self._load_cached_plan(cache_key, workers)
308        if cached:
309            await self._log(f"Cache hit — reusing plan ({len(cached)} steps)")
310            plan = cached
311        else:
312            await self._log("No cache hit — generating plan with LLM...")
313            plan = await self._decompose(task, workers)
314            if not plan:
315                await self._log("Decomposition failed — answering directly")
316                return await self._llm_answer(task)
317
318        # ── 2. Spawn any missing agents declared in the plan ───────────────
319        plan = await self._ensure_agents(plan)
320
321        # ── 3. Execute ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
322        await self._log(f"Executing {len(plan)} step(s)...")
323        results = await self._execute(plan)
324
325        # ── 4. Synthesize ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
326        answer = await self._synthesize(task, plan, results)
327
328        # ── 5. Cache successful plan ───────────────────────────────────────
329        if not cached:
330            self._save_plan_cache(cache_key, task, plan)
331            await self._log("Plan cached for future reuse.")
332
333        await self._log("Task complete.")
334        if self._auto_terminate:
335            asyncio.create_task(self._deferred_stop())
336
337        return answer
338
339    # ── Pipeline code validator ────────────────────────────────────────────
340
341    def _validate_pipeline_code(self, plan: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
342        return validate_pipeline_code(plan, self.name)
343
344    # ── Plan cache ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
345
346    def _load_cached_plan(self, cache_key: str, workers: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[Any] | None:
347        alive = {w["name"] for w in workers} | {"main", self.name}
348        return select_cached_plan(self.recall(PLAN_CACHE_KEY) or {}, cache_key, alive, self.name)
349
350    def _save_plan_cache(self, cache_key: str, task: str, plan: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
351        raw = self.recall(PLAN_CACHE_KEY) or {}
352        self.persist(PLAN_CACHE_KEY, with_plan_cached(raw, cache_key, task, plan))
353
354    # ── Worker discovery ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
355
356    def _local_workers(self, manifest_map: dict[str, Any], seen: set[str]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
357        """Workers running in this process, described for the planning prompt."""
358        workers: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
359        if not self._registry:
360            return workers
361        for actor in self._registry.all_actors():
362            if actor.name in SKIP_AGENTS or actor.name == self.name:
363                continue
364            if actor.name.startswith("planner-"):
365                continue
366            seen.add(actor.name)
367            manifest = manifest_map.get(actor.name, {})
368            workers.append(
369                {
370                    "name": actor.name,
371                    "type": type(actor).__name__,
372                    "node": None,
373                    "remote": False,
374                    "description": (
375                        manifest.get("description")
376                        or getattr(actor, "description", "")
377                        or getattr(actor, "system_prompt", "")[:100]
378                        or type(actor).__name__
379                    ),
380                    "capabilities": manifest.get("capabilities", []),
381                    "input_schema": manifest.get("input_schema", {}),
382                    "output_schema": manifest.get("output_schema", {}),
383                    "publishes": manifest.get("publishes", []),
384                    "observed_samples": manifest.get("observed_samples", {}),
385                }
386            )
387        return workers
388
389    def _remote_workers(
390        self, main: Any, manifest_map: dict[str, Any], seen: set[str]
391    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
392        """Workers on other nodes, taken from the heartbeats main has seen."""
393        workers: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
394        if main:
395            for node_name, nd in main._known_nodes.items():
396                if time.time() - nd.get("last_seen", 0) > 30:
397                    continue  # node offline — skip
398                for aname in nd.get("agents", []):
399                    if aname in seen or aname in SKIP_AGENTS:
400                        continue
401                    seen.add(aname)
402                    manifest = manifest_map.get(aname, {})
403                    workers.append(
404                        {
405                            "name": aname,
406                            "type": "RemoteAgent",
407                            "node": node_name,
408                            "remote": True,
409                            "description": manifest.get(
410                                "description", f"Remote agent on {node_name}"
411                            ),
412                            "capabilities": manifest.get("capabilities", []),
413                            "input_schema": manifest.get("input_schema", {}),
414                            "output_schema": manifest.get("output_schema", {}),
415                            "publishes": manifest.get("publishes", []),
416                            "observed_samples": manifest.get("observed_samples", {}),
417                        }
418                    )
419        return workers
420
421    def _discover_workers(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
422        if not self._registry:
423            return []
424        # Pull full manifests from main's capability registry (includes schemas)
425        main = find_main_actor(self._registry)
426        manifest_map: dict[str, Any] = {}
427        if main:
428            for cap in main.list_capabilities():
429                manifest_map[cap["name"]] = cap
430
431        workers = []
432        seen = set()
433
434        # ── Local actors ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
435        workers += self._local_workers(manifest_map, seen)
436
437        # ── Remote agents from live node heartbeats ───────────────────────────
438        workers += self._remote_workers(main, manifest_map, seen)
439
440        return workers
441
442    # ── Decomposition ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
443
444    async def _topic_schema_context(self) -> str:
445        """Live topic samples, so generated code uses real field names."""
446        topic_schema_ctx = ""
447        try:
448            from ...core.topic_bus import get_topic_bus
449
450            bus = get_topic_bus()
451            if bus:
452                sample_lines = []
453                for contract in bus.registry.all_contracts():
454                    samples = contract.observed_samples or {}
455                    for topic, info in samples.items():
456                        example = info.get("example", {})
457                        fields = info.get("fields", {})
458                        sample_lines.append(
459                            f"  {topic} (by {contract.name}): fields={fields}  example={example}"
460                        )
461                if not sample_lines:
462                    sample_lines = await self._sample_live_topics(bus)
463                if sample_lines:
464                    topic_schema_ctx = (
465                        "\n\nLIVE TOPIC SCHEMAS (use EXACTLY these field names in generated code):\n"
466                        + "\n".join(sample_lines)
467                        + "\nCRITICAL: Use the exact field names from the samples above. "
468                        "If a sample shows 'temp', use payload['temp'] — NOT payload['temperature'].\n"
469                    )
470        except Exception as exc:
471            logger.debug("[%s] No live topic samples available: %s", self.name, exc)
472        return topic_schema_ctx
473
474    async def _decompose(self, task: str, workers: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
475        """LLM breaks task into steps. Can declare missing agents with spawn configs."""
476        if not self.llm:
477            return []
478
479        workers_desc = "\n".join(_fmt_worker(w) for w in workers)
480
481        # ── Gather live topic samples for schema context ──────────────────
482        topic_schema_ctx = await self._topic_schema_context()
483
484        prompt = DECOMPOSE_PROMPT.format(
485            workers_desc=workers_desc,
486            topic_schema_ctx=topic_schema_ctx,
487            task=task,
488        )
489
490        try:
491            response, _usage = await self.llm.complete(
492                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
493                system=self._now_context()
494                + "\nYou are a JSON-only task planner. Output only valid JSON arrays, nothing else.",
495                max_tokens=1500,
496            )
497            self._accrue_usage(_usage)
498            plan = json.loads(extract_json_array(response))
499            if isinstance(plan, list) and plan:
500                return plan
501        except Exception:
502            logger.exception("[%s] Decomposition failed", self.name)
503        return []
504
505    # ── Direct answer (fallback when a plan is not the right shape) ────────
506
507    async def _llm_answer(self, task: str) -> str:
508        if not self.llm:
509            return f"[No LLM available: {task}]"
510        try:
511            response, _usage = await self.llm.complete(
512                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": task}],
513                system="You are a helpful assistant.",
514                max_tokens=2048,
515            )
516            self._accrue_usage(_usage)
517        except Exception as e:
518            return f"[LLM error: {e}]"
519        else:
520            return response
521
522    # ── Helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
523
524    async def _lifetime_watchdog(self) -> None:
525        """Hard lifetime cap.
526
527        A planner must never outlive its task. Whether it finishes normally,
528        gets stuck waiting on an approval round-trip that never returns, or sets
529        up a persistent pipeline, it self-removes after _max_lifetime_s so
530        planners don't accumulate until an app restart.
531
532        Spawned pipeline agents are independent actors (registered in main's
533        spawn registry), so terminating the planner does NOT stop them.
534        """
535        try:
536            await asyncio.sleep(self._max_lifetime_s)
537        except asyncio.CancelledError:
538            return
539        if not self._terminated:
540            mins = self._max_lifetime_s / 60
541            await self._log(f"Max lifetime ({mins:.0f} min) reached — self-terminating.")
542            await self._terminate()
543
544    async def _release_from_registry(self) -> None:
545        """Let go of everything holding this planner alive, Supervisor first.
546
547        spawn() registers every child with the Supervisor, which keeps a strong
548        reference and a name in its order. Unregistering alone would drop the
549        planner from the message registry while the Supervisor still held the
550        object, so _specs would grow by one planner per request until the app
551        restarted. release() drops the reference and retires the spec, which
552        also rules out a restart race. Mirrors the delete path main uses.
553        """
554        if self._registry:
555            sup = getattr(self._registry, "_supervisor_ref", None)
556            if sup is not None:
557                try:
558                    sup.release(self.name)
559                except Exception as exc:
560                    logger.debug("[%s] Supervisor release failed: %s", self.name, exc)
561
562        if self._registry:
563            try:
564                await self._registry.unregister(self.actor_id)
565            except Exception as exc:
566                logger.debug("[%s] Unregister failed: %s", self.name, exc)
567
568    async def _terminate(self) -> None:
569        """Idempotent teardown: cancel watchdog + pending futures, unregister, stop."""
570        if self._terminated:
571            return
572        self._terminated = True
573
574        # Cancel the watchdog unless we are being invoked *from* it.
575        if (
576            self._lifetime_task
577            and not self._lifetime_task.done()
578            and self._lifetime_task is not asyncio.current_task()
579        ):
580            self._lifetime_task.cancel()
581
582        # Fail any in-flight delegations so nothing awaits a dead planner.
583        for fut in list(self._result_futures.values()):
584            if not fut.done():
585                fut.cancel()
586        self._result_futures.clear()
587
588        await self._log("Self-terminating.")
589
590        # ── Release from the Supervisor FIRST ──────────────────────────────
591        # spawn() auto-registers every child under the Supervisor, which pins a
592        # strong reference (spec.actor) and keeps the name in _order. Without
593        # releasing, unregister()+stop() only removes us from the message
594        # registry — the Supervisor still holds the object, so it is never
595        # garbage-collected and _specs grows one entry per planner until the app
596        # restarts. release() drops the actor reference and marks the spec
597        # retired (which also prevents any restart race). This mirrors main's
598        # own delete path: release() → unregister() → stop().
599        await self._release_from_registry()
600        try:
601            await self.stop()
602        except Exception as exc:
603            logger.debug("[%s] Stop failed: %s", self.name, exc)
604
605    async def _deferred_stop(self, delay: float = 2.0) -> None:
606        await asyncio.sleep(delay)
607        await self._terminate()
608
609    async def _log(self, msg: str) -> None:
610        logger.info("[%s] %s", self.name, msg)
611        await self._mqtt_publish(
612            f"agents/{self.actor_id}/logs",
613            {"type": "log", "message": msg, "timestamp": time.time()},
614        )

 68        auto_terminate: bool = True,

 81        # Dry-run support:
 82        #   plan_only=True       → produce a plan, return it as JSON, do NOT spawn.
 83        #   approved_plan=<dict> → skip planning, execute the supplied plan directly.
 84        # These are mutually exclusive in practice. If both are somehow set,
 85        # approved_plan takes precedence (it is checked first in _run_plan) and
 86        # the plan is executed; plan_only is ignored. on_start() enforces this
 87        # and logs it so the behaviour is never silent.

 91        self._spawned_by_planner: list[str] = []  # agents we created this run
 92        # Per-agent spawn outcome: name → {"ok": bool, "error": str|None}
 93        # Sent back to main in the RESULT payload so it knows what actually happened.
 94        self._spawn_results: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
 95
 96        # Lifecycle: a planner must never outlive its task. _max_lifetime_s is a
 97        # hard cap after which the planner self-removes regardless of state, so
 98        # proposal/pipeline/approved planners don't accumulate until an app
 99        # restart. _terminated guards against double-teardown; _lifetime_task
100        # holds the watchdog so normal completion can cancel it.
101        self._max_lifetime_s: float = max_lifetime_s
102        self._terminated: bool = False
103        self._lifetime_task: asyncio.Task | None = None
104
105        # Cost tracking — accumulated across all llm.complete() calls this session
106        self.total_input_tokens: int = 0
107        self.total_output_tokens: int = 0
108        self.total_cost_usd: float = 0.0
109        self._last_period_cost_usd: float = 0.0

190    async def handle_message(self, msg: Message) -> None:
191        if msg.type == MessageType.TASK:
192            payload = msg.payload if isinstance(msg.payload, dict) else {"text": str(msg.payload)}
193            task_text = payload.get("text") or payload.get("task") or str(msg.payload)
194            self._reply_to_id = (
195                payload.get("_reply_to") or msg.reply_to or msg.sender_id or self._reply_to_id
196            )
197            task_id = payload.get("_task_id")
198            await self._log(f"Received task: {task_text[:80]}")
199            result = await self._run_plan(task_text)
200            if self._reply_to_id:
201                # Use the initiating task_id (from main) so the future resolves,
202                # falling back to the message-level task_id if present
203                resolve_id = self._reply_task_id or task_id
204                reply: dict[str, Any] = {"result": result, "text": result}
205                if resolve_id:
206                    reply["_task_id"] = resolve_id
207                if self._spawned_by_planner:
208                    reply["spawned"] = self._spawned_by_planner
209                await self.send(self._reply_to_id, MessageType.RESULT, reply)

248class ScheduledAgent(Actor):
249    """First-class scheduled trigger agent. See module docstring for spec format.
250
251    Spawn-time kwargs:
252        name:        actor name (e.g. "evening-lights-trigger")
253        schedule:    dict — one of the schedule specs documented above
254        timezone:    optional str — overrides system tz; main injects user's
255                     pref_timezone here
256        publish_topic: optional str — defaults to "schedule/<name>/fired"
257        description: optional str — for /rules display
258    """
259
260    def __init__(
261        self,
262        schedule: dict | None = None,
263        timezone: str | None = None,
264        publish_topic: str | None = None,
265        description: str = "",
266        **kwargs,
267    ):
268        kwargs.setdefault("name", "scheduled")
269        super().__init__(**kwargs)
270        if not isinstance(schedule, dict):
271            raise ValueError(
272                f"ScheduledAgent requires a 'schedule' dict, got {type(schedule).__name__}"
273            )
274        self._schedule: dict = dict(schedule)  # defensive copy
275        self._user_tz: str | None = timezone
276        self._tz = _resolve_timezone(self._schedule.get("tz"), timezone)
277        self._publish_topic: str = publish_topic or f"schedule/{self.name}/fired"
278        self.description: str = (
279            description or f"Scheduled trigger ({self._schedule.get('type', '?')})"
280        )
281
282        # Validate the schedule eagerly so a malformed spec fails at spawn,
283        # not at first fire. Computing the next fire time is the cheapest
284        # full validation we can do.
285        try:
286            now = datetime.now(self._tz)
287            self._compute_next_fire(now, last_fire=None)
288        except Exception as e:
289            raise ValueError(f"Invalid schedule for {self.name}: {e}") from e
290
291        # Background loop handle
292        self._loop_task: asyncio.Task | None = None
293        # Used by handle_message for manual trigger/inspect commands
294        self._manual_trigger_event: asyncio.Event = asyncio.Event()
295
296    # ── Lifecycle ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
297
298    async def on_start(self):
299        # Restore last-fire state if persisted
300        state = self.recall("_schedule_state") or {}
301        if isinstance(state, dict):
302            self._state = _ScheduleState(
303                **{k: v for k, v in state.items() if k in ("last_fire_iso", "fire_count")}
304            )
305        else:
306            self._state = _ScheduleState()
307
308        # Catch-up logic for "once" schedules: fire if the moment was within
309        # the last 5 minutes. Otherwise, we missed it for good — self-delete.
310        if self._schedule.get("type") == "once":
311            try:
312                fire_at = _next_fire_once(self._schedule["at"], self._tz)
313                now = datetime.now(self._tz)
314                if self._state.fire_count > 0:
315                    # Already fired in a previous run — nothing to do
316                    logger.info(f"[{self.name}] One-shot already fired previously, exiting")
317                    asyncio.create_task(self._self_delete())
318                    return
319                if fire_at < now:
320                    delta = (now - fire_at).total_seconds()
321                    if delta <= _ONESHOT_CATCHUP_S:
322                        logger.info(
323                            f"[{self.name}] One-shot fire missed by {delta:.0f}s "
324                            f"(within catchup window) — firing now"
325                        )
326                        await self._fire(now_utc=datetime.now(timezone.utc))
327                    else:
328                        logger.info(
329                            f"[{self.name}] One-shot fire missed by {delta:.0f}s "
330                            f"(beyond {_ONESHOT_CATCHUP_S:.0f}s catchup) — exiting"
331                        )
332                    # Either way, a once-schedule that's past is done
333                    asyncio.create_task(self._self_delete())
334                    return
335            except Exception as e:
336                logger.error(f"[{self.name}] Once-schedule on_start error: {e}")
337
338        await self._log(
339            f"Scheduled agent ready. type={self._schedule.get('type')} "
340            f"tz={self._tz} publishes={self._publish_topic}"
341        )
342        self._loop_task = asyncio.create_task(self._run_loop())
343
344    async def on_stop(self):
345        if self._loop_task and not self._loop_task.done():
346            self._loop_task.cancel()
347            # gather rather than a bare await: the scheduling loop's own
348            # CancelledError comes back as a value, so ignoring it cannot also
349            # swallow a cancellation aimed at whoever called stop(). `except
350            # (CancelledError, Exception)` could not tell the two apart, and
351            # eating the caller's is what left a supervisor's watch loop
352            # believing it had never been cancelled — a shutdown that hangs.
353            (outcome,) = await asyncio.gather(self._loop_task, return_exceptions=True)
354            # Reported, not dropped: gather *retrieves* the exception, so a loop
355            # that died of something real would otherwise vanish at shutdown.
356            # CancelledError is a BaseException, so this is a real crash only.
357            if isinstance(outcome, Exception):
358                logger.error("[%s] scheduling loop ended in error: %s", self.name, outcome)
359
360    # ── Scheduling loop ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
361
362    async def _run_loop(self):
363        """Sleep until the next fire time, fire, recompute, repeat.
364
365        Wake bounded to _MAX_SLEEP_S so DST transitions / clock jumps /
366        laptop sleep don't leave us stranded. On wake we always recompute
367        from current time, never trust an accumulated deadline.
368        """
369        while self.state.value not in ("stopped", "failed"):
370            try:
371                now_local = datetime.now(self._tz)
372                last_fire = self._last_fire_local(now_local.tzinfo)
373                next_fire = self._compute_next_fire(now_local, last_fire)
374                wait_s = (next_fire - now_local).total_seconds()
375                if wait_s <= 0:
376                    # Edge case: clock jumped forward past the fire. Fire now.
377                    wait_s = 0
378                # Bound the sleep so we re-evaluate periodically
379                sleep_for = min(wait_s, _MAX_SLEEP_S)
380                logger.debug(
381                    f"[{self.name}] next fire at {next_fire.isoformat()} "
382                    f"(sleeping {sleep_for:.1f}s of {wait_s:.1f}s remaining)"
383                )
384
385                # Wait either for the deadline OR a manual-trigger signal,
386                # whichever comes first. Manual trigger fires now without
387                # advancing the schedule.
388                self._manual_trigger_event.clear()
389                try:
390                    await asyncio.wait_for(
391                        self._manual_trigger_event.wait(),
392                        timeout=sleep_for if sleep_for > 0 else 0.001,
393                    )
394                    manual = True
395                except asyncio.TimeoutError:
396                    manual = False
397
398                # If we woke early via the bounded re-check (not at the deadline,
399                # not manual), just loop and recompute.
400                if not manual:
401                    now_local = datetime.now(self._tz)
402                    if now_local < next_fire:
403                        continue  # not time yet, recompute and sleep again
404
405                # Time to fire (or manually triggered)
406                await self._fire(
407                    now_utc=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
408                    manual=manual,
409                )
410
411                # If this was a "once" schedule, we're done
412                if self._schedule.get("type") == "once":
413                    logger.info(f"[{self.name}] One-shot fired — self-deleting")
414                    asyncio.create_task(self._self_delete())
415                    return
416
417            except asyncio.CancelledError:
418                break
419            except Exception as e:
420                logger.error(f"[{self.name}] Loop error: {e!r} — backing off 30s")
421                await asyncio.sleep(30)
422
423    def _last_fire_local(self, tzinfo: Any) -> datetime | None:
424        """Convert persisted UTC ISO timestamp to a tz-aware local datetime."""
425        if not self._state.last_fire_iso:
426            return None
427        try:
428            dt = datetime.fromisoformat(self._state.last_fire_iso)
429            if dt.tzinfo is None:
430                dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
431            return dt.astimezone(tzinfo)
432        except Exception:
433            return None
434
435    def _compute_next_fire(self, now_local: datetime, last_fire: datetime | None) -> datetime:
436        """Dispatch to the right next-fire calculator based on schedule type."""
437        spec = self._schedule
438        stype = (spec.get("type") or "").strip().lower()
439
440        if stype == "daily":
441            at = spec.get("at")
442            if not at:
443                raise ValueError("daily schedule requires 'at' (e.g. '17:00')")
444            return _next_fire_daily(now_local, at)
445
446        if stype == "weekly":
447            at = spec.get("at")
448            days = spec.get("days") or []
449            if not at:
450                raise ValueError("weekly schedule requires 'at'")
451            return _next_fire_weekly(now_local, at, days)
452
453        if stype == "interval":
454            secs = spec.get("seconds") or spec.get("every_seconds")
455            if secs is None:
456                # Allow {"every": "30m"} as a convenience
457                every = spec.get("every", "")
458                secs = _parse_duration(every) if every else None
459            if not isinstance(secs, (int, float)):
460                raise ValueError(f"interval schedule requires 'seconds' (int), got {secs!r}")
461            return _next_fire_interval(now_local, int(secs), last_fire)
462
463        if stype == "once":
464            at = spec.get("at")
465            if not at:
466                raise ValueError("once schedule requires 'at' (ISO-8601 datetime)")
467            return _next_fire_once(at, self._tz)
468
469        if stype == "cron":
470            expr = spec.get("expr") or spec.get("expression")
471            if not expr:
472                raise ValueError("cron schedule requires 'expr' (e.g. '0 17 * * *')")
473            return _next_fire_cron(now_local, expr)
474
475        raise ValueError(
476            f"Unknown schedule type: {stype!r}. Use one of: daily, weekly, interval, once, cron."
477        )
478
479    # ── Firing ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
480
481    async def _fire(self, now_utc: datetime, manual: bool = False):
482        """Publish the fire event and update persisted state."""
483        payload = {
484            "fired_at": now_utc.isoformat(),
485            "schedule_type": self._schedule.get("type", "?"),
486            "agent": self.name,
487            "manual": manual,
488        }
489        try:
490            await self._mqtt_publish(self._publish_topic, payload)
491            self._state.last_fire_iso = now_utc.isoformat()
492            self._state.fire_count += 1
493            self.persist(
494                "_schedule_state",
495                {
496                    "last_fire_iso": self._state.last_fire_iso,
497                    "fire_count": self._state.fire_count,
498                },
499            )
500            await self._log(
501                f"Fired{' (manual)' if manual else ''} → {self._publish_topic} "
502                f"[count={self._state.fire_count}]"
503            )
504        except Exception as e:
505            logger.error(f"[{self.name}] Fire failed: {e!r}")
506
507    async def _self_delete(self):
508        """Remove from registry and stop. Used for completed once-schedules."""
509        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
510        if self._registry:
511            try:
512                await self._registry.unregister(self.actor_id)
513            except Exception:
514                pass
515        # Best-effort: ask main to drop us from the spawn registry too
516        if self._registry:
517            main = find_main_actor(self._registry)
518            if main:
519                try:
520                    main._remove_from_spawn_registry(self.name)
521                except Exception:
522                    pass
523        await self.stop()
524
525    # ── Message handling ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
526
527    async def handle_message(self, msg: Message):
528        """Supports two task types for inspection / testing:
529
530        {"action": "trigger"} — fire NOW without advancing the schedule
531        {"action": "info"}    — return current schedule + next fire info
532        """
533        if msg.type != MessageType.TASK:
534            return
535        payload = msg.payload if isinstance(msg.payload, dict) else {}
536        action = (payload.get("action") or payload.get("text") or "").strip().lower()
537        reply_to = msg.reply_to or msg.sender_id
538        task_id = payload.get("_task_id")
539
540        async def _reply(body: dict):
541            if not reply_to:
542                return
543            r = dict(body)
544            if task_id:
545                r["_task_id"] = task_id
546            await self.send(reply_to, MessageType.RESULT, r)
547
548        if action in ("trigger", "fire", "fire now"):
549            self._manual_trigger_event.set()
550            await _reply({"result": f"Manual trigger queued for {self.name}"})
551            return
552
553        if action in ("info", "next", "status"):
554            try:
555                now_local = datetime.now(self._tz)
556                last = self._last_fire_local(now_local.tzinfo)
557                next_fire = self._compute_next_fire(now_local, last)
558                info = {
559                    "name": self.name,
560                    "schedule": self._schedule,
561                    "tz": str(self._tz),
562                    "publish_topic": self._publish_topic,
563                    "next_fire": next_fire.isoformat(),
564                    "last_fire": self._state.last_fire_iso,
565                    "fire_count": self._state.fire_count,
566                }
567                await _reply({"result": info, "info": info})
568            except Exception as e:
569                await _reply({"error": str(e)})
570            return
571
572        await _reply({"error": f"Unknown action: {action!r}"})
573
574    # ── Helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
575
576    async def _log(self, msg: str):
577        logger.info(f"[{self.name}] {msg}")
578        await self._mqtt_publish(
579            f"agents/{self.actor_id}/logs",
580            {"type": "log", "message": msg, "timestamp": time.time()},
581        )

First-class scheduled trigger agent. See module docstring for spec format.

Spawn-time kwargs: name: actor name (e.g. "evening-lights-trigger") schedule: dict — one of the schedule specs documented above timezone: optional str — overrides system tz; main injects user's pref_timezone here publish_topic: optional str — defaults to "schedule//fired" description: optional str — for /rules display

ScheduledAgent( schedule: dict | None = None, timezone: str | None = None, publish_topic: str | None = None, description: str = '', **kwargs) 
260    def __init__(
261        self,
262        schedule: dict | None = None,
263        timezone: str | None = None,
264        publish_topic: str | None = None,
265        description: str = "",
266        **kwargs,
267    ):
268        kwargs.setdefault("name", "scheduled")
269        super().__init__(**kwargs)
270        if not isinstance(schedule, dict):
271            raise ValueError(
272                f"ScheduledAgent requires a 'schedule' dict, got {type(schedule).__name__}"
273            )
274        self._schedule: dict = dict(schedule)  # defensive copy
275        self._user_tz: str | None = timezone
276        self._tz = _resolve_timezone(self._schedule.get("tz"), timezone)
277        self._publish_topic: str = publish_topic or f"schedule/{self.name}/fired"
278        self.description: str = (
279            description or f"Scheduled trigger ({self._schedule.get('type', '?')})"
280        )
281
282        # Validate the schedule eagerly so a malformed spec fails at spawn,
283        # not at first fire. Computing the next fire time is the cheapest
284        # full validation we can do.
285        try:
286            now = datetime.now(self._tz)
287            self._compute_next_fire(now, last_fire=None)
288        except Exception as e:
289            raise ValueError(f"Invalid schedule for {self.name}: {e}") from e
290
291        # Background loop handle
292        self._loop_task: asyncio.Task | None = None
293        # Used by handle_message for manual trigger/inspect commands
294        self._manual_trigger_event: asyncio.Event = asyncio.Event()
description: str
async def on_start(self): 
298    async def on_start(self):
299        # Restore last-fire state if persisted
300        state = self.recall("_schedule_state") or {}
301        if isinstance(state, dict):
302            self._state = _ScheduleState(
303                **{k: v for k, v in state.items() if k in ("last_fire_iso", "fire_count")}
304            )
305        else:
306            self._state = _ScheduleState()
307
308        # Catch-up logic for "once" schedules: fire if the moment was within
309        # the last 5 minutes. Otherwise, we missed it for good — self-delete.
310        if self._schedule.get("type") == "once":
311            try:
312                fire_at = _next_fire_once(self._schedule["at"], self._tz)
313                now = datetime.now(self._tz)
314                if self._state.fire_count > 0:
315                    # Already fired in a previous run — nothing to do
316                    logger.info(f"[{self.name}] One-shot already fired previously, exiting")
317                    asyncio.create_task(self._self_delete())
318                    return
319                if fire_at < now:
320                    delta = (now - fire_at).total_seconds()
321                    if delta <= _ONESHOT_CATCHUP_S:
322                        logger.info(
323                            f"[{self.name}] One-shot fire missed by {delta:.0f}s "
324                            f"(within catchup window) — firing now"
325                        )
326                        await self._fire(now_utc=datetime.now(timezone.utc))
327                    else:
328                        logger.info(
329                            f"[{self.name}] One-shot fire missed by {delta:.0f}s "
330                            f"(beyond {_ONESHOT_CATCHUP_S:.0f}s catchup) — exiting"
331                        )
332                    # Either way, a once-schedule that's past is done
333                    asyncio.create_task(self._self_delete())
334                    return
335            except Exception as e:
336                logger.error(f"[{self.name}] Once-schedule on_start error: {e}")
337
338        await self._log(
339            f"Scheduled agent ready. type={self._schedule.get('type')} "
340            f"tz={self._tz} publishes={self._publish_topic}"
341        )
342        self._loop_task = asyncio.create_task(self._run_loop())

Called when actor starts. Override for init logic.

async def on_stop(self): 
344    async def on_stop(self):
345        if self._loop_task and not self._loop_task.done():
346            self._loop_task.cancel()
347            # gather rather than a bare await: the scheduling loop's own
348            # CancelledError comes back as a value, so ignoring it cannot also
349            # swallow a cancellation aimed at whoever called stop(). `except
350            # (CancelledError, Exception)` could not tell the two apart, and
351            # eating the caller's is what left a supervisor's watch loop
352            # believing it had never been cancelled — a shutdown that hangs.
353            (outcome,) = await asyncio.gather(self._loop_task, return_exceptions=True)
354            # Reported, not dropped: gather *retrieves* the exception, so a loop
355            # that died of something real would otherwise vanish at shutdown.
356            # CancelledError is a BaseException, so this is a real crash only.
357            if isinstance(outcome, Exception):
358                logger.error("[%s] scheduling loop ended in error: %s", self.name, outcome)

Called when actor stops. Override for cleanup.

async def handle_message(self, msg: Message): 
527    async def handle_message(self, msg: Message):
528        """Supports two task types for inspection / testing:
529
530        {"action": "trigger"} — fire NOW without advancing the schedule
531        {"action": "info"}    — return current schedule + next fire info
532        """
533        if msg.type != MessageType.TASK:
534            return
535        payload = msg.payload if isinstance(msg.payload, dict) else {}
536        action = (payload.get("action") or payload.get("text") or "").strip().lower()
537        reply_to = msg.reply_to or msg.sender_id
538        task_id = payload.get("_task_id")
539
540        async def _reply(body: dict):
541            if not reply_to:
542                return
543            r = dict(body)
544            if task_id:
545                r["_task_id"] = task_id
546            await self.send(reply_to, MessageType.RESULT, r)
547
548        if action in ("trigger", "fire", "fire now"):
549            self._manual_trigger_event.set()
550            await _reply({"result": f"Manual trigger queued for {self.name}"})
551            return
552
553        if action in ("info", "next", "status"):
554            try:
555                now_local = datetime.now(self._tz)
556                last = self._last_fire_local(now_local.tzinfo)
557                next_fire = self._compute_next_fire(now_local, last)
558                info = {
559                    "name": self.name,
560                    "schedule": self._schedule,
561                    "tz": str(self._tz),
562                    "publish_topic": self._publish_topic,
563                    "next_fire": next_fire.isoformat(),
564                    "last_fire": self._state.last_fire_iso,
565                    "fire_count": self._state.fire_count,
566                }
567                await _reply({"result": info, "info": info})
568            except Exception as e:
569                await _reply({"error": str(e)})
570            return
571
572        await _reply({"error": f"Unknown action: {action!r}"})
